## Revision 5

Revision 4 reached CONSENSUS in round 9. Implementing it, the end-to-end
script (`design/research/11-tests-e2e.md`) found two failures in the
`references/` mechanism of P1:

1. Claude Code denied both reads in `-p` mode, because the files sit outside
   the working directory. The model answered anyway, with no upstream rules
   loaded. An interactive session would ask for permission on each read.
2. Codex read the files in 1 of 8 runs with a short prompt, and in 4 of 4
   with the plugin's own default prompt. Whether the rules load depended on
   the prompt.

Revision 5 changes only how the skill gets the texts. It embeds them with a
`{{upstream <name>}}` template directive, so the skill body is the hook
bundle byte for byte. Everything else in revision 4 stands: no plugin
dependencies, byte-for-byte mirrors, the frozen hook handlers, the launcher's
resume rule, the generated `plugins/`, the doctor, and CI.

It also records two findings from the same run:

- With both mirrors installed, Codex 0.154.0 loaded `au-unslop:unslop` for
  an unrelated question in 2 of 4 runs, and 0.157.1 in 0 of 4. That is
  upstream's frontmatter, kept on purpose by P2. A user with always-on and
  this mirror gets a second unslop that `stop unslop` does not control. The
  README says so, and the check for an unprompted skill load now runs
  before the mirrors are installed.
- A mirror kept by name in Claude Code stays at its old version after the
  upgrade until `claude plugin update` runs on it. P10 now says so.

The second end-to-end run on revision 5 passed every check: Claude Code 17
of 17, Codex 0.154.0 19 of 19, Codex 0.157.1 19 of 19, and `migrate` 16 of
16 in each runtime. Both runtimes received the whole skill body byte for
byte, so Codex does not cut a skill of about 22 KB.

It also measured one platform limit (`11`, last section). With always-on
off, Claude Code 2.1.283 re-attaches an invoked skill after `/compact` cut
to 20,000 characters, which drops unslop rules 32 and 33, the END line, and
the final check. After `--resume` and then `/compact`, it re-attaches
nothing. The always-on hook is not affected, because it injects the whole
bundle again on `compact`.

Revision 5 documents this instead of reshaping the skill:

- Shrinking the body under 20,000 characters would fix only the first case,
  and would mean cutting overlay text that five review rounds settled, with
  upstream growth pushing it over again later.
- Moving the final check ahead of the upstream texts would lose other rules
  instead, and would break the identity between the skill body and the hook
  bundle, because chunk 1 has no room for it under the 10,000-character cap.
- The README tells users who work in long, compacting sessions to turn on
  always-on, or to invoke the skill again after a compaction. A unit test
  reports the skill's size against the 20,000-character re-attach budget, so
  the gap stays visible.

## Round 10 responses

| Round 10 item | Response |
| --- | --- |
| Blocking 1, P9 still names reference files | P9 now asserts that each cache copy matches every shipped file byte for byte, including the skill with both embedded upstream blocks |
| Blocking 2, "changes nothing" conflicts with the lifecycle | P1 now says the duplicate adds no rules, but invoking re-enables both modes, while a hook reload keeps the known states |
# Decisions

Each entry records what was decided, why, the evidence, and when to revisit
it. Evidence names the CLI versions tested, because plugin behavior changes
between releases. Re-test before relying on an entry after an upgrade.

Tested versions unless an entry says otherwise: Claude Code 2.1.283,
Codex CLI 0.154.0 and 0.157.1, and the `openai/codex` main branch source as
of 2026-09-26.

Entry numbers are stable ids. A retired entry keeps its number and says
what replaced it.

History:

- `PLAN.md` holds the v0.1.0 design and its five Codex review rounds
  (`round-1` to `round-5`).
- `RESTRUCTURE.md` holds the 0.2.0 split into several plugins.
- `STRUCTURE-v2.md` holds the 0.3.0 restructure, accepted after Codex
  review rounds 6 to 9. Its research and test runs are in `research/`,
  indexed by `research/00-synthesis.md`.
- This file supersedes all three where they disagree.

## Behavior

### D1. Tie-breaker by surface

On a conflict, i-have-adhd wins in a direct reply to the user and unslop
wins in all other writing. Rules that do not conflict apply everywhere.

- Why: the user fixed this requirement on 2026-09-12. Replies need the ADHD
  shape. Files, commits, and PR text need unslop's prose rules.
- Where: `src/adhd-unslop/overlay/10-precedence.md`, with the outcome
  table for each known interaction.

### D2. Upstream text stays verbatim

The overlay adds scope, precedence, lifecycle, and a final check. It never
rewrites either upstream skill. The vendored mirrors ship the upstream
`SKILL.md` byte for byte, and `adhd-unslop` ships the upstream bodies with
only the frontmatter removed.

- Why: upstream updates stay mechanical. An earlier hand-merged attempt,
  `unslop-final`, rewrote ADHD's examples and lost the reply shape.
- Enforced by: `tests/build.test.mjs`, which compares the files byte for
  byte.

### D3. Citations by number are the contract with upstream

The overlay cites upstream items as "ADHD rule N", "ADHD exception N",
"ADHD check N", "unslop rule N", and "unslop process N". `sync.mjs`
refuses an upstream change that removes a cited item.

- Why: a removed item makes the overlay point at nothing, and nobody
  notices.
- Evidence: on 2026-09-26 upstream unslop removed process step 3, the
  self-audit. The final check cited "process 1 to 3". The original gate
  checked only rules and let the change through. The gate now covers all
  five labels, and the final check cites "unslop process 1 and 2".
- Where: `CITATION_KINDS` in `tools/sync.mjs`.

## Packaging

### D4. One marketplace; adhd-unslop is self-contained

The repo is a Claude Code and Codex marketplace with three plugins.
`adhd-unslop` ships everything it needs: a skill that embeds the overlay
and both upstream texts, the always-on hook, and a doctor skill. `au-i-have-adhd` and `au-unslop` are optional standalone mirrors.

- Why: in 0.2.x `adhd-unslop` depended on the two mirrors. That failed in
  practice (D16), Codex has no dependencies (D15), and no repo out of 25
  that ship for both runtimes uses plugin `dependencies`. Repos that share
  text between plugins copy it at build time and check the copies
  (`research/03`). The user's requirements still hold: the text comes only
  from our own pinned copies, and i-have-adhd stays available as its own
  plugin.
- Cost: the skill carries its own copy of each upstream text, generated
  from the same `upstream/` files as the mirrors and the hook chunks, and
  checked by `build.mjs --check`.
- A new plugin reuses an upstream by embedding it with a `{{upstream
  <name>}}` template line and listing it in `upstreams` in
  `tools/plugins.json` (D11).
- History: 0.2.0 chose dependencies over an earlier proposal to copy the
  texts. 0.3.0 reverses that, per `STRUCTURE-v2.md` P1.

### D5. Vendor into our marketplace, never depend on a third party

The upstream text lives in `upstream/`, pinned by commit and sha256 in
`tools/upstream.json`, and ships in our own plugins.

- Why: a third-party marketplace needs its own install step, and we cannot
  validate what it ships.
- We are the only repo of the seven that vendor third-party skills that
  pins each file by commit and hash (`research/04`).
- Rejected: `git-subdir` sources pointing at the upstream repos. The
  i-have-adhd repo root is a whole plugin with its own always-on hook, and
  `plugins/pstack` holds more than 40 skills. We would ship their hooks and
  skills, and lose the pin and citation checks.

### D6. Vendored plugins carry the `au-` prefix

Plugin names are `au-i-have-adhd` and `au-unslop`. Skill names stay
`i-have-adhd` and `unslop`.

- Why: a skill's name is `plugin:skill`, with no marketplace in it. A user
  with the upstream i-have-adhd plugin installed would have two skills
  named `i-have-adhd:i-have-adhd`.
- Evidence: Claude Code uses whichever same-name plugin was installed
  first, tested in both orders, 3 of 3 runs each, typed invocation
  included. In Codex a typed `$dep:dep` found both copies and reported the
  clash. Two different plugin names with the same skill name, such as
  `a:shared` and `b:shared`, both list and both run by full name
  (`research/08` L6).
- The user chose `au-` "for now".

### D7. Vendored mirrors keep the upstream frontmatter

The mirrors ship the upstream `SKILL.md` unchanged. The build generates
`agents/openai.yaml` so Codex matches Claude Code: `allow_implicit_invocation:
false` when the upstream sets `disable-model-invocation: true`, `true`
otherwise. Neither upstream skill folder has its own `openai.yaml`.

- Result: i-have-adhd stays user-only and unslop stays model-invocable, as
  upstream ships them. Typed invocation works in both runtimes.
- History: 0.2.x rewrote the frontmatter so `adhd-unslop` could load the
  mirrors through the Skill tool. Nothing loads them now.

### D8. The composed skill runs only when asked

`adhd-unslop` keeps `disable-model-invocation: true` and
`allow_implicit_invocation: false`. It runs on explicit invocation or
through the always-on hook. The doctor skill has the same settings.

### D9. The adhd-unslop skill embeds the upstream texts

The skill's body, after a one-line generated comment, is the always-on
bundle byte for byte: the overlay sections, the i-have-adhd block, the
unslop block, and the final check. It reads no files.

- Why: a first 0.3.0 build had the skill read the texts from `references/`
  files next to it. Claude Code denied both reads in `-p` mode, because the
  files sit outside the working directory, and an interactive session would
  ask for permission each time. Codex skipped the reads in 7 of 8 runs with
  a short prompt (`research/11`). Rules that must always apply cannot
  depend on a permission rule or on the model choosing to read a file.
  `references/` suits optional detail. These texts are the rules.
- Rejected: `allowed-tools: Read` in the frontmatter. It lets Claude Code
  read without asking but pre-approves every Read while the skill is active,
  and does nothing for Codex.
- Embedding contract: a `{{upstream <name>}}` template line becomes the
  BEGIN line, the upstream body with its frontmatter removed and a final
  newline, and the END line. The hook chunks carry the same bytes.
- Size: about 21,800 bytes. Codex does not cut it. Codex cuts at 8,000 bytes
  only for a plugin with a root `plugin.json` that uses the agent-plugins
  `$schema` (`research/07` C1). The end-to-end check confirms the whole
  skill arrives in both runtimes.
- A user who invokes the skill while always-on already delivered the bundle
  gets a second, identical copy of the rules. It adds no rules, but invoking
  re-enables both modes, as the lifecycle rules say, so a mode the user had
  stopped comes back. A hook reload keeps the known mode states.
- Compaction limit: without always-on, Claude Code 2.1.283 re-attaches an
  invoked skill after `/compact` cut to 20,000 characters, which drops the
  last unslop rules and the final check, and after `--resume` then
  `/compact` it re-attaches nothing (`research/11`). The always-on hook
  injects the whole bundle again on `compact`, so the README points long,
  compacting sessions at always-on. Shrinking the skill would fix only the
  first case and would cut settled overlay text. A unit test reports the
  size against the 20,000-character budget.
- History: 0.2.x loaded the mirrors through the Skill tool. 0.1.0 embedded
  the texts, as 0.3.0 does again.

### D10. Every file under plugins/ is generated

Hand-written sources live in `src/<plugin>/` and `upstream/`. Marketplace
entries point at `./plugins/<name>`. `build.mjs --check` fails on a stale or
missing file, and on any file under `plugins/`, `.claude-plugin/`, or
`.agents/plugins/` that the build does not write. Only `build.mjs --prune`
deletes such files.

- Why generated: with `"source": "./"`, Codex copied the whole repo,
  including `.git`, `design/`, and `tests/`, into its plugin cache. Codex
  install copies only the plugin's own directory and skips symlinks, so
  plugins cannot share files through `../` or links.
- Why the stray check: before 0.3.0 a leftover file under `plugins/`
  shipped and passed CI (`research/04`, `research/05`). claude-octopus and
  gstack check for strays too.
- Why no automatic delete: a normal build must not remove files a person
  put there by mistake. The review in round 6 required an explicit flag.

### D11. One config file for plugins

`tools/plugins.json` lists every plugin: name, version, kind (`vendored`
or `authored`), descriptions, keywords, the Codex `interface`, and for an
authored plugin its skills, each skill's embedded `upstreams`, and the
always-on chunk list. `tools/build.mjs` generates both marketplace files, every
manifest, each plugin's `README.md`, `NOTICE.md`, and `LICENSES/`, and all
skill files from it.

- An authored plugin's skill folders in `src/<plugin>/skills/` are copied.
  A `SKILL.md.tmpl` is rendered. Its syntax is two line directives:
  `{{include <path under src/<plugin>/>}}` inserts a file, and
  `{{upstream <name>}}` inserts a pinned upstream block. The build fails
  when a template's upstream directives and its `upstreams` list disagree.
  gstack renders skills from templates the same way.
- Adding a plugin: add its entry, write `src/<name>/skills/<skill>/`, embed
  any upstream with `{{upstream <name>}}`, list it in `upstreams`, build,
  and test. The steps are in `AGENTS.md`.

### D22. Manifests follow the documented minimum

- Both native manifests stay for each plugin. Codex falls back to the
  Claude files and still loads skills and hooks, but loses the `interface`
  text, and `interface` in a Claude manifest fails `claude plugin validate
  --strict` (`research/02`). hashicorp uses the same two-file layout.
- Claude Code marketplace entries carry no `version`. The docs say not to
  set it in both places, and install, listing, and update all use
  `plugin.json` (`research/08` L3).
- The Codex marketplace keeps `policy.products: ["CODEX"]`. Dropping it
  would publish the plugins to ChatGPT and Atlas too.
- The Codex manifest names `"hooks": "./hooks/hooks.json"` when the plugin
  ships hooks, as every repo that ships Codex plugin hooks does. Trust
  survives the explicit path (`research/07` C3).
- Claude Code manifests carry `homepage`, `repository`, and `keywords`.
- No root `plugin.json` with the agent-plugins `$schema`. Codex would read
  it first and cut skills at 8,000 bytes.

## Hooks

### D12. The always-on hook embeds both texts, in three chunks

The hook prints the overlay and both upstream bodies from files inside
`adhd-unslop`, split across three handlers.

- Why embedded: a hook cannot count on another plugin, and the always-on
  path must not depend on the model reading files first.
- Why chunked: Claude Code saves a hook value over 10,000 characters to a
  file and shows the model only a path and the first 2,000 characters
  (`research/08` L5). The cap is documented at
  code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks.md#json-output and cannot be raised. The
  text is about 21,500 characters. Codex allows 2,500 tokens per handler by
  default, counted as ceil(chars / 4), and cuts the middle of anything
  longer (`research/07` C6). Each handler sets `additionalContextLimit:
  5000`, because the built chunks with non-ASCII text were not tested
  against the default.
- Each chunk carries a bundle id, the first 12 hex characters of the text's
  sha256. The header states that a bundle is complete only when all three
  chunks with that id are present, each with its END line. Claude Code
  delivers the chunks in the order the handlers finish, and Codex in the
  declared order (`research/09`).
- The header is worded as statements of fact. The Claude Code docs warn
  that imperative hook text can trigger prompt-injection defenses.
- We are the only repo of 25 that chunks. The others inject under about
  8,000 characters from one handler (`research/01`).

### D13. Only adhd-unslop has an always-on hook

A plugin that reuses i-have-adhd must not add its own always-on hook.

- Why: two hooks would inject the ADHD rules twice, possibly from different
  pins.

### D14. Always-on is opt-in

Either `~/.claude/.adhd-unslop-always` or `~/.codex/.adhd-unslop-always`,
or the same name under `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` or `CODEX_HOME`, turns it on in
both runtimes. `ADHD_UNSLOP_ALWAYS` overrides the flags for one process:

- `0`, `false`, or `off`, in any case: off, even with a flag.
- `1`, `true`, or `on`: on, without a flag.
- Unset or empty: the flag files decide.
- Any other value counts as unset, and the doctor reports it.

Without opt-in the hook prints nothing. A broken install prints one JSON
`systemMessage` and no context. The hook never blocks session start.

- Why the switch: CI and scripted runs need a way off without deleting a
  user's flag file (planning-with-files issue #195, `research/01`).

### D23. The launcher decides what to do on resume

The matcher is `startup|resume|clear|compact`. On `resume` the launcher
prints nothing in Claude Code and injects in Codex. It tells them apart by
`PLUGIN_ROOT`, which Codex sets for plugin hooks and Claude Code never does
(`research/10`). When it cannot tell, it injects. It reads `source` from the
SessionStart payload on stdin with a one-second timeout, and injects when
stdin is missing or unreadable.

- Claude Code keeps the earlier injection in a resumed session, so a
  `resume` match added a second copy of about 24,000 characters on every
  resume (`research/08` L1). `/compact`, `/clear`, and auto-compaction each
  leave exactly one copy (`research/09`).
- Codex duplicates on resume too (`research/07` C4), but it can also lose
  the copy. Codex fires `compact` only when the next turn starts, so a user
  who compacts and quits before sending a message resumes with no copy
  (`research/09`). A duplicate costs tokens. A missing copy silently turns
  always-on off. Codex keeps injecting on resume.
- A forked Claude Code session sends `source: "fork"` and carries the
  parent's copy, so `fork` needs no match.
- The hook definitions did not change, so Codex trust recorded for 0.2.2
  stays valid (D24).
- Claude Code edge case: turning always-on on during a session and then
  resuming it gives no copy until the next startup, `/clear`, or
  compaction. The README says to start a new session.

### D24. The chunk handlers are frozen

The three chunk handlers keep the exact fields and positions users trusted
in 0.2.2. `tests/hook.test.mjs` compares them with
`tests/fixtures/trusted-session-start-group.json`.

- Why: Codex keys hook trust by plugin, hooks file path, event, group, and
  handler index, and checks a hash of every handler field. A version bump,
  an explicit `hooks` path, or a manifest move keeps trust. Renaming the
  hooks file or changing any handler field, including adding or removing
  `additionalContextLimit`, loses it (`research/07` C3).
- Behavior changes belong in the launcher script, whose content is not part
  of the hash. Removing the 0.2.x dependency group, which came after the
  chunk group, shifted nothing.
- To change a handler anyway, update the fixture on purpose and tell Codex
  users to review the hooks in `/hooks` once.

### D25. No output style, no per-session mode tracker, no subagent injection

- Output style: a plugin can force one with `force-for-plugin: true`, with
  no size cap and persistence through compaction (`research/08` L8). It
  overrides the user's own `outputStyle` whenever the plugin is enabled,
  which bypasses the opt-in flag. No repo of the 25 ships one, and Codex
  would still need the hook. Revisit if Claude Code adds an opt-in style
  that composes with the user's style.
- Mode tracker: caveman stores mode state per session so compaction cannot
  turn a mode back on. It needs a `UserPromptSubmit` hook on every prompt
  in both runtimes, with its own Codex trust entry, to fix a rare case that
  a repeated stop command also fixes.
- Subagent injection: `SubagentStart` would add the bundle to every
  subagent, with no stated need.

## Dependencies

### D15. Retired in 0.3.0: Claude Code dependencies and the Codex warning

0.2.x declared the mirrors as Claude Code `dependencies` and shipped a
SessionStart hook that warned Codex users about a missing mirror. D4
replaced both. What was learned still holds:

- Codex has no plugin dependencies. The manifest has no field, `openai.yaml`
  `dependencies.tools` acts only on `mcp` entries, and
  `INSTALLED_BY_DEFAULT` installs nothing from a local or git marketplace.
- A hook can run `codex plugin add` to install a missing plugin. The user
  chose not to, because it changes their config without asking.
- `codex exec` does not print a hook's `systemMessage`.

### D16. Updates do not cascade

Each plugin updates on its own. `claude plugin update` of a plugin leaves
its dependencies at their old versions. Updating 0.1.0 to 0.2.0 did not
install newly declared dependencies, and a repeated `claude plugin install`
added one missing dependency per run. In Codex, running `codex plugin add`
again installs the newer version.

Upgrade from 0.2.x to 0.3.0, as the README states:

- Claude Code: `claude plugin marketplace update adhd-unslop`, then
  `claude plugin update adhd-unslop@adhd-unslop`, then optionally `claude
  plugin prune` to remove the mirrors that 0.2.x installed as dependencies.
  A mirror the user installed by name stays.
- Codex: `codex plugin marketplace upgrade adhd-unslop`, then `codex plugin
  add adhd-unslop@adhd-unslop`. Hook trust carries over (D24). Remove a
  mirror with `codex plugin remove` only if it was installed for
  `adhd-unslop` alone.
- `tests/e2e/run.sh migrate` checks both paths from 0.2.2.

## Versions and upstream updates

### D17. Per-plugin versions, raised by the bump, enforced in CI

Each plugin has its own version in `tools/plugins.json`. `sync.mjs` raises
the patch version of every plugin that ships the changed upstream text,
once per run: its mirror, any plugin whose skills embed it, and any plugin
whose always-on chunks carry it. A future `presentation` plugin that embeds
i-have-adhd gets a new version whenever i-have-adhd changes.

- Why: installed copies update only when the version changes. A text
  change without a version bump reports "already at the latest version"
  in Claude Code (`research/08`).
- Enforced by: `tools/version-gate.mjs` in `verify.yml`. On a pull request
  it fails when the pull request changed files under `plugins/<name>/`,
  measured from the merge base, and that plugin's version is not greater
  than on the tip of the base branch. Comparing with the tip also catches a
  version that another merged pull request already used. The pattern comes
  from expo.

### D18. Daily bump PR, issue on failure

`.github/workflows/upstream-bump.yml` runs daily. It checks the pins with
`sync.mjs --verify-remote`, which refetches each pinned file and compares
its hash, then runs `sync.mjs --latest`. It opens or updates one PR on
branch `upstream-bump`, or opens one issue when a pin does not match
upstream or a bump fails its checks. A person reviews each PR for new
conflicts before merging.

- Why a PR: an upstream change can add a conflict the outcome table does
  not cover.
- It uses the default `GITHUB_TOKEN`, with no extra secret. A PR opened
  with that token does not trigger other workflows, so the job starts
  `verify.yml` with `gh workflow run --ref upstream-bump`. That run reports
  as a check on the PR's head commit, verified on PR #2. The PR's own
  `pull_request` run shows `action_required` until someone approves it.
- Needs the repository setting "Allow GitHub Actions to create and approve
  pull requests", turned on 2026-09-26.
- `--latest` asks for the newest commit that touched each pinned file, and
  skips an upstream when that commit changed none of them.

### D19. The marketplace name stays `adhd-unslop` for now

- Why: renaming changes every install id, such as `adhd-unslop@adhd-unslop`.
  Revisit when `presentation` or another unrelated plugin arrives. A
  plugin rename could use Claude Code's `renames` map. Nothing documents a
  marketplace rename.

## Codex specifics

### D20. Invoke Codex skills by full name, never symlink

Users type `$adhd-unslop:adhd-unslop`. The README gives no
`~/.agents/skills` symlink route, and the doctor warns about one.

- Why: Codex names a symlinked skill after the plugin that contains its
  target, so a link into this repo became a second
  `adhd-unslop:adhd-unslop`. With two skills of one name, Codex injects
  neither. That caused the 2026-09-12 finding that plugin skills were
  missing from `codex exec`. The finding was wrong: plugin skills do load.
  A bare `$adhd-unslop` does not match a plugin skill.
- The README no longer offers a `~/.codex/AGENTS.md` fallback. It named a
  skill that Codex hides from the model, and hooks are the supported
  always-on path.

## Diagnostics

### D26. A user-only doctor skill

`adhd-unslop:doctor` runs `scripts/doctor.mjs` from its own folder. It
prints OK, WARN, or FAIL lines, each with its fix, and changes nothing. It
reports the runtime and plugin root, the installed version, the optional
mirrors, the always-on flags and switch, the chunk hashes and sizes, the
Codex hooks feature, the installed hook definitions, and a
`~/.agents/skills` name clash.

- Why: silent hooks make a broken install look the same as always-on being
  off. ECC, gstack, claude-octopus, planning-with-files, oh-my-codex, and
  oh-my-claudecode ship doctors (`research/04`).
- It never reports a missing mirror as a problem, because the mirrors are
  optional.
- It does not parse Codex trust records, whose layout is undocumented. It
  tells Codex users to confirm trust in `/hooks`.

## Testing and CI

### D21. End-to-end tests run the real CLIs in throwaway homes

`tests/e2e/run.sh` installs the marketplace into temporary Claude Code
and Codex homes and drives the models. By default it uses a copy of the
working tree. With `E2E_REPO` and `E2E_REF` it installs from GitHub.
`migrate` mode serves 0.2.2 and the working tree from a local `git
http-backend` and checks the upgrade in both runtimes.

- Why a git source for real paths: `claude plugin install` from a local
  directory writes a cache copy but reports that the plugin loads in place
  from that directory, so a local run may read the source instead of the
  cache. A git source takes the same path as a user's install. Claude Code
  takes `owner/repo#ref`, Codex takes `owner/repo --ref <ref>`, and Claude
  Code rejects `file://` URLs.
- The model's working directory sits away from the marketplace copy, and
  the homes are deleted on exit. Stray copies on disk caused two false
  passes.
- Codex needs a copy of `~/.codex/auth.json` in the throwaway home, deleted
  on exit, and `</dev/null` on every `codex exec`. Codex also writes the
  shell environment, API keys included, into
  `$CODEX_HOME/shell_snapshots/`, so the throwaway home must be deleted.
- It needs signed-in CLIs, so it runs locally. Run it before merging a
  change to skills, hooks, or manifests.

### D27. Keyless load checks in CI, with pinned CLIs

`verify.yml` runs on pull requests, pushes to `main`, and manual dispatch:

- `checks`: `sync.mjs --check`, `build.mjs --check`, unit tests, and on
  pull requests the version gate (D17).
- `load`: installs pinned Claude Code and Codex versions and runs
  `tools/load-check.mjs` in throwaway homes with no keys. It validates every
  manifest with `claude plugin validate --strict`, installs `adhd-unslop`
  alone in both CLIs and asserts that nothing else installs, installs the
  mirrors by name, and reads the Codex catalog through `codex app-server`
  (`plugin/list`, `plugin/read`, `hooks/list`).
- `workflows`: actionlint and zizmor.

- Why: both CLIs load plugins with no sign-in (`research/02`, `research/05`).
  trailofbits proved the pattern. Only the model-driven checks need keys.
- Why pinned: a CLI release that breaks plugin loading would otherwise turn
  every open PR red with no commit here to explain it.

### D28. A daily drift check against the latest CLIs

`cli-drift.yml` runs the same load check daily against the latest Claude
Code and Codex releases. On failure it opens or updates one issue. On a pass
with newer releases it opens or updates one PR, on branch `cli-pins`, that
raises the pins in `tools/cli-versions.json`, and starts `verify.yml` on it.

- Why: the platform facts below go stale with CLI releases. The drift job
  is the re-check, and the pins PR keeps CI current without a person
  watching for releases. caveman uses the same pinned-plus-drift model.
- Why a JSON file: `GITHUB_TOKEN` cannot push a change to a workflow file,
  so the pins cannot live in `verify.yml`.
- The latest CLIs run in a job with a read-only token. The jobs that open
  the issue or the PR run no CLI, so a bad CLI release never runs with
  write access.
- Before merging a pins PR, re-test the platform facts it could change and
  update the tested versions at the top of this file.

### D29. Workflow hygiene

- Actions are pinned by commit SHA with a version comment. Dependabot
  updates them weekly with a seven-day cooldown, in one grouped PR. The
  actionlint image and the zizmor version are pinned in `verify.yml` and
  raised by hand.
- `.gitattributes` sets LF line endings for hand-written files. It stores
  `upstream/` and every generated file byte for byte, so a mirror of a CRLF
  upstream stays identical to it, and it marks generated files as
  generated.
- No Markdown lint: upstream text must stay verbatim (D2).

    43	// Every upstream whose text a plugin ships: its mirror, the upstreams its skills
    44	// embed, and its always-on chunks. sync.mjs raises the version of each such plugin.
    45	export function upstreamsShipped(plugin) {
    46	  const names = new Set();
    47	  if (plugin.kind === "vendored") names.add(plugin.upstream);
    48	  for (const skill of Object.values(plugin.skills ?? {})) for (const n of skill.upstreams ?? []) names.add(n);
    49	  for (const chunk of plugin.alwaysOn ?? []) for (const part of chunk) if (part.upstream) names.add(part.upstream);
    50	  return [...names];
    51	}

    53	export function markers(name, pins) {
    54	  const pin = pins[name];
    55	  return {
    56	    begin: `<!-- BEGIN upstream ${name} ${pin.repo}/${pin.files["SKILL.md"].path} @${pin.commit} -->\n`,
    57	    end: `<!-- END upstream ${name} -->\n`,
    58	  };
    59	}
    60	
    61	// The upstream block (design/STRUCTURE-v2.md P1): the BEGIN line, the upstream
    62	// SKILL.md without frontmatter and with a final newline, the END line. The same
    63	// bytes go into a skill that embeds the upstream and into the always-on chunks.
    64	export function upstreamBlock(name, pins) {
    65	  const { begin, end } = markers(name, pins);
    66	  return begin + endsWithNewline(stripFrontmatter(read("upstream", name, "SKILL.md"))) + end;
    67	}

    69	// True when upstream frontmatter sets disable-model-invocation: true. Accepts
    70	// CRLF, since upstream files are kept byte for byte.
    71	export function userOnly(skillText) {
    72	  const m = skillText.match(/^---\r?\n([\s\S]*?)\r?\n---\r?\n/);
    73	  return Boolean(m && /^disable-model-invocation:\s*true\s*$/m.test(m[1]));
    74	}

    76	export function openaiYaml({ displayName, shortDescription, defaultPrompt, allowImplicit }) {
    77	  const lines = ["interface:", `  display_name: ${JSON.stringify(displayName)}`, `  short_description: ${JSON.stringify(shortDescription)}`];
    78	  if (defaultPrompt) lines.push(`  default_prompt: ${JSON.stringify(defaultPrompt)}`);
    79	  lines.push("", "policy:", `  allow_implicit_invocation: ${allowImplicit}`, "");
    80	  return lines.join("\n");
    81	}
    82	
    83	// Template syntax, one directive per line:
    84	//   {{include <path under src/<plugin>/>}}  inserts that file
    85	//   {{upstream <name>}}                     inserts the pinned upstream block
    86	// Any other line that starts with {{ fails the build, so a typo never ships.
    87	const DIRECTIVE = /^\{\{(include|upstream) ([^{}]+)\}\}\r?$/;
    88	
    89	export function templateUpstreams(text) {
    90	  return text.split("\n").map((line) => line.match(DIRECTIVE)).filter((m) => m && m[1] === "upstream").map((m) => m[2]);
    91	}
    92	
    93	export function renderTemplate(pluginName, text, pins = loadPins()) {
    94	  return text
    95	    .split("\n")
    96	    .map((raw) => {
    97	      const line = raw.replace(/\r$/, "");
    98	      if (line.startsWith("{{") && !DIRECTIVE.test(line)) throw new Error(`${pluginName}: unknown template line: ${line}`);
    99	      const inc = line.match(/^\{\{include (.+)\}\}$/);
   100	      if (inc) return read("src", pluginName, inc[1]).replace(/\n$/, "");
   101	      const up = line.match(/^\{\{upstream (.+)\}\}$/);
   102	      if (up) {
   103	        if (!pins[up[1]]) throw new Error(`${pluginName}: template embeds unpinned upstream ${up[1]}`);
   104	        return upstreamBlock(up[1], pins).replace(/\n$/, "");
   105	      }
   106	      return line;
   107	    })
   108	    .join("\n");
   109	}
   110	
   111	function walk(dir) {
   112	  const out = [];
   113	  if (!fs.existsSync(dir)) return out;
   114	  for (const entry of fs.readdirSync(dir, { withFileTypes: true })) {
   115	    if (IGNORED_NAMES.has(entry.name)) continue;
   116	    const abs = path.join(dir, entry.name);
   117	    if (entry.isDirectory()) out.push(...walk(abs));
   118	    else out.push(abs);
   119	  }
   120	  return out;
   121	}
   122	
   123	// The always-on chunks: each chunk is its parts joined by a blank line.
   124	export function composeChunks(plugin, pins) {
   125	  const chunks = (plugin.alwaysOn ?? []).map((parts) =>
   126	    parts
   127	      .map((part) => (part.upstream ? upstreamBlock(part.upstream, pins) : endsWithNewline(read("src", plugin.name, part.file))))
   128	      .join("\n"),
   129	  );
   130	  const body = chunks.join("");
   131	  const manifest = {
   132	    generatedBy: "tools/build.mjs",
   133	    compositeSha256: sha256(body),
   134	    chunks: chunks.map((c, i) => ({
   135	      index: i + 1,
   136	      file: `${i + 1}.md`,
   137	      sha256: sha256(c),
   138	      bytes: Buffer.byteLength(c, "utf8"),
   139	      utf16Units: c.length,
   140	    })),
   141	  };
   142	  return { chunks, body, manifest };
   143	}

   246	function noticeText(plugin, pins) {
   247	  const shipped = upstreamsShipped(plugin);
   248	  if (!shipped.length) return null;
   249	  const lines = [
   250	    "# Notice",
   251	    "",
   252	    plugin.kind === "vendored"
   253	      ? "This plugin ships an upstream skill file unchanged, byte for byte."
   254	      : "This plugin ships upstream skill text unchanged after removing its YAML frontmatter, in its skill and in the always-on hook chunks.",
   255	    "Each upstream keeps its own MIT license in `LICENSES/`.",
   256	    "",
   257	    "| Upstream | Repository | Commit | File | License file |",
   258	    "| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |",
   259	  ];
   260	  for (const name of shipped) {
   261	    const pin = pins[name];
   262	    lines.push(`| ${name} | https://github.com/${pin.repo} | ${pin.commit} | ${pin.files["SKILL.md"].path} | LICENSES/${name}.LICENSE |`);
   263	  }
   264	  if (shipped.includes("unslop")) lines.push("", "The unslop skill in pstack-claude is a port of Lauren Tan's pstack for Cursor.");
   265	  lines.push("");
   266	  return lines.join("\n");
   267	}

   269	export function expectedFiles() {
   270	  const config = loadConfig();
   271	  const pins = loadPins();
   272	  const files = new Map();
   273	  files.set(".claude-plugin/marketplace.json", json(claudeMarketplace(config)));
   274	  files.set(".agents/plugins/marketplace.json", json(codexMarketplace(config)));
   275	
   276	  for (const plugin of config.plugins) {
   277	    const root = `plugins/${plugin.name}`;
   278	    let hasHooks = false;
   279	
   280	    if (plugin.kind === "vendored") {
   281	      const text = read("upstream", plugin.upstream, "SKILL.md");
   282	      const skillDir = `${root}/skills/${plugin.skill}`;
   283	      files.set(`${skillDir}/SKILL.md`, text);
   284	      files.set(`${skillDir}/agents/openai.yaml`, openaiYaml({
   285	        displayName: plugin.codexInterface.displayName,
   286	        shortDescription: plugin.codexInterface.shortDescription,
   287	        allowImplicit: !userOnly(text),
   288	      }));
   289	    } else if (plugin.kind === "authored") {
   290	      const srcSkills = path.join(repo, "src", plugin.name, "skills");
   291	      const onDisk = fs.existsSync(srcSkills) ? fs.readdirSync(srcSkills).filter((d) => !IGNORED_NAMES.has(d)) : [];
   292	      const listed = Object.keys(plugin.skills ?? {});
   293	      const unlisted = onDisk.filter((d) => !listed.includes(d));
   294	      const missing = listed.filter((d) => !onDisk.includes(d));
   295	      if (unlisted.length || missing.length) {
   296	        throw new Error(`${plugin.name}: skills in tools/plugins.json and src/${plugin.name}/skills/ differ (unlisted: ${unlisted.join(", ") || "none"}; missing: ${missing.join(", ") || "none"})`);
   297	      }
   298	      for (const [skill, spec] of Object.entries(plugin.skills ?? {})) {
   299	        const srcDir = path.join(srcSkills, skill);
   300	        let embedded = [];
   301	        for (const abs of walk(srcDir)) {
   302	          const rel = path.relative(srcDir, abs).split(path.sep).join("/");
   303	          const out = `${root}/skills/${skill}/`;
   304	          if (rel === "SKILL.md.tmpl") {
   305	            const tmpl = fs.readFileSync(abs, "utf8");
   306	            embedded = templateUpstreams(tmpl);
   307	            files.set(out + "SKILL.md", renderTemplate(plugin.name, tmpl, pins));
   308	          } else {
   309	            files.set(out + rel, fs.readFileSync(abs, "utf8"));
   310	          }
   311	        }
   312	        const listed = spec.upstreams ?? [];
   313	        if (embedded.join() !== listed.join()) {
   314	          throw new Error(`${plugin.name}:${skill}: the template embeds [${embedded.join(", ")}] but tools/plugins.json lists upstreams [${listed.join(", ")}]`);
   315	        }
   316	      }
   317	      const srcHooks = path.join(repo, "src", plugin.name, "hooks");
   318	      for (const abs of walk(srcHooks)) {
   319	        hasHooks = true;
   320	        files.set(`${root}/hooks/${path.relative(srcHooks, abs).split(path.sep).join("/")}`, fs.readFileSync(abs, "utf8"));
   321	      }
   322	      if (plugin.alwaysOn) {
   323	        const { chunks, manifest } = composeChunks(plugin, pins);
   324	        if (chunks.length !== TOTAL_CHUNKS) throw new Error(`${plugin.name}: alwaysOn lists ${chunks.length} chunks; the launcher expects ${TOTAL_CHUNKS}`);
   325	        chunks.forEach((c, i) => files.set(`${root}/hooks/chunks/${i + 1}.md`, c));
   326	        files.set(`${root}/hooks/chunks/manifest.json`, json(manifest));
   327	      }
   328	    } else {
   329	      throw new Error(`${plugin.name}: unknown kind ${plugin.kind}`);
   330	    }
   331	
   332	    files.set(`${root}/.claude-plugin/plugin.json`, json(claudePluginJson(plugin, config)));
   333	    files.set(`${root}/.codex-plugin/plugin.json`, json(codexPluginJson(plugin, config, hasHooks)));
   334	    files.set(`${root}/README.md`, pluginReadme(plugin, config));
   335	    const notice = noticeText(plugin, pins);
   336	    if (notice) files.set(`${root}/NOTICE.md`, notice);
   337	    for (const up of upstreamsShipped(plugin)) files.set(`${root}/LICENSES/${up}.LICENSE`, read("upstream", up, "LICENSE"));
   338	  }
   339	  return files;
   340	}

   342	// Files under a generated folder that the build would not write. `root` lets
   343	// tests run against a copy instead of the working tree.
   344	export function strayFiles(expected = expectedFiles(), root = repo) {
   345	  const strays = [];
   346	  for (const top of GENERATED_ROOTS) {
   347	    for (const abs of walk(path.join(root, top))) {
   348	      const rel = path.relative(root, abs).split(path.sep).join("/");
   349	      if (!expected.has(rel)) strays.push(rel);
   350	    }
   351	  }
   352	  return strays.sort();
   353	}
   354	
   355	export function staleFiles(expected = expectedFiles()) {
   356	  const stale = [];
   357	  for (const [file, text] of expected) {
   358	    let current = null;
   359	    try { current = read(file); } catch { /* missing */ }
   360	    if (current !== text) stale.push(file);
   361	  }
   362	  return stale;
   363	}
   364	
   365	export function writeAll(expected = expectedFiles()) {
   366	  for (const [file, text] of expected) {
   367	    const abs = path.join(repo, file);
   368	    fs.mkdirSync(path.dirname(abs), { recursive: true });
   369	    if (!fs.existsSync(abs) || fs.readFileSync(abs, "utf8") !== text) fs.writeFileSync(abs, text);
   370	  }
   371	}
   372	
   373	function removeEmptyDirs(dir) {
   374	  if (!fs.existsSync(dir)) return;
   375	  for (const entry of fs.readdirSync(dir, { withFileTypes: true })) {
   376	    if (entry.isDirectory()) removeEmptyDirs(path.join(dir, entry.name));
   377	  }
   378	  if (fs.readdirSync(dir).length === 0) fs.rmdirSync(dir);
   379	}
   380	
   381	export function prune(expected = expectedFiles(), root = repo) {
   382	  const strays = strayFiles(expected, root);
   383	  for (const rel of strays) fs.rmSync(path.join(root, rel));
   384	  for (const top of GENERATED_ROOTS) removeEmptyDirs(path.join(root, top));
   385	  return strays;
   386	}
   387	
   388	if (process.argv[1] && path.resolve(process.argv[1]) === fileURLToPath(import.meta.url)) {
   389	  try {
   390	    const expected = expectedFiles();
   391	    if (process.argv.includes("--check")) {
   392	      const stale = staleFiles(expected);
   393	      const strays = strayFiles(expected);
   394	      if (stale.length) console.error("stale or missing generated files:\n  " + stale.join("\n  "));
   395	      if (strays.length) console.error("stray files under generated folders (run node tools/build.mjs --prune):\n  " + strays.join("\n  "));
   396	      if (stale.length || strays.length) process.exit(1);
   397	      console.log("generated files are current");
   398	    } else {
   399	      writeAll(expected);
   400	      console.log(`wrote ${expected.size} generated files`);
   401	      if (process.argv.includes("--prune")) {
   402	        for (const rel of prune(expected)) console.log(`deleted stray ${rel}`);
   403	      } else {
   404	        const strays = strayFiles(expected);
   405	        if (strays.length) console.warn("stray files under generated folders (delete with --prune):\n  " + strays.join("\n  "));
   406	      }
   407	    }
   408	  } catch (err) {
   409	    console.error(err.message);
   410	    process.exit(1);
   411	  }
   412	}
     1	#!/usr/bin/env node
     2	// Keep upstream/ in step with the pins in tools/upstream.json.
     3	//
     4	//   node tools/sync.mjs --check                 verify upstream/ files against pinned sha256
     5	//   node tools/sync.mjs --bump <name> <commit>  fetch <name> at <commit> into .sync-staging/,
     6	//                                               check dependencies and rule citations, swap in,
     7	//                                               raise plugin versions, build and test,
     8	//                                               promote on success, restore on failure
     9	//   node tools/sync.mjs --verify-remote         refetch every pinned file at its pinned commit and
    10	//                                               compare it with the pinned sha256
    11	//   node tools/sync.mjs --latest [--report <file>]
    12	//                                               bump every upstream whose pinned files changed
    13	//                                               on its default branch, write a Markdown report,
    14	//                                               exit 1 if any bump failed
    15	//
    16	// Set GITHUB_TOKEN to avoid the unauthenticated GitHub API rate limit.
    17	// No dependencies. Uses global fetch (Node 18 or later).
    18	
    19	import { execFileSync } from "node:child_process";
    20	import fs from "node:fs";
    21	import path from "node:path";
    22	import { fileURLToPath } from "node:url";
    23	import { sha256, stripFrontmatter } from "../src/adhd-unslop/hooks/lib.mjs";
    24	import { GENERATED_ROOTS, upstreamsShipped } from "./build.mjs";
    25	
    26	const repo = path.join(path.dirname(fileURLToPath(import.meta.url)), "..");
    27	const pinsPath = path.join(repo, "tools", "upstream.json");
    28	const staging = path.join(repo, ".sync-staging");
    29	const overlayDir = path.join(repo, "src", "adhd-unslop", "overlay");
    30	
    31	const read = (p) => fs.readFileSync(p, "utf8");
    32	const readPins = () => JSON.parse(read(pinsPath));
    33	const configPath = path.join(repo, "tools", "plugins.json");
    34	const readConfig = () => JSON.parse(read(configPath));

    36	export function checkPins(pins = readPins()) {
    37	  const problems = [];
    38	  for (const [name, pin] of Object.entries(pins.upstreams)) {
    39	    for (const [file, meta] of Object.entries(pin.files)) {
    40	      const local = path.join(repo, "upstream", name, file);
    41	      if (!fs.existsSync(local)) { problems.push(`${name}/${file}: missing`); continue; }
    42	      const actual = sha256(read(local));
    43	      if (actual !== meta.sha256) problems.push(`${name}/${file}: sha256 ${actual} != pinned ${meta.sha256}`);
    44	    }
    45	  }
    46	  return problems;
    47	}
    48	
    49	// Runtime dependencies the composite cannot ship: relative Markdown links and
    50	// sibling directories a skill would read at run time.
    51	export function dependencyHits(body) {
    52	  const hits = [];
    53	  body.split("\n").forEach((line, i) => {
    54	    if (/\]\((?!https?:|#|mailto:)[^)]+\)/.test(line)) hits.push(`${i + 1}: relative link: ${line.trim()}`);
    55	    if (/(^|[\s`(])(\.\/)?(references|scripts|agents)\//.test(line)) hits.push(`${i + 1}: sibling directory: ${line.trim()}`);
    56	  });
    57	  return hits;
    58	}
    59	
    60	// Upstream files are kept byte for byte, so a body may use CRLF. Every reader
    61	// below works on LF.
    62	const lf = (text) => text.replace(/\r\n/g, "\n");
    63	
    64	// Numbered items in the section that starts with `heading`, up to the next `## `.
    65	function listNumbers(body, heading) {
    66	  const start = body.indexOf(`\n${heading}\n`);
    67	  if (start < 0) return [];
    68	  const rest = body.slice(start + heading.length + 2);
    69	  const end = rest.search(/^## /m);
    70	  const section = end < 0 ? rest : rest.slice(0, end);
    71	  return [...section.matchAll(/^(\d+)\. /gm)].map((m) => Number(m[1]));
    72	}
    73	
    74	// Every citation label the overlay may use, the upstream it points into, and
    75	// how to read the numbers that exist in that upstream body.
    76	export const CITATION_KINDS = [
    77	  { label: "ADHD rule", upstream: "i-have-adhd", numbers: (b) => [...lf(b).matchAll(/^### (\d+)\. /gm)].map((m) => Number(m[1])) },
    78	  { label: "ADHD exception", upstream: "i-have-adhd", numbers: (b) => listNumbers(lf(b), "## When to break the rules") },
    79	  { label: "ADHD check", upstream: "i-have-adhd", numbers: (b) => listNumbers(lf(b), "## Pre-send check") },
    80	  { label: "unslop rule", upstream: "unslop", numbers: (b) => [...lf(b).matchAll(/^(\d+)\. \*\*/gm)].map((m) => Number(m[1])) },
    81	  { label: "unslop process", upstream: "unslop", numbers: (b) => listNumbers(lf(b), "## Process") },
    82	];
    83	
    84	const kindFor = (label) => CITATION_KINDS.find((k) => k.label === label);
    85	const ruleLabel = (name) => (name === "unslop" ? "unslop rule" : "ADHD rule");
    86	
    87	export function ruleNumbers(name, body) {
    88	  return kindFor(ruleLabel(name)).numbers(body);
    89	}
    90	
    91	export function citedNumbers(label) {
    92	  const text = fs.readdirSync(overlayDir).map((f) => read(path.join(overlayDir, f))).join("\n");
    93	  const re = new RegExp(`${label}s? (\\d+)(?:(?:,| and| to) (\\d+))*`, "g");
    94	  const cited = new Set();
    95	  for (const m of text.matchAll(re)) {
    96	    const nums = m[0].match(/\d+/g).map(Number);
    97	    if (/ to /.test(m[0]) && nums.length === 2) for (let n = nums[0]; n <= nums[1]; n++) cited.add(n);
    98	    else nums.forEach((n) => cited.add(n));
    99	  }
   100	  return cited;
   101	}
   102	
   103	export function overlayCitations(name) {
   104	  return citedNumbers(ruleLabel(name));
   105	}
   106	
   107	export function citationReport(name, oldBody, newBody) {
   108	  const warnings = [];
   109	  const failures = [];
   110	  for (const kind of CITATION_KINDS.filter((k) => k.upstream === name)) {
   111	    const oldNums = new Set(kind.numbers(oldBody));
   112	    const newNums = new Set(kind.numbers(newBody));
   113	    const cited = citedNumbers(kind.label);
   114	    if (kind.label === ruleLabel(name)) {
   115	      warnings.push(...[...newNums].filter((n) => !oldNums.has(n) && !cited.has(n)).map((n) => `${kind.label} ${n} is new and not cited in the overlay`));
   116	    }
   117	    failures.push(...[...cited].filter((n) => !newNums.has(n)).map((n) => `the overlay cites ${kind.label} ${n}, which no longer exists upstream`));
   118	  }
   119	  return { warnings, failures };
   120	}
   121	
   122	function githubHeaders() {
   123	  const h = { Accept: "application/vnd.github+json", "User-Agent": "adhd-unslop-sync" };
   124	  if (process.env.GITHUB_TOKEN) h.Authorization = `Bearer ${process.env.GITHUB_TOKEN}`;
   125	  return h;
   126	}
   127	
   128	async function fetchRaw(repoSlug, commit, filePath) {
   129	  const url = `https://raw.githubusercontent.com/${repoSlug}/${commit}/${filePath}`;
   130	  const res = await fetch(url);
   131	  if (!res.ok) throw new Error(`${res.status} fetching ${url}`);
   132	  return res.text();
   133	}
   134	
   135	// Newest commit on the default branch that touched any pinned file of this upstream.
   136	export async function latestCommit(pin) {
   137	  let newest = null;
   138	  for (const meta of Object.values(pin.files)) {
   139	    const url = `https://api.github.com/repos/${pin.repo}/commits?path=${encodeURIComponent(meta.path)}&per_page=1`;
   140	    const res = await fetch(url, { headers: githubHeaders() });
   141	    if (!res.ok) throw new Error(`${res.status} fetching ${url}`);
   142	    const [c] = await res.json();
   143	    if (c && (!newest || c.commit.committer.date > newest.date)) newest = { sha: c.sha, date: c.commit.committer.date };
   144	  }
   145	  return newest?.sha ?? null;
   146	}
   147	
   148	export function bumpPatch(version) {
   149	  const m = /^(\d+)\.(\d+)\.(\d+)$/.exec(version);
   150	  if (!m) throw new Error(`cannot bump version ${version}`);
   151	  return `${m[1]}.${m[2]}.${Number(m[3]) + 1}`;
   152	}
   153	
   154	// Plugins whose shipped text includes one of these upstreams: its mirror, any
   155	// skill that embeds it, and any always-on chunk that carries it.
   156	export function pluginsEmbedding(config, names) {
   157	  return config.plugins.filter((p) => upstreamsShipped(p).some((n) => names.includes(n))).map((p) => p.name);
   158	}
   159	
   160	// Raise each affected plugin's patch version once, however many upstreams changed.
   161	export function raiseVersions(config, names) {
   162	  const affected = pluginsEmbedding(config, names);
   163	  for (const p of config.plugins) if (affected.includes(p.name)) p.version = bumpPatch(p.version);
   164	  return config.plugins.filter((p) => affected.includes(p.name)).map((p) => `${p.name} ${p.version}`);
   165	}

   167	function run(cmd, args) {
   168	  execFileSync(cmd, args, { cwd: repo, stdio: "inherit" });
   169	}
   170	
   171	function buildAndTest() {
   172	  run("node", ["tools/build.mjs"]);
   173	  run("node", ["--test", ...fs.readdirSync(path.join(repo, "tests")).filter((f) => f.endsWith(".test.mjs")).map((f) => path.join("tests", f))]);
   174	}

   176	const GENERATED = GENERATED_ROOTS;
   177	
   178	// Copy everything a bump can change, and return a function that puts it back.
   179	function snapshot(label) {
   180	  const dir = path.join(staging, `${label}.backup`);
   181	  fs.rmSync(dir, { recursive: true, force: true });
   182	  for (const r of [...GENERATED, "upstream", "tools/upstream.json", "tools/plugins.json"]) {
   183	    fs.cpSync(path.join(repo, r), path.join(dir, r), { recursive: true });
   184	  }
   185	  return {
   186	    restore() {
   187	      for (const r of [...GENERATED, "upstream", "tools/upstream.json", "tools/plugins.json"]) {
   188	        fs.rmSync(path.join(repo, r), { recursive: true, force: true });
   189	        fs.cpSync(path.join(dir, r), path.join(repo, r), { recursive: true });
   190	      }
   191	      fs.rmSync(dir, { recursive: true, force: true });
   192	    },
   193	    discard() {
   194	      fs.rmSync(dir, { recursive: true, force: true });
   195	    },
   196	  };
   197	}
   198	
   199	async function fetchUpstream(pin, commit) {
   200	  const fetched = {};
   201	  for (const [file, meta] of Object.entries(pin.files)) fetched[file] = await fetchRaw(pin.repo, commit, meta.path);
   202	  return fetched;
   203	}
   204	
   205	// Returns { name, from, to, warnings, versions }. Throws on refusal or failure,
   206	// after restoring every file it touched.
   207	export async function bump(name, commit, { versions = true, fetched } = {}) {
   208	  const pins = readPins();
   209	  const pin = pins.upstreams[name];
   210	  if (!pin) throw new Error(`unknown upstream ${name}; known: ${Object.keys(pins.upstreams).join(", ")}`);
   211	  const stageDir = path.join(staging, name);
   212	  fs.rmSync(stageDir, { recursive: true, force: true });
   213	  fs.mkdirSync(stageDir, { recursive: true });
   214	
   215	  fetched ??= await fetchUpstream(pin, commit);
   216	  for (const [file, text] of Object.entries(fetched)) fs.writeFileSync(path.join(stageDir, file), text);
   217	  const newBody = stripFrontmatter(fetched["SKILL.md"]);
   218	  const deps = dependencyHits(newBody);
   219	  if (deps.length) {
   220	    throw new Error(`refusing to bump ${name}: new body has runtime dependencies the plugins do not ship:\n  ${deps.join("\n  ")}\nstaged files left in ${stageDir}`);
   221	  }
   222	  const oldBody = stripFrontmatter(read(path.join(repo, "upstream", name, "SKILL.md")));
   223	  const { warnings, failures } = citationReport(name, oldBody, newBody);
   224	  if (failures.length) throw new Error(`refusing to bump ${name}:\n  ${failures.join("\n  ")}\nstaged files left in ${stageDir}`);
   225	
   226	  const backup = snapshot(name);
   227	  const from = pin.commit;
   228	  let raised = [];
   229	  try {
   230	    for (const [file, text] of Object.entries(fetched)) {
   231	      fs.writeFileSync(path.join(repo, "upstream", name, file), text);
   232	      pin.files[file].sha256 = sha256(text);
   233	    }
   234	    pin.commit = commit;
   235	    fs.writeFileSync(pinsPath, JSON.stringify(pins, null, 2) + "\n");
   236	    if (versions) {
   237	      const config = readConfig();
   238	      raised = raiseVersions(config, [name]);
   239	      fs.writeFileSync(configPath, JSON.stringify(config, null, 2) + "\n");
   240	    }
   241	    buildAndTest();
   242	  } catch (err) {
   243	    backup.restore();
   244	    throw new Error(`bump of ${name} failed and was rolled back (${err.message}). Staged files remain in ${stageDir}.`);
   245	  }
   246	  backup.discard();
   247	  fs.rmSync(stageDir, { recursive: true, force: true });
   248	  return { name, from, to: commit, warnings, versions: raised };
   249	}
   250	
   251	export async function latest() {
   252	  const pins = readPins();
   253	  const results = [];
   254	  for (const [name, pin] of Object.entries(pins.upstreams)) {
   255	    try {
   256	      const sha = await latestCommit(pin);
   257	      if (!sha || sha === pin.commit) {
   258	        results.push({ name, status: "current" });
   259	        continue;
   260	      }
   261	      const fetched = await fetchUpstream(pin, sha);
   262	      const unchanged = Object.entries(pin.files).every(([file, meta]) => sha256(fetched[file]) === meta.sha256);
   263	      if (unchanged) {
   264	        results.push({ name, status: "unchanged", to: sha });
   265	        continue;
   266	      }
   267	      const r = await bump(name, sha, { versions: false, fetched });
   268	      results.push({ ...r, status: "bumped" });
   269	    } catch (err) {
   270	      results.push({ name, status: "failed", error: err.message });
   271	    }
   272	  }
   273	  const bumped = results.filter((r) => r.status === "bumped").map((r) => r.name);
   274	  let versions = [];
   275	  if (bumped.length) {
   276	    const config = readConfig();
   277	    versions = raiseVersions(config, bumped);
   278	    fs.writeFileSync(configPath, JSON.stringify(config, null, 2) + "\n");
   279	    buildAndTest();
   280	  }
   281	  return { results, versions };
   282	}
   283	
   284	export function reportMarkdown({ results, versions }, pins = readPins()) {
   285	  const lines = ["# Upstream skill updates", "", "| Upstream | Result | Detail |", "| --- | --- | --- |"];
   286	  for (const r of results) {
   287	    const repoSlug = pins.upstreams[r.name].repo;
   288	    if (r.status === "bumped") lines.push(`| ${r.name} | updated | [${r.from.slice(0, 7)}...${r.to.slice(0, 7)}](https://github.com/${repoSlug}/compare/${r.from}...${r.to}) |`);
   289	    else if (r.status === "unchanged") lines.push(`| ${r.name} | no change | ${r.to.slice(0, 7)} changed no pinned file |`);
   290	    else if (r.status === "current") lines.push(`| ${r.name} | no change | pinned commit is the latest |`);
   291	    else lines.push(`| ${r.name} | failed | see below |`);
   292	  }
   293	  if (versions.length) {
   294	    lines.push("", "## New plugin versions", "", ...versions.map((v) => `- ${v}`), "");
   295	    lines.push("Installed copies update only when each plugin is updated. Neither `claude plugin update` nor Codex updates dependencies on their own.");
   296	  }
   297	  const warnings = results.flatMap((r) => r.warnings ?? []);
   298	  if (warnings.length) lines.push("", "## Warnings", "", ...warnings.map((w) => `- ${w}`));
   299	  const failed = results.filter((r) => r.status === "failed");
   300	  if (failed.length) {
   301	    lines.push("", "## Failures", "");
   302	    for (const f of failed) lines.push(`### ${f.name}`, "", "```", f.error, "```", "");
   303	    lines.push("A failure usually means upstream removed a rule the overlay cites. Update `src/adhd-unslop/overlay/`, then run `node tools/sync.mjs --bump <name> <commit>`.");
   304	  }
   305	  lines.push("", "Review the upstream diff for new conflicts and record them in the outcome table in `src/adhd-unslop/overlay/10-precedence.md`.", "");
   306	  return lines.join("\n");
   307	}
   308	
   309	// Refetch each pinned file at its pinned commit and compare it with the pin.
   310	// Catches a hand edit to upstream/ that also rewrote the sha256 in the pin.
   311	export async function verifyRemote(pins = readPins()) {
   312	  const problems = [];
   313	  for (const [name, pin] of Object.entries(pins.upstreams)) {
   314	    for (const [file, meta] of Object.entries(pin.files)) {
   315	      const text = await fetchRaw(pin.repo, pin.commit, meta.path);
   316	      const actual = sha256(text);
   317	      if (actual !== meta.sha256) problems.push(`${name}/${file}: upstream at ${pin.commit} has sha256 ${actual}, pinned ${meta.sha256}`);
   318	    }
   319	  }
   320	  return problems;
   321	}
   322	
   323	if (process.argv[1] && path.resolve(process.argv[1]) === fileURLToPath(import.meta.url)) {
   324	  const [, , cmd, ...rest] = process.argv;
   325	  try {
   326	    if (cmd === "--check") {
   327	      const problems = checkPins();
   328	      if (problems.length) { console.error(problems.join("\n")); process.exit(1); }
   329	      console.log("upstream/ matches tools/upstream.json");
   330	    } else if (cmd === "--verify-remote") {
   331	      const problems = await verifyRemote();
   332	      if (problems.length) { console.error(problems.join("\n")); process.exit(1); }
   333	      console.log("every pinned file matches its upstream commit");
   334	    } else if (cmd === "--bump" && rest.length === 2) {
   335	      const r = await bump(rest[0], rest[1]);
   336	      r.warnings.forEach((w) => console.warn(`warning: ${w}`));
   337	      console.log(`promoted ${r.name} to ${r.to}; new versions: ${r.versions.join(", ") || "none"}. Review: git diff`);
   338	    } else if (cmd === "--latest") {
   339	      const i = rest.indexOf("--report");
   340	      const summary = await latest();
   341	      const md = reportMarkdown(summary);
   342	      if (i >= 0 && rest[i + 1]) fs.writeFileSync(rest[i + 1], md);
   343	      console.log(md);
   344	      if (summary.results.some((r) => r.status === "failed")) process.exit(1);
   345	    } else {
   346	      console.error("usage: node tools/sync.mjs --check | --verify-remote | --bump <name> <commit> | --latest [--report <file>]");
   347	      process.exit(2);
   348	    }
   349	  } catch (err) {
   350	    console.error(err.message);
   351	    process.exit(1);
   352	  }
   353	}
     1	#!/usr/bin/env node
     2	// Fail when a plugin's shipped files changed but its version did not rise.
     3	//
     4	//   node tools/version-gate.mjs --base <git-ref>
     5	//
     6	// For each plugin in tools/plugins.json at HEAD: when
     7	// `git diff --name-only <base>...HEAD -- plugins/<name>/` lists any file
     8	// (changed, added, or removed), the plugin's version at HEAD must be greater,
     9	// by semver, than its version in tools/plugins.json at <base>. A plugin absent
    10	// at <base> passes. Installed copies update only on a version change, so this
    11	// enforces the rule in AGENTS.md.
    12	//
    13	// Exits 1 when a plugin fails, and 2 on a usage or git error.
    14	
    15	import { spawnSync } from "node:child_process";
    16	import path from "node:path";
    17	import { fileURLToPath } from "node:url";
    18	
    19	const SEMVER = /^(0|[1-9]\d*)\.(0|[1-9]\d*)\.(0|[1-9]\d*)(?:-((?:0|[1-9]\d*|\d*[A-Za-z-][0-9A-Za-z-]*)(?:\.(?:0|[1-9]\d*|\d*[A-Za-z-][0-9A-Za-z-]*))*))?(?:\+[0-9A-Za-z-]+(?:\.[0-9A-Za-z-]+)*)?$/;
    20	
    21	// Parse a semver 2.0.0 version, or return null.
    22	export function parseSemver(version) {
    23	  const m = typeof version === "string" ? version.match(SEMVER) : null;
    24	  if (!m) return null;
    25	  return { core: [BigInt(m[1]), BigInt(m[2]), BigInt(m[3])], pre: m[4] ? m[4].split(".") : [] };
    26	}
    27	
    28	// Semver precedence: -1, 0, or 1. Build metadata is ignored. Throws on an invalid version.
    29	export function compareSemver(a, b) {
    30	  const pa = parseSemver(a);
    31	  const pb = parseSemver(b);
    32	  if (!pa) throw new Error(`not a semver version: ${JSON.stringify(a)}`);
    33	  if (!pb) throw new Error(`not a semver version: ${JSON.stringify(b)}`);
    34	  for (let i = 0; i < 3; i++) {
    35	    if (pa.core[i] !== pb.core[i]) return pa.core[i] < pb.core[i] ? -1 : 1;
    36	  }
    37	  // A version with a prerelease sorts before the same version without one.
    38	  if (!pa.pre.length || !pb.pre.length) return pa.pre.length === pb.pre.length ? 0 : pa.pre.length ? -1 : 1;
    39	  for (let i = 0; i < Math.max(pa.pre.length, pb.pre.length); i++) {
    40	    const x = pa.pre[i];
    41	    const y = pb.pre[i];
    42	    if (x === undefined) return -1;
    43	    if (y === undefined) return 1;
    44	    if (x === y) continue;
    45	    const xNum = /^\d+$/.test(x);
    46	    const yNum = /^\d+$/.test(y);
    47	    if (xNum && yNum) return BigInt(x) < BigInt(y) ? -1 : 1;
    48	    if (xNum !== yNum) return xNum ? -1 : 1;
    49	    return x < y ? -1 : 1;
    50	  }
    51	  return 0;
    52	}
    53	
    54	// Versions by plugin name from a parsed tools/plugins.json.
    55	export function versionsOf(config) {
    56	  const out = new Map();
    57	  for (const p of config?.plugins ?? []) out.set(p.name, p.version);
    58	  return out;
    59	}
    60	
    61	// The gate itself, with no git.
    62	//   head:    parsed tools/plugins.json at HEAD
    63	//   base:    parsed tools/plugins.json at the base, or null when the base has none
    64	//   changed: plugin name -> files changed under plugins/<name>/
    65	// Returns one result per plugin at HEAD: { name, ok, message }.
    66	export function evaluate({ head, base, changed }) {
    67	  const baseVersions = versionsOf(base);
    68	  return (head?.plugins ?? []).map(({ name, version }) => {
    69	    const files = changed.get?.(name) ?? changed[name] ?? [];
    70	    const result = (ok, message) => ({ name, ok, message });
    71	    if (!files.length) return result(true, `no changes under plugins/${name}/ (${version})`);
    72	    const count = `${files.length} file${files.length === 1 ? "" : "s"} changed`;
    73	    if (!parseSemver(version)) return result(false, `${count}, but the version at HEAD, ${JSON.stringify(version)}, is not semver`);
    74	    if (!baseVersions.has(name)) return result(true, `${count}, new plugin at ${version}`);
    75	    const before = baseVersions.get(name);
    76	    if (!parseSemver(before)) return result(false, `${count}, but the version at the base, ${JSON.stringify(before)}, is not semver`);
    77	    if (compareSemver(version, before) > 0) return result(true, `${count}, version ${before} -> ${version}`);
    78	    return result(false, `${count}, but the version is ${version} and must rise above ${before} in tools/plugins.json`);
    79	  });
    80	}
    81	
    82	function git(cwd, args) {
    83	  const r = spawnSync("git", args, { cwd, stdio: ["ignore", "pipe", "pipe"], encoding: "utf8", maxBuffer: 64 * 1024 * 1024 });
    84	  if (r.error) throw new Error(`git ${args.join(" ")}: ${r.error.message}`);
    85	  return { ok: r.status === 0, stdout: r.stdout, stderr: r.stderr.trim() };
    86	}
    87	
    88	function mustGit(cwd, args) {
    89	  const r = git(cwd, args);
    90	  if (!r.ok) throw new Error(`git ${args.join(" ")} failed: ${r.stderr}`);
    91	  return r.stdout;
    92	}
    93	
    94	// Read the inputs from git in `cwd` and evaluate them.
    95	export function gate({ base, cwd }) {
    96	  if (!git(cwd, ["rev-parse", "--verify", "--quiet", `${base}^{commit}`]).ok) {
    97	    throw new Error(`base ${base} is not a commit here (a shallow clone needs fetch-depth: 0)`);
    98	  }
    99	  const head = JSON.parse(mustGit(cwd, ["show", "HEAD:tools/plugins.json"]));
   100	  const atBase = git(cwd, ["cat-file", "-e", `${base}:tools/plugins.json`]).ok
   101	    ? JSON.parse(mustGit(cwd, ["show", `${base}:tools/plugins.json`]))
   102	    : null;
   103	  const changed = new Map();
   104	  for (const { name } of head.plugins ?? []) {
   105	    const out = mustGit(cwd, ["diff", "--name-only", "--no-renames", `${base}...HEAD`, "--", `plugins/${name}/`]);
   106	    changed.set(name, out.split("\n").filter(Boolean));
   107	  }
   108	  return { results: evaluate({ head, base: atBase, changed }), changed, baseHasConfig: atBase !== null };
   109	}
   110	
   111	if (process.argv[1] && path.resolve(process.argv[1]) === fileURLToPath(import.meta.url)) {
   112	  const args = process.argv.slice(2);
   113	  const i = args.indexOf("--base");
   114	  const base = i >= 0 ? args[i + 1] : undefined;
   115	  if (!base || base.startsWith("--") || args.length !== 2) {
   116	    console.error("usage: node tools/version-gate.mjs --base <git-ref>");
   117	    process.exit(2);
   118	  }
   119	  const repo = path.join(path.dirname(fileURLToPath(import.meta.url)), "..");
   120	  let outcome;
   121	  try {
   122	    outcome = gate({ base, cwd: repo });
   123	  } catch (err) {
   124	    console.error(err.message);
   125	    process.exit(2);
   126	  }
   127	  if (!outcome.baseHasConfig) console.log(`${base} has no tools/plugins.json; every plugin counts as new`);
   128	  for (const r of outcome.results) {
   129	    console.log(`${r.ok ? "PASS" : "FAIL"}  ${r.name}: ${r.message}`);
   130	    if (!r.ok) for (const f of outcome.changed.get(r.name).slice(0, 20)) console.log(`      ${f}`);
   131	  }
   132	  if (!outcome.results.length) {
   133	    console.log("FAIL  tools/plugins.json at HEAD lists no plugins");
   134	    process.exit(1);
   135	  }
   136	  process.exit(outcome.results.every((r) => r.ok) ? 0 : 1);
   137	}

    36	// ADHD_UNSLOP_ALWAYS overrides the flag files for one process.
    37	// Unset or empty: the flag files decide. 0, false, off: off. 1, true, on: on.
    38	// Any other value counts as unset, and the doctor reports it.
    39	export function alwaysOnSetting(env = process.env) {
    40	  const raw = env.ADHD_UNSLOP_ALWAYS;
    41	  if (raw === undefined || raw === "") return { mode: "unset", raw };
    42	  const value = raw.trim().toLowerCase();
    43	  if (["0", "false", "off"].includes(value)) return { mode: "off", raw };
    44	  if (["1", "true", "on"].includes(value)) return { mode: "on", raw };
    45	  return { mode: "invalid", raw };
    46	}

    48	export function flagExists(env = process.env, home = os.homedir()) {
    49	  return flagPaths(env, home).some((p) => {
    50	    try {

    52	    } catch {
    53	      return false;
    54	    }
    55	  });
    56	}

    58	export function optedIn(env = process.env, home = os.homedir()) {
    59	  const { mode } = alwaysOnSetting(env);
    60	  if (mode === "off") return false;
    61	  if (mode === "on") return true;
    62	  return flagExists(env, home);

    81	// Read the SessionStart payload from stdin. Resolves to the parsed object, or
    82	// null when stdin is a TTY, empty, invalid, or silent for timeoutMs.
    83	export function readHookInput(stream = process.stdin, timeoutMs = 1000) {
    84	  return new Promise((resolve) => {
    85	    if (!stream || stream.isTTY) {
    86	      resolve(null);
    87	      return;
    88	    }
    89	    let data = "";
    90	    let done = false;
    91	    const finish = () => {
    92	      if (done) return;
    93	      done = true;
    94	      clearTimeout(timer);
    95	      try {
    96	        resolve(data.trim() ? JSON.parse(data) : null);
    97	      } catch {
    98	        resolve(null);
    99	      }
   100	    };
   101	    const timer = setTimeout(finish, timeoutMs);
   102	    stream.setEncoding("utf8");
   103	    stream.on("data", (chunk) => {
   104	      data += chunk;
   105	    });
   106	    stream.on("end", finish);
   107	    stream.on("error", finish);
   108	  });
   109	}

   111	export function bundleId(compositeSha) {
   112	  return compositeSha.slice(0, BUNDLE_ID_LENGTH);
   113	}

   115	export function chunkHeader(index, id) {
   116	  return [
   117	    `ADHD-UNSLOP INSTRUCTIONS. Chunk ${index} of ${TOTAL_CHUNKS} from bundle ${id}.`,
   118	    `These instructions come from the adhd-unslop always-on hook, which the user turned on. A bundle is complete when all ${TOTAL_CHUNKS} chunks with the same bundle id are present, each ending with its END line. Until a bundle is complete, the previously selected complete bundle and the current mode states stay in effect, the missing chunk is named once, and nothing activates from the partial set.`,
   119	    "A repeated chunk with the same bundle id and index is a repeat, not a new activation. Chunks from different bundle ids are never combined. A newly completed bundle replaces its rules without resetting mode states. Chunks from an older bundle do not select that bundle again.",
   120	    "Receiving instructions does not change mode state. The latest known state of the ADHD mode and the unslop mode in this session stays in effect. Once a complete bundle is available, each unknown mode defaults to active.",
   121	    "Precedence. On a direct reply ADHD wins a conflict. Elsewhere unslop wins.",
   122	    "",
   123	  ].join("\n");
   124	}
   125	
   126	export function chunkFooter(index, id, flags) {
   127	  return [
   128	    "",
   129	    `END adhd-unslop chunk ${index} of ${TOTAL_CHUNKS} (${id}). Always-on stops when every opt-in flag is removed (${flags.join(", ")}) or when ADHD_UNSLOP_ALWAYS=0 is set. "normal mode" turns both modes off for this session.`,
   130	    "",
   131	  ].join("\n");
   132	}
   133	
   134	// Assemble and validate one chunk. Returns { ok: true, text } or { ok: false, reason }.
   135	// `root` is the plugin root that contains hooks/chunks/.
   136	export function renderChunk(root, index, { flags, tokenLimit = DEFAULT_TOKEN_LIMIT } = {}) {
   137	  if (!Number.isInteger(index) || index < 1 || index > TOTAL_CHUNKS) {
   138	    return { ok: false, reason: `invalid chunk index ${String(index)}` };
   139	  }
   140	  const dir = path.join(root, "hooks", "chunks");
   141	  let manifest;
   142	  try {
   143	    manifest = JSON.parse(fs.readFileSync(path.join(dir, "manifest.json"), "utf8"));
   144	  } catch {
   145	    return { ok: false, reason: "manifest missing or unreadable" };
   146	  }
   147	  const entry = manifest?.chunks?.[index - 1];
   148	  if (!entry || typeof manifest.compositeSha256 !== "string") {
   149	    return { ok: false, reason: "manifest malformed" };
   150	  }
   151	  let payload;
   152	  try {
   153	    payload = fs.readFileSync(path.join(dir, `${index}.md`), "utf8");
   154	  } catch {
   155	    return { ok: false, reason: `chunk file ${index}.md missing` };
   156	  }
   157	  if (sha256(payload) !== entry.sha256) {
   158	    return { ok: false, reason: `chunk ${index} hash mismatch` };
   159	  }
   160	  const id = bundleId(manifest.compositeSha256);
   161	  const text = chunkHeader(index, id) + payload + chunkFooter(index, id, flags);
   162	  if (text.length > MAX_CHARS) {
   163	    return { ok: false, reason: `chunk ${index} is ${text.length} characters, over ${MAX_CHARS}` };
   164	  }
   165	  const tokens = estimateTokens(text);
   166	  if (tokens > tokenLimit) {
   167	    return { ok: false, reason: `chunk ${index} is about ${tokens} tokens, over ${tokenLimit}` };
   168	  }
   169	  return { ok: true, text, tokens };
   170	}

    89	  const pb = b.split(/[.+-]/).map((n) => Number.parseInt(n, 10) || 0);

    97	// The version a plugin dir declares, from either manifest.
    98	function manifestVersion(dir) {
    99	  for (const m of [".claude-plugin", ".codex-plugin"]) {
   100	    const v = readJson(path.join(dir, m, "plugin.json"))?.version;
   101	    if (typeof v === "string" && v) return v;
   102	  }
   103	  return null;
   104	}

   106	// Load the launcher's helpers from the installed plugin, so the doctor checks
   107	// exactly what the hook runs.

   119	if (!runtime) {

   131	ok(`plugin root: ${root}`);

   139	}[runtime] ?? (isFile(checkoutBuild) ? `node ${shq(checkoutBuild)}` : `reinstall ${id} with your runtime's plugin commands`);
   140	const reinstallThen = runtime ? "start a new session" : null;

   150	// 3. Optional mirrors. Never WARN or FAIL: adhd-unslop does not need them.
   151	function mirrorVersion(name) {
   152	  // Repo checkout: plugins/<name>/ next to plugins/adhd-unslop/.
   153	  const sibling = path.join(root, "..", name);
   154	  const direct = manifestVersion(sibling);
   155	  if (direct) return direct;
   156	  // Installed: <cache>/<marketplace>/<name>/<version>/. Claude Code keeps
   157	  // replaced versions for a while and marks them with .orphaned_at.
   158	  const base = path.join(root, "..", "..", name);
   159	  let entries = [];
   160	  try {
   161	    entries = fs.readdirSync(base, { withFileTypes: true });
   162	  } catch {
   163	    return null;
   164	  }
   165	  const versions = entries
   166	    .filter((e) => e.isDirectory() && !fs.existsSync(path.join(base, e.name, ".orphaned_at")))
   167	    .map((e) => manifestVersion(path.join(base, e.name)))
   168	    .filter(Boolean)
   169	    .sort(compareVersions);
   170	  return versions.at(-1) ?? null;
   171	}
   172	for (const name of MIRRORS) {
   173	  const v = mirrorVersion(name);
   174	  ok(v ? `${name}: installed (${v})` : `${name}: not installed (optional)`);
   175	}

   215	  } else {

   229	// Returns true or false for hooks under [features], or null when unset.
   230	function readFeaturesHooks(file) {
   231	  let text;
   232	  try {
   233	    text = fs.readFileSync(file, "utf8");
   234	  } catch {
   235	    return null;
   236	  }
   237	  let table = "";
   238	  let value = null;
   239	  for (const raw of text.split(/\r?\n/)) {
   240	    const line = raw.replace(/\s+#.*$/, "").replace(/^#.*$/, "").trim();
   241	    if (!line) continue;
   242	    const header = line.match(/^\[\s*([^\[\]]+?)\s*\]$/);
   243	    if (header) {
   244	      table = header[1].replace(/"/g, "");
   245	      continue;
   246	    }
   247	    if (line.startsWith("[")) {
   248	      table = "[array]";
   249	      continue;
   250	    }
   251	    const key = table === "features" ? /^"?hooks"?\s*=\s*(true|false)\b/ : table === "" ? /^"?features"?\s*\.\s*"?hooks"?\s*=\s*(true|false)\b/ : null;
   252	    const m = key && line.match(key);
   253	    if (m) value = m[1] === "true";
   254	    // The inline-table form: features = { hooks = false, ... }
   255	    const inline = table === "" && line.match(/^"?features"?\s*=\s*\{([^}]*)\}/);
   256	    const im = inline && inline[1].match(/(?:^|,)\s*"?hooks"?\s*=\s*(true|false)\b/);
   257	    if (im) value = im[1] === "true";
   258	  }
   259	  return value;
   260	}
