+function runClaude(bin, copy, exp, tmp) {
+  const home = path.join(tmp, "claude-home");
+  const configDir = path.join(tmp, "claude-config");
+  fs.mkdirSync(home, { recursive: true });
+  fs.mkdirSync(configDir, { recursive: true });
+  const env = baseEnv({ HOME: home, USERPROFILE: home, CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR: configDir });
+  const opts = { env, cwd: copy };
+  console.log(`claude: ${cliVersion(bin, env)}`);
+
+  const first = exp.plugins.filter((p) => p.kind === "authored");
+  const second = exp.plugins.filter((p) => p.kind !== "authored");
+  try {
+    for (const target of [".claude-plugin/marketplace.json", ...exp.plugins.map((p) => `plugins/${p.name}`)]) {
+      const r = run(bin, ["plugin", "validate", "--strict", path.join(copy, target)], opts);
+      check(`claude: plugin validate --strict ${target}`, r.ok, () => `${r.problem}\n${tail(r.output)}`);
+    }
+
+    step("claude: plugin marketplace add <copy>", bin, ["plugin", "marketplace", "add", copy], opts);
+    for (const p of first) step(`claude: plugin install ${p.id}`, bin, ["plugin", "install", p.id], opts);
+    checkClaudeInstalled("claude step 1", claudeList(bin, opts, "claude step 1"), first, exp.mkt, configDir);
+
+    for (const p of second) step(`claude: plugin install ${p.id}`, bin, ["plugin", "install", p.id], opts);
+    checkClaudeInstalled("claude step 2", claudeList(bin, opts, "claude step 2"), exp.plugins, exp.mkt, configDir);
+  } catch (err) {
+    if (!(err instanceof Abort)) fail("claude: unexpected error", err.stack ?? err.message);
+  }
+}

+// ---------------------------------------------------------------- Codex app-server
+
+function startAppServer(bin, { cwd, env }) {
+  const child = spawn(bin, ["app-server", "--listen", "stdio://"], { cwd, env, stdio: ["pipe", "pipe", "pipe"] });
+  children.add(child);
+  let stderr = "";
+  let exited = null;
+  let nextId = 0;
+  const pending = new Map();
+  const rejectAll = (err) => {
+    for (const { reject, timer } of pending.values()) {
+      clearTimeout(timer);
+      reject(err);
+    }
+    pending.clear();
+  };
+  // Drain stderr so a full pipe never blocks the server.
+  child.stderr.on("data", (d) => {
+    stderr = (stderr + d).slice(-20_000);
+  });
+  child.stdin.on("error", () => { /* reported through exit */ });
+  child.on("error", (err) => {
+    exited = { error: err };
+    rejectAll(new Error(`app-server failed to start: ${err.message}`));
+  });
+  child.on("exit", (code, signal) => {
+    exited = { code, signal };
+    children.delete(child);
+    rejectAll(new Error(`app-server exited (${code ?? signal})\n${tail(stderr)}`));
+  });
+  // One JSON object per line. Responses carry an id and no method; notifications
+  // and server requests are ignored.
+  readline.createInterface({ input: child.stdout }).on("line", (line) => {
+    line = line.trim();
+    if (!line.startsWith("{")) return;
+    let msg;
+    try { msg = JSON.parse(line); } catch { return; }
+    if (msg.method !== undefined || !pending.has(msg.id)) return;
+    const { resolve, timer } = pending.get(msg.id);
+    pending.delete(msg.id);
+    clearTimeout(timer);
+    resolve(msg);
+  });
+
+  const send = (msg) => child.stdin.write(JSON.stringify({ jsonrpc: "2.0", ...msg }) + "\n");
+  return {
+    request(method, params, timeout = RPC_TIMEOUT_MS) {
+      return new Promise((resolve, reject) => {
+        if (exited) return reject(new Error(`app-server is not running (${JSON.stringify(exited)})\n${tail(stderr)}`));
+        const id = ++nextId;
+        const timer = setTimeout(() => {
+          pending.delete(id);
+          reject(new Error(`${method} timed out after ${timeout / 1000}s\n${tail(stderr)}`));
+        }, timeout);
+        pending.set(id, { resolve, reject, timer });
+        send({ id, method, params });
+      });
+    },
+    notify(method, params) {
+      send(params === undefined ? { method } : { method, params });
+    },
+    async close() {
+      if (exited) return;
+      const done = new Promise((resolve) => child.once("exit", resolve));
+      child.stdin.end();
+      child.kill("SIGTERM");
+      const timer = setTimeout(() => child.kill("SIGKILL"), 3000);
+      await done;
+      clearTimeout(timer);
+    },
+  };
+}
+
+async function rpc(server, label, method, params, what = method) {
+  let msg;
+  try {
+    msg = await server.request(method, params);
+  } catch (err) {
+    fail(`${label}: ${what}`, err.message);
+    throw new Abort(what);
+  }
+  if (!check(`${label}: ${what} succeeds`, !msg.error, () => JSON.stringify(msg.error, null, 2))) throw new Abort(what);
+  return msg.result ?? {};
+}
+
+async function codexCatalog(bin, copy, exp, env, label) {
+  const server = startAppServer(bin, { cwd: copy, env });
+  try {
+    await rpc(server, label, "initialize", {
+      clientInfo: { name: "adhd-unslop-load-check", title: "adhd-unslop load check", version: "0" },
+      capabilities: { experimentalApi: true, requestAttestation: false, optOutNotificationMethods: [] },
+    });
+    server.notify("initialized");
+
+    // plugin/list: one local marketplace with this name, read from the Codex file.
+    const listed = await rpc(server, label, "plugin/list", { cwds: [copy], marketplaceKinds: ["local"] });
+    const loadErrors = listed.marketplaceLoadErrors ?? [];
+    check(`${label}: plugin/list reports no marketplaceLoadErrors`, loadErrors.length === 0, JSON.stringify(loadErrors, null, 2));
+    const ours = (listed.marketplaces ?? []).filter((m) => m.name === exp.mkt);
+    check(`${label}: plugin/list shows exactly one marketplace named ${exp.mkt}`, ours.length === 1, `found ${ours.length}: ${JSON.stringify(ours.map((m) => m.path))}`);
+    const codexMarketplace = path.join(copy, ".agents", "plugins", "marketplace.json");
+    if (ours.length === 1) {
+      check(`${label}: ${exp.mkt} is read from .agents/plugins/marketplace.json`, path.resolve(ours[0].path ?? "") === codexMarketplace, `path: ${ours[0].path}`);
+      const names = (ours[0].plugins ?? []).map((p) => p.name);
+      check(`${label}: ${exp.mkt} lists ${show(exp.plugins.map((p) => p.name))}`, sameSet(names, exp.plugins.map((p) => p.name)), `listed: ${show(names)}`);
+    }
+
+    // plugin/read reads the marketplace entry, installed or not.
+    for (const p of exp.plugins) {
+      let plugin;
+      try {
+        plugin = (await rpc(server, label, "plugin/read", { marketplacePath: codexMarketplace, remoteMarketplaceName: null, pluginName: p.name }, `plugin/read ${p.name}`)).plugin ?? {};
+      } catch (err) {
+        if (err instanceof Abort) continue;
+        throw err;
+      }
+      const skills = (plugin.skills ?? []).map((s) => s.name);
+      check(`${label}: ${p.name} skills are ${show(p.fullSkills)}`, skills.length > 0 && sameSet(skills, p.fullSkills), `read: ${show(skills)}`);
+      const hooks = (plugin.hooks ?? []).map((h) => h.key);
+      check(`${label}: ${p.name} hook keys are ${p.hookKeys.length ? p.hookKeys.map((k) => k.split(":").slice(-2).join(":")).join(" ") : "none"}`, sameSet(hooks, p.hookKeys), `read: ${show(hooks)}\nexpected: ${show(p.hookKeys)}`);
+      const version = plugin.summary?.localVersion;
+      check(`${label}: ${p.name} version ${p.version}`, version === p.version, `localVersion: ${version}`);
+      const displayName = plugin.summary?.interface?.displayName ?? null;
+      check(`${label}: ${p.name} interface.displayName from .codex-plugin`, displayName === p.displayName, `displayName: ${JSON.stringify(displayName)}, expected ${JSON.stringify(p.displayName)}`);
+    }
+
+    // hooks/list reports the installed plugins' hooks, from the cache copy.
+    const hookList = await rpc(server, label, "hooks/list", { cwds: [copy] });
+    const entries = hookList.data ?? [];
+    const problems = entries.flatMap((e) => [...(e.warnings ?? []), ...(e.errors ?? [])]);
+    check(`${label}: hooks/list reports no warnings or errors`, problems.length === 0, JSON.stringify(problems, null, 2));
+    const all = new Map();
+    for (const e of entries) for (const h of e.hooks ?? []) all.set(h.key, h);
+    const listedHooks = [...all.values()].filter((h) => String(h.pluginId ?? "").endsWith(`@${exp.mkt}`));
+    for (const p of exp.plugins) {
+      const mine = listedHooks.filter((h) => h.pluginId === p.id);
+      check(`${label}: hooks/list for ${p.name}: ${p.hookKeys.length ? p.hookKeys.map((k) => k.split(":").slice(-2).join(":")).join(" ") : "none"}`, sameSet(mine.map((h) => h.key), p.hookKeys), `listed: ${show(mine.map((h) => h.key))}\nexpected: ${show(p.hookKeys)}`);
+      if (!mine.length) continue;
+      const suffix = ["plugins", "cache", exp.mkt, p.name, p.version, ...p.hooksFile.split("/")].join(path.sep);
+      const wrong = mine.filter((h) => !path.resolve(h.sourcePath ?? "").endsWith(path.sep + suffix));
+      check(`${label}: hooks/list for ${p.name} reads the ${p.version} cache copy`, wrong.length === 0, wrong.map((h) => `${h.key}: ${h.sourcePath}`).join("\n"));
+      const unhashed = mine.filter((h) => !/^sha256:[0-9a-f]{64}$/.test(h.currentHash ?? ""));
+      check(`${label}: hooks/list for ${p.name} gives each handler a trust hash`, unhashed.length === 0, unhashed.map((h) => `${h.key}: ${h.currentHash}`).join("\n"));
+      console.log(`      trust: ${mine.map((h) => `${h.key.split(":").slice(-2).join(":")}=${h.trustStatus}`).join(" ")}`);
+    }
+  } finally {
+    await server.close();
+  }
+}

+async function runCodex(bin, copy, exp, tmp) {
+  const home = path.join(tmp, "codex-home");
+  const codexHome = path.join(tmp, "codex-config");
+  fs.mkdirSync(home, { recursive: true });
+  fs.mkdirSync(codexHome, { recursive: true });
+  const env = baseEnv({ HOME: home, USERPROFILE: home, CODEX_HOME: codexHome, CODEX_APP_SERVER_DISABLE_MANAGED_CONFIG: "1", RUST_LOG: "warn" });
+  const opts = { env, cwd: copy };
+  console.log(`codex: ${cliVersion(bin, env)}`);
+
+  const cache = path.join(codexHome, "plugins", "cache", exp.mkt);
+  const checkCodexInstalled = (label, installed) => {
+    checkCacheLayout(label, cache, installed);
+    for (const p of installed) {
+      const dir = path.join(cache, p.name, p.version);
+      if (fs.existsSync(dir)) checkInstalledFiles(label, p, dir);
+    }
+  };
+  const first = exp.plugins.filter((p) => p.kind === "authored");
+  const second = exp.plugins.filter((p) => p.kind !== "authored");
+  try {
+    step("codex: plugin marketplace add <copy>", bin, ["plugin", "marketplace", "add", copy], opts);
+    for (const p of first) step(`codex: plugin add ${p.id}`, bin, ["plugin", "add", p.id], opts);
+    checkCodexInstalled("codex step 1", first);
+
+    for (const p of second) step(`codex: plugin add ${p.id}`, bin, ["plugin", "add", p.id], opts);
+    checkCodexInstalled("codex step 2", exp.plugins);
+
+    await codexCatalog(bin, copy, exp, env, "codex catalog");
+  } catch (err) {
+    if (!(err instanceof Abort)) fail("codex: unexpected error", err.stack ?? err.message);
+  }
+}
+
+// ---------------------------------------------------------------- main
+
+async function main() {
+  const opts = parseArgs(process.argv.slice(2));
+  const tmp = makeTempRoot();
+  const copy = path.join(tmp, "marketplace");
+  const count = copyRepo(opts.repo, copy);
+  console.log(`marketplace copy: ${count} files from ${opts.repo}`);
+  const exp = expectations(copy);
+  if (!exp.plugins.length) fail("tools/plugins.json lists plugins", "no plugins found");
+  if (!exp.plugins.some((p) => p.kind === "authored")) fail("tools/plugins.json lists an authored plugin", "step one would install nothing");
+
+  if (opts.only !== "codex") runClaude(opts.claude, copy, exp, tmp);
+  if (opts.only !== "claude") await runCodex(opts.codex, copy, exp, tmp);
+
+  console.log(`\n${passed} passed, ${failed} failed`);
+  process.exitCode = failed ? 1 : 0;
+}
+
+main().catch((err) => {
+  console.error(err.stack ?? err.message);
+  process.exitCode = 1;
+});

### src/adhd-unslop/overlay/00-intro.md
     1	# adhd-unslop
     2	
     3	This skill combines i-have-adhd and unslop:
     4	
     5	- i-have-adhd helps a reader with ADHD act on replies
     6	- unslop removes AI patterns from writing
     7	
     8	Both skills are used unchanged from upstream, and their texts are part of these instructions. The added rules cover:
     9	
    10	1. Where each mode applies
    11	2. Which mode wins when they conflict
    12	3. How to turn each mode off
    13	
    14	Cite rules as:
    15	
    16	- "ADHD rule N", "ADHD exception N", "ADHD check N"
    17	- "unslop rule N", "unslop process N"### src/adhd-unslop/overlay/10-precedence.md
     1	## Scope and precedence
     2	
     3	Follow only active-mode rules and their conditions and exceptions. Rules conflict when following one would violate the other.
     4	
     5	When both modes apply and conflict:
     6	
     7	- ADHD wins for a direct reply
     8	- Unslop wins for other writing
     9	
    10	A rule without a conflict still applies. Example: ADHD has no rule about em dashes or the word `delve`, so unslop rules 13 and 7 apply to direct replies too.
    11	
    12	This file's scope, lifecycle, and precedence sections override conflicting statements in the i-have-adhd and unslop texts.
    13	
    14	Unslop's "Must always apply" instruction applies to every passage you write or edit while unslop mode is active.
    15	
    16	### Classify each passage
    17	
    18	**Direct reply.** This text addresses the current user about their request. It includes:
    19	
    20	- Answers, progress reports, clarifying questions, and status restatements.
    21	- Required tool-call announcements and task or plan tool entries the user reads.
    22	- Commands or snippets offered as the user's next step.
    23	- Your proposed next steps shown for approval before you act.
    24	
    25	**Other writing.** This covers all other text you write or edit:
    26	
    27	- Requested deliverables and their files.
    28	- Code comments and natural-language strings the task permits you to edit.
    29	- Commit messages, PR and issue text, third-party messages, and application copy.
    30	- Subagent instructions, reports between agents, and compaction summaries.
    31	- Text supplied for rewriting, editing, or translation.
    32	
    33	A document drafted in chat remains a deliverable. A requested plan is other writing, even while awaiting approval. Text supplied for rewriting remains editable inside quotation marks.
    34	
    35	Apply these boundary rules:
    36	
    37	- Classify each passage separately. A turn can contain both types. "I wrote docs/links.md" is a direct reply. The file's contents are other writing.
    38	- Code fences, delivery method, and storage do not determine the type. A fenced command for the user's next step is a direct reply. An unfenced README draft is other writing.
    39	- Style edits must preserve syntax, identifiers, paths, URLs, schemas, exact-match data, and verbatim quotations. The task may authorize changes to them. Preserve required output structure. Apply style rules only to editable prose.
    40	- Keep headings and labels in that form. Apply active style rules to their wording without forcing them into sentences.
    41	- Do not add status lines, next-action lines, or estimates to a deliverable only because both modes are active.
    42	
    43	### Outcome table
    44	
    45	This table applies when both modes are active and applicable. It does not override either upstream's exceptions. For a conflict not listed here, use the precedence rule above.
    46	
    47	| Interaction | Direct reply, ADHD wins | Other writing, unslop wins |
    48	| --- | --- | --- |
    49	| 1 Fragments | Allow functional fragments from ADHD's examples for next actions, progress, completion, and errors. Examples include "Step 3 of 5 done: schema updated." and "Cause: missing header. Fix: add it." Otherwise, apply unslop's sentence rules to running prose. | Write running prose in complete sentences with articles and verbs. Do not use colons to connect clauses. |
    50	| 2 Parentheses | Use parentheses only for locators, such as "(lines 42 to 58)" or "(see `auth.ts:42`)". Do not use them for asides. | Rewrite the text as a sentence or a comma clause. |
    51	| 3 Closing question | When work remains, end with one action the reader can finish in under two minutes, such as "Run `npm test` and paste the first failing line." End with one necessary question instead when ADHD, the task, or the runtime requires it. ADHD cases include a separate tangent, real ambiguity, a destructive action, and a debug spiral. Do not request authorization already given. | Remove stock closers. Keep a closing request or action the deliverable requires, such as the decision an email asks for. |
    52	| 4 Estimates | Give an approximate duration when the reader must plan or start. State whose time you are estimating and the main assumption. Use a range when unsure. If you cannot estimate responsibly, say what to check first. | Keep estimates the document needs and state their assumptions. Do not present an estimate as a measurement. |
    53	| 5 State | During multi-step work, state progress each turn in the checklist or one concrete line. Do not repeat the whole plan. | Include status only when it is part of the document's content. |
    54	| 6 Lists | Aim for five items per group. Show every item when completeness matters. | Use as many items as the content needs. Preserve completeness. |
    55	| 7 Tone | Follow ADHD's guidance for replies to the user. | Match the deliverable's audience and intended tone. |
    56	| 8 Announcements | Remove preambles and announcements of intended work unless the runtime requires them. Start with the answer or action. | Not applicable. |
### src/adhd-unslop/overlay/20-lifecycle.md
     1	## Lifecycle
     2	
     3	A mode is a rule set, either ADHD or unslop. Each mode has its own switch. A chunk is one of the three parts delivered by the always-on hook.
     4	
     5	**Activation.** The user activates the skill with `/adhd-unslop` in Claude Code or `$adhd-unslop:adhd-unslop` in Codex. Explicit invocation enables both modes. The always-on hook can also activate the skill at session startup or clear.
     6	
     7	Hook delivery:
     8	
     9	1. Mode defaults initialize only after all three matching chunks are available.
    10	2. An incomplete bundle initializes neither mode.
    11	3. A complete bundle preserves known mode states and defaults each unknown mode to active.
    12	
    13	Switches:
    14	
    15	- "stop adhd mode" disables ADHD and leaves unslop's current state unchanged.
    16	- "stop unslop" disables unslop and leaves ADHD's current state unchanged.
    17	- "normal mode" disables both.
    18	- Invoking the skill again enables both.
    19	
    20	Confirm each change in one line that names which modes are now active. Quoted or discussed control phrases are not commands.
    21	
    22	**State rule.**
    23	
    24	1. Restore the latest known state of each mode in this session.
    25	2. Explicit invocation enables both modes.
    26	3. Stop commands change only the named mode.
    27	4. Receiving or reloading these instructions preserves known states.
    28	5. Once a complete matching bundle is available, each unknown mode defaults to active.
    29	
    30	A newly completed bundle with a different hash replaces the rules without resetting mode states. Repeated chunks from an older bundle do not reactivate that bundle.
    31	
    32	**Persistence.** Active modes stay active for the rest of the session, including across topic changes. If you are unsure whether a mode is still active, treat it as active. The always-on hook also runs on compact, and on resume in Codex, to restore these instructions after context loss.
    33	
    34	**Known limitation.** Mode state exists only in the conversation. Compaction or resume can lose it. Reinjection restores the instructions without recovering lost state, so it may restore the active defaults. A stop command may need repeating.
    35	
    36	**Runtime precedence.** The runtime's system prompt and the user's direct instructions outrank both modes. ADHD exception 6 states this for ADHD. The same precedence applies to unslop.
### src/adhd-unslop/overlay/90-final-check.md
     1	## Final check
     2	
     3	Before sending, complete these checks in order. Apply only the checks for active modes.
     4	
     5	1. Classify each passage as a direct reply or other writing.
     6	2. If unslop mode is active, run unslop process 1 and 2 on every passage. In direct replies, preserve any functional fragment, locator parenthesis, next-action line, or status line the active ADHD rules require. Follow the outcome table.
     7	3. If ADHD mode is active, run ADHD checks 1 to 5 on direct replies only. Then verify each direct reply's first and last lines as ADHD requires.
     8	4. Confirm you added no session bookkeeping to other writing.
     9	5. Confirm applying this file did not override any upstream exception.
    10	
    11	These checks do not replace the upstream processes they call for. Both upstream texts are part of these instructions.

     9	Run the doctor script that ships in this skill's folder. It only reads files and changes nothing.
    10	
    11	- In Claude Code, run `node "${CLAUDE_SKILL_DIR}/scripts/doctor.mjs"`.
    12	- In Codex, run `node "<dir>/scripts/doctor.mjs"`, where `<dir>` is the absolute path of the folder that holds this `SKILL.md`.
    13	
    14	Run only that path, and never search the disk for another copy of the script.
    15	
    16	The script prints one line per check, starting with `OK`, `WARN`, or `FAIL`. Each `WARN` or `FAIL` line has a `fix:` line under it, and sometimes a `then:` line. A `fix:` line holds either one shell command or one instruction. A `then:` line is a step for the user after the fix. The script exits with code 1 when a check fails. That exit code is the expected result for a broken install, not a problem with the script, so do not debug the script.
    17	
    18	## Report and fixes
    19	
    20	1. Show the user the full output in a code block, unchanged.
    21	2. If there are no `WARN` or `FAIL` lines, say the install looks healthy and stop.
    22	3. Otherwise, go through the fixes one at a time. For a `fix:` line that is a shell command, show it exactly as printed and ask the user. Run it only after the user says yes. For an instruction, show it to the user instead of acting on it. Then show any `then:` line, and move to the next fix.
    23	
    24	Never run a fix without asking, and never change anything the output does not name.
     1	# adhd-unslop
     2	
     3	This repo is a plugin marketplace for Claude Code and Codex. Its main plugin
     4	combines [i-have-adhd](https://github.com/ayghri/i-have-adhd) and pstack's
     5	[unslop](https://github.com/michael-denyer/pstack-claude) with one
     6	tie-breaker.
     7	
     8	| Plugin | Skills | What it is |
     9	| --- | --- | --- |
    10	| `adhd-unslop` | `adhd-unslop`, `doctor` | The overlay rules plus both upstream texts, an always-on hook, and a doctor. Everything you need. |
    11	| `au-i-have-adhd` | `i-have-adhd` | Optional. A pinned, unchanged copy of ayghri/i-have-adhd |
    12	| `au-unslop` | `unslop` | Optional. A pinned, unchanged copy of the unslop skill from pstack-claude |
    13	
    14	All upstream text comes from copies pinned by commit and sha256 in
    15	`tools/upstream.json`. The `au-` prefix keeps the mirrors from clashing with
    16	the upstream plugins of the same name.
    17	
    18	## The rule
    19	
    20	Both rule sets stay active. When a rule from each would produce different text
    21	for the same passage:
    22	
    23	- In a direct reply to the user, i-have-adhd wins.
    24	- In all other writing, unslop wins. This includes files, docs, commit
    25	  messages, PR text, subagent prompts, and text you were asked to rewrite.
    26	
    27	Compatible rules apply everywhere. The skill defines both surfaces per
    28	passage, lists the known interactions in an outcome table, and adds
    29	independent off switches. The overlay text is in `src/adhd-unslop/overlay/`.
    30	
    31	## Install
    32	
    33	### Claude Code
    34	
    35	```bash
    36	claude plugin marketplace add rubenvarela/adhd-unslop
    37	claude plugin install adhd-unslop@adhd-unslop
    38	```
    39	
    40	Type `/adhd-unslop` in a session. If another command uses that name, type
    41	`/adhd-unslop:adhd-unslop`. The skill carries both upstream texts itself. It
    42	has `disable-model-invocation: true`, so nothing applies until you invoke it
    43	or turn on always-on mode.
    44	
    45	### Codex
    46	
    47	```bash
    48	codex plugin marketplace add rubenvarela/adhd-unslop --ref main
    49	codex plugin add adhd-unslop@adhd-unslop
    50	```
    51	
    52	Type `$adhd-unslop:adhd-unslop` in a session. Codex matches plugin skills by
    53	their full name, so a bare `$adhd-unslop` finds nothing.
    54	
    55	Do not link the skill into `~/.agents/skills`. Codex names a linked skill
    56	after the plugin that contains it, so the link becomes a second
    57	`adhd-unslop:adhd-unslop`, and with two skills of one name Codex loads
    58	neither. The doctor warns about such a link.
    59	
    60	### The optional mirrors
    61	
    62	Install `au-i-have-adhd` or `au-unslop` only if you want that skill on its
    63	own. `adhd-unslop` never needs them.
    64	
    65	```bash
    66	claude plugin install au-i-have-adhd@adhd-unslop     # then /au-i-have-adhd:i-have-adhd
    67	codex plugin add au-unslop@adhd-unslop               # then $au-unslop:unslop
    68	```
    69	
    70	They behave exactly as upstream ships them: i-have-adhd runs only when you
    71	type it, and unslop can also be chosen by the model. With the unslop mirror
    72	installed, Codex sometimes loads it on its own. That copy is separate from
    73	`adhd-unslop`, so `stop unslop` does not turn it off. If you use
    74	`adhd-unslop`, you do not need the unslop mirror.
    75	
    76	## Update
    77	
    78	Each plugin updates on its own.
    79	
    80	```bash
    81	claude plugin marketplace update adhd-unslop
    82	claude plugin update adhd-unslop@adhd-unslop
    83	
    84	codex plugin marketplace upgrade adhd-unslop
    85	codex plugin add adhd-unslop@adhd-unslop
    86	```
    87	
    88	Update a mirror the same way if you installed one.
    89	
    90	### From 0.2.x
    91	
    92	0.2.x installed the two mirrors as dependencies of `adhd-unslop`. 0.3.0 does
    93	not need them.
    94	
    95	- Claude Code: run the update commands above, then `claude plugin prune` to
    96	  remove the mirrors that 0.2.x installed for you. A mirror you installed by
    97	  name stays; update it with `claude plugin update au-unslop@adhd-unslop` or
    98	  `claude plugin update au-i-have-adhd@adhd-unslop`.
    99	- Codex: run the update commands above. Your hook trust carries over, because
   100	  the hook definitions did not change. Remove the mirrors with `codex plugin
   101	  remove au-i-have-adhd@adhd-unslop` and `codex plugin remove
   102	  au-unslop@adhd-unslop` if you installed them only for `adhd-unslop`.
   103	
   104	## Always-on mode
   105	
   106	Create a flag file to deliver the rules at session start without invoking
   107	the skill:
   108	
   109	```bash
   110	touch ~/.claude/.adhd-unslop-always      # or "$CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR/.adhd-unslop-always"
   111	touch ~/.codex/.adhd-unslop-always       # or "$CODEX_HOME/.adhd-unslop-always"
   112	```
   113	
   114	Either flag turns always-on on in both runtimes. Remove every flag to stop.
   115	
   116	`ADHD_UNSLOP_ALWAYS` overrides the flags for one process, which helps in CI
   117	and scripted runs:
   118	
   119	- `ADHD_UNSLOP_ALWAYS=0`, `false`, or `off` turns it off even when a flag
   120	  exists.
   121	- `ADHD_UNSLOP_ALWAYS=1`, `true`, or `on` turns it on without a flag.
   122	- Any other value is ignored, and the doctor warns about it.
   123	
   124	Codex runs plugin hooks only after you review and trust them:
   125	
   126	1. Open `/hooks` in an interactive Codex session.
   127	2. Trust the `adhd-unslop` handlers.
   128	3. Restart.
   129	
   130	### When the rules arrive
   131	
   132	The hook runs at `startup`, `clear`, `compact`, and `resume`.
   133	
   134	- Claude Code keeps the earlier copy in a resumed session, so the hook adds
   135	  nothing on resume. If you turn always-on on in the middle of a session,
   136	  start a new session to get the rules.
   137	- Codex also keeps the earlier copy, but it can lose it: after a manual
   138	  compaction, Codex fires the hook only when your next message starts. If
   139	  you compact and quit before sending a message, the resumed session would
   140	  have no copy. So the hook injects on every Codex resume, which can leave a
   141	  second copy in context.
   142	- If the rules ever seem missing, invoke `/adhd-unslop` or
   143	  `$adhd-unslop:adhd-unslop`, or run the doctor. Invoking it while
   144	  always-on already delivered the rules adds a second, identical copy, and
   145	  turns both modes back on, including one you had stopped.
   146	
   147	### How the always-on hook works
   148	
   149	The hook carries its own copy of both upstream texts, so it works without the
   150	mirrors and without the model reading any file first.
   151	
   152	Claude Code caps each hook's output at 10,000 characters, and Codex allows
   153	about 2,500 tokens per handler by default. The rules are about 21,500
   154	characters, so the hook delivers them as three chunks from three handlers
   155	under one matcher:
   156	
   157	1. Scope, surfaces, precedence, and lifecycle.
   158	2. The i-have-adhd body, verbatim.
   159	3. The unslop body, verbatim, plus the final check.
   160	
   161	Every chunk has the same header, with its index and the first 12
   162	hexadecimal characters of the bundle's SHA-256. The header states that a
   163	bundle counts only when all three chunks with that id arrive, each with its
   164	END line, and that arriving instructions do not change mode state.
   165	
   166	Each handler sets `additionalContextLimit: 5000` for Codex. The launcher
   167	checks each chunk hash against `hooks/chunks/manifest.json` and checks the
   168	assembled size against both caps before printing. With always-on on and a
   169	broken install, it prints one JSON `systemMessage` with no context. With
   170	always-on off, it prints nothing.
   171	
   172	## Doctor
   173	
   174	Type `/adhd-unslop:doctor` or `$adhd-unslop:doctor`. It prints one OK, WARN,
   175	or FAIL line per check, with the fix for each problem, and changes nothing.
   176	It checks the install, the optional mirrors, the always-on flags and switch,
   177	the hook chunks, the Codex hooks feature, and a `~/.agents/skills` name
   178	clash. You can also run it directly:
   179	
   180	```bash
   181	node ~/.claude/plugins/cache/adhd-unslop/adhd-unslop/<version>/skills/doctor/scripts/doctor.mjs
   182	```
   183	
   184	## Switches
   185	
   186	- `stop adhd mode` turns the ADHD rules off. unslop stays as it was.
   187	- `stop unslop` turns the unslop rules off. ADHD stays as it was.
   188	- `normal mode` turns both off.
   189	- Invoking the skill again turns both on.
   190	
   191	Known limitations:
   192	
   193	- Mode state lives in the conversation. Compaction can lose it, and the
   194	  re-injected instructions then restore the active defaults. Repeat the stop
   195	  command if that happens.
   196	- Without always-on, Claude Code keeps an invoked skill through `/compact`
   197	  only up to 20,000 characters, and this skill is about 21,800, so the last
   198	  unslop rules and the final check drop out. After a resume and a compaction
   199	  it keeps none of it. For long sessions that compact, turn on always-on,
   200	  which delivers the whole rule set again at every compaction, or invoke the
   201	  skill again after compacting.
   202	
   203	## Upstream updates
   204	
   205	The `Bump upstream skills` workflow runs daily. It first runs
   206	`node tools/sync.mjs --verify-remote`, which refetches each pinned file and
   207	compares its hash. Then `node tools/sync.mjs --latest`:
   208	
   209	1. Finds the newest upstream commit that touched a pinned file.
   210	2. Skips an upstream when that commit changed none of the pinned files.
   211	3. Fetches the files and refuses a body that references files the plugins
   212	   do not ship, such as `references/`, `scripts/`, or relative links.
   213	4. Refuses a body that drops a rule, exception, check, or process step the
   214	   overlay cites.
   215	5. Swaps the files in, raises the patch version of each plugin that ships
   216	   the text, rebuilds, and runs the tests. It restores everything if a step
   217	   fails.
   218	
   219	The workflow opens or updates one PR with the results and starts the verify
   220	workflow on it. When a bump fails, it opens an issue with the reason. The
   221	usual cause is an upstream change to a rule the overlay cites, which needs an
   222	overlay edit. It needs the repository setting "Allow GitHub Actions to create
   223	and approve pull requests".
   224	
   225	To bump by hand:
   226	
   227	```bash
   228	node tools/sync.mjs --check                        # upstream/ matches the pins
   229	node tools/sync.mjs --bump i-have-adhd <commit>    # or: --bump unslop <commit>
   230	git diff
   231	```
   232	
   233	Review the upstream diff for conflicts with the other skill. Record them in
   234	the outcome table in `src/adhd-unslop/overlay/10-precedence.md`.
   235	
   236	## Editing
   237	
   238	Edit only `src/`, `tools/plugins.json`, and `tools/upstream.json`. Then:
   239	
   240	```bash
   241	node tools/build.mjs
   242	node --test tests/*.test.mjs
   243	```
   244	
   245	`node tools/build.mjs` generates everything under `plugins/` and both
   246	marketplace files. `node tools/build.mjs --check` fails when a generated file
   247	is stale or when a stray file sits under a generated folder, and
   248	`node tools/build.mjs --prune` deletes strays. Raise a plugin's version in
   249	`tools/plugins.json` whenever its shipped files change. CI enforces this.
   250	
   251	To add a plugin that uses i-have-adhd:
   252	
   253	1. Add an entry to `tools/plugins.json` with `"kind": "authored"` and
   254	   `"skills": { "<skill>": { "upstreams": ["i-have-adhd"] } }`.
   255	2. Write `src/<plugin>/skills/<skill>/SKILL.md.tmpl` with a line
   256	   `{{upstream i-have-adhd}}` where the rules belong, and
   257	   `agents/openai.yaml` for its Codex policy. The build puts the pinned
   258	   i-have-adhd text in place of that line.
   259	3. Build and test. Give the plugin no always-on hook of its own, or it would
   260	   inject the ADHD rules a second time.
   261	
   262	## Checks
   263	
   264	- `verify.yml` runs on every pull request and push to `main`: the pin check,
   265	  the generated-file check, the unit tests, a version gate on pull requests,
   266	  a keyless load check that installs the plugins into pinned Claude Code and
   267	  Codex versions, and workflow linting.
   268	- `cli-drift.yml` runs the load check daily against the latest CLI releases.
   269	  It opens an issue when that fails, and a PR that raises the pins in
   270	  `tools/cli-versions.json` when newer releases pass.
   271	- `tests/e2e/run.sh` drives the real models in throwaway homes. It needs both
   272	  CLIs signed in, so it runs locally. `tests/e2e/run.sh migrate` checks the
   273	  upgrade from 0.2.2 in both runtimes. `E2E_REPO=<owner/repo>
   274	  E2E_REF=<branch>` installs from GitHub.
   275	
   276	## Layout
   277	
   278	```
   279	.claude-plugin/marketplace.json     GENERATED Claude Code marketplace
   280	.agents/plugins/marketplace.json    GENERATED Codex marketplace
   281	plugins/                            GENERATED, every file
   282	  adhd-unslop/                      overlay skill, doctor, always-on hook
   283	  au-i-have-adhd/                   pinned copy of i-have-adhd
   284	  au-unslop/                        pinned copy of unslop
   285	src/adhd-unslop/                    hand-written sources
   286	  overlay/                          overlay sections
   287	  skills/                           skill templates, doctor, Codex metadata
   288	  hooks/                            hooks.json, launcher, shared helpers
   289	upstream/                           upstream files at the pinned commits
   290	tools/                              build.mjs, sync.mjs, load-check.mjs, version-gate.mjs,
   291	                                    plugins.json, upstream.json, cli-versions.json
   292	tests/                              node:test suite, fixtures, and tests/e2e/
   293	design/DECISIONS.md                 decisions, reasons, and verified platform facts
   294	design/                             plans, research, review rounds, and test runs
   295	AGENTS.md                           rules for agents; Claude Code and Codex both read it
   296	```

     1	# Notice
     2	
     3	This marketplace ships two upstream works.
     4	
     5	- The `au-i-have-adhd` and `au-unslop` plugins each carry one upstream
     6	  `SKILL.md`, unchanged.
     7	- The `adhd-unslop` plugin carries both upstream bodies, unchanged after
     8	  removing their YAML frontmatter, in its skill and in its always-on hook
     9	  chunks.
    10	
    11	Each plugin ships the MIT license texts it needs in `LICENSES/` and lists
    12	them in its `NOTICE.md`. `upstream/<name>/LICENSE` holds the originals.
    13	Pinned commits live in `tools/upstream.json`.
    14	
    15	| Upstream | Author | Repository | File | Shipped in |
    16	| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
    17	| i-have-adhd | Ayoub Ghriss | https://github.com/ayghri/i-have-adhd | skills/i-have-adhd/SKILL.md | `au-i-have-adhd`, `adhd-unslop` |
    18	| unslop (pstack-claude) | Michael Denyer's port of Lauren Tan's pstack | https://github.com/michael-denyer/pstack-claude | plugins/pstack/skills/unslop/SKILL.md | `au-unslop`, `adhd-unslop` |
    19	
    20	The overlay text and sources in `src/`, the tooling in `tools/`, and the
    21	tests are original to this repository and are MIT licensed (see `LICENSE`).

    71	// A turn/completed counts only for turnId: Codex can send the compaction

    73	function settled(threadId, doneMethods, turnId = () => null) {

    41	
    42	const waiting = new Map();
    43	let buffer = "";
    44	server.stdout.setEncoding("utf8");
    45	server.stdout.on("data", (chunk) => {
    46	  buffer += chunk;
    47	  let nl;
    48	  while ((nl = buffer.indexOf("\n")) >= 0) {
    49	    const line = buffer.slice(0, nl).trim();
    50	    buffer = buffer.slice(nl + 1);
    51	    if (!line.startsWith("{")) continue;
    52	    let msg;
    53	    try {
    54	      msg = JSON.parse(line);
    55	    } catch {
    56	      continue;
    57	    }
    58	    if (msg.id !== undefined && waiting.has(msg.id)) {
    59	      waiting.get(msg.id)(msg);
    60	      waiting.delete(msg.id);
    61	    }
    62	  }
    63	});
    64	
    65	let nextId = 0;
    66	function request(method, params, timeoutMs = 60000) {
    67	  const id = ++nextId;
    68	  return new Promise((resolve, reject) => {
    69	    const timer = setTimeout(() => reject(new Error(`${method} timed out`)), timeoutMs);
    70	    waiting.set(id, (msg) => {
    71	      clearTimeout(timer);
    72	      if (msg.error) reject(new Error(`${method}: ${JSON.stringify(msg.error)}`));
    73	      else resolve(msg.result);
    74	    });
    75	    server.stdin.write(JSON.stringify({ jsonrpc: "2.0", id, method, params }) + "\n");
    76	  });
    77	}
    78	
    79	function notify(method) {
    80	  server.stdin.write(JSON.stringify({ jsonrpc: "2.0", method }) + "\n");
    81	}

    83	async function listHooks() {
    84	  await request("initialize", {
    85	    clientInfo: { name: "adhd-unslop-e2e", title: "adhd-unslop e2e", version: "0" },
    86	    capabilities: { experimentalApi: true, requestAttestation: false, optOutNotificationMethods: [] },
    87	  });
    88	  notify("initialized");
    89	  const result = await request("hooks/list", { cwds: [cwd] });
    90	  const hooks = [];
    91	  for (const entry of result?.data ?? []) {
    92	    for (const e of entry.errors ?? []) console.error(`hooks/list error: ${JSON.stringify(e)}`);
    93	    for (const h of entry.hooks ?? []) hooks.push(h);
    94	  }
    95	  return hooks;
    96	}
    97	
    98	let code = 0;
    99	try {
   100	  const hooks = await listHooks();
   101	  if (mode === "list") {
   102	    for (const h of hooks) {
   103	      const { key, pluginId: id, trustStatus, currentHash, sourcePath } = h;
   104	      console.log(JSON.stringify({ key, pluginId: id, trustStatus, currentHash, sourcePath }));
   105	    }
   106	  } else {
   107	    const configPath = path.join(codexHome, "config.toml");
   108	    const existing = fs.existsSync(configPath) ? fs.readFileSync(configPath, "utf8") : "";
   109	    let written = 0;
   110	    let text = "";
   111	    for (const h of hooks.filter((x) => x.pluginId === pluginId)) {
   112	      if (!h.key || !h.currentHash) continue;
   113	      if (existing.includes(`[hooks.state."${h.key}"]`)) continue;
   114	      text += `\n[hooks.state."${h.key}"]\ntrusted_hash = "${h.currentHash}"\n`;
   115	      written++;
   116	    }
   117	    if (text) fs.appendFileSync(configPath, text);
   118	    console.log(written);
   119	  }
   120	} catch (err) {
   121	  console.error(`codex-hooks.mjs: ${err.message}`);
   122	  if (stderr) console.error(stderr.slice(-2000));
   123	  code = 1;
   124	} finally {
   125	  server.stdin.end();
   126	  server.kill("SIGTERM");
   127	  const killer = setTimeout(() => server.kill("SIGKILL"), 3000);
   128	  server.on("exit", () => {
   129	    clearTimeout(killer);
   130	    process.exit(code);
   131	  });
   132	}
     1	// Runs several turns in one Claude Code print-mode process for
     2	// tests/e2e/run.sh, so state held in memory, such as which skills were
     3	// invoked, survives from turn to turn. Each prompt is sent as a stream-json
     4	// user message after the previous turn's result event. Slash commands such as
     5	// /compact work as prompts.
     6	//
     7	//   node tests/e2e/claude-turns.mjs <claude-bin> <log> <prompt>...
     8	//
     9	// Runs in the current directory with the caller's environment. Writes every
    10	// stdout and stderr line to <log>. Exits 1 when the process ends before the
    11	// last result or a turn takes longer than 5 minutes.
    12	
    13	import { spawn } from "node:child_process";
    14	import fs from "node:fs";
    15	
    16	const [claude, log, ...prompts] = process.argv.slice(2);
    17	if (!claude || !log || !prompts.length) {
    18	  console.error("usage: claude-turns.mjs <claude-bin> <log> <prompt>...");
    19	  process.exit(2);
    20	}
    21	
    22	const out = fs.createWriteStream(log);
    23	const child = spawn(
    24	  claude,
    25	  ["-p", "--input-format", "stream-json", "--output-format", "stream-json", "--verbose", "--include-hook-events"],
    26	  { stdio: ["pipe", "pipe", "pipe"] },
    27	);
    28	child.stderr.on("data", (d) => out.write(d));
    29	
    30	let next = 0;
    31	let timer;
    32	function send() {
    33	  clearTimeout(timer);
    34	  if (next >= prompts.length) {
    35	    child.stdin.end();
    36	    return;
    37	  }
    38	  const content = prompts[next++];
    39	  child.stdin.write(JSON.stringify({ type: "user", message: { role: "user", content } }) + "\n");
    40	  timer = setTimeout(() => {
    41	    out.write(`claude-turns.mjs: turn ${next} timed out\n`);
    42	    child.kill("SIGTERM");
    43	  }, 300000);
    44	}
    45	
    46	let buffer = "";
    47	let results = 0;
    48	child.stdout.setEncoding("utf8");
    49	child.stdout.on("data", (chunk) => {
    50	  out.write(chunk);
    51	  buffer += chunk;
    52	  let nl;
    53	  while ((nl = buffer.indexOf("\n")) >= 0) {
    54	    const line = buffer.slice(0, nl);
    55	    buffer = buffer.slice(nl + 1);
    56	    if (!line.startsWith("{")) continue;
    57	    try {
    58	      if (JSON.parse(line).type === "result") {
    59	        results++;
    60	        send();
    61	      }
    62	    } catch {
    63	      // Not JSON; already logged.
    64	    }
    65	  }
    66	});
    67	
    68	child.on("exit", (code) => {
    69	  clearTimeout(timer);
    70	  out.end(() => process.exit(results >= prompts.length ? 0 : code || 1));
    71	});

     1	// Parsers for tests/e2e/run.sh. Each subcommand reads one log or transcript
     2	// and prints what it found. Assertion subcommands exit 1 on failure.
     3	//
     4	//   bundle <claude|codex> <file> <bundle-id> <exact|atleast|none> [after-compact]
     5	//     Counts each chunk's END line in the context records only: SessionStart
     6	//     attachments in a Claude Code transcript (attachment.content), developer
     7	//     messages in a Codex rollout. A Claude record also repeats the text in
     8	//     stdout and rendered, so a plain grep would count every copy three times.
     9	//     exact: each chunk once with <bundle-id>, and no END line from another
    10	//     bundle. atleast: each chunk at least once with <bundle-id>. none: no END
    11	//     line at all. after-compact counts only the context after the last
    12	//     compaction: Claude Code records after the last compact_boundary, and
    13	//     for Codex the replacement_history of the last compacted record plus
    14	//     the developer messages after it. It fails when nothing was compacted.
    15	//   skill-arrived <claude|codex> <file> <SKILL.md> <final-line> [whole]
    16	//     One context record holds the skill text: the Claude Code skill message
    17	//     or tool result in a transcript, the injected skill message in a Codex
    18	//     rollout. It must carry both "<!-- BEGIN upstream" lines and <final-line>.
    19	//     With "whole", it must also hold the SKILL.md body, everything after the
    20	//     frontmatter, byte for byte.
    21	//   compacted <transcript> <skill-name> <final-line>
    22	//     After the last compact boundary of a Claude Code transcript, reports the
    23	//     invoked_skills attachment for <skill-name>: its size, whether it was cut,
    24	//     and whether it still holds <final-line>. Exits 0 only when it does.
    25	//   no-skill <stream.jsonl>
    26	//     No Skill tool call and no Read of a SKILL.md or references/ file.
    27	//   session <stream.jsonl>
    28	//     Prints the Claude Code session id.
    29	//   plugins <claude|codex> <list.json>
    30	//     Prints "id version" for each installed plugin, from `plugin list --json`.
    31	//     Claude Code lines add the install path.
    32	//   hooks-trusted <hooks.jsonl> <plugin-id> <version> <key>...
    33	//     Every hook of <plugin-id> in `codex-hooks.mjs list` output is trusted,
    34	//     comes from the <version> cache folder, and the keys are exactly <key>...
    35	
    36	import fs from "node:fs";
    37	
    38	const END = /END adhd-unslop chunk (\d) of 3 \(([0-9a-f]+)\)/g;
    39	
    40	function jsonLines(file) {
    41	  const out = [];
    42	  for (const line of fs.readFileSync(file, "utf8").split("\n")) {
    43	    if (!line.startsWith("{")) continue;
    44	    try {
    45	      out.push(JSON.parse(line));
    46	    } catch {
    47	      // Skip non-JSON lines such as CLI warnings.
    48	    }
    49	  }
    50	  return out;
    51	}
    52	
    53	function texts(value) {
    54	  if (typeof value === "string") return [value];
    55	  if (Array.isArray(value)) return value.flatMap(texts);
    56	  if (value && typeof value === "object") {
    57	    if (typeof value.text === "string") return [value.text];
    58	    if ("content" in value) return texts(value.content);
    59	  }
    60	  return [];
    61	}
    62	
    63	function contextTexts(kind, file, scope) {
    64	  let records = jsonLines(file);
    65	  const afterCompact = scope === "after-compact";
    66	  if (kind === "claude") {
    67	    if (afterCompact) {
    68	      const last = records.findLastIndex((r) => r.type === "system" && r.subtype === "compact_boundary");
    69	      if (last < 0) throw new Error("no compact_boundary in the transcript");
    70	      records = records.slice(last + 1);
    71	    }
    72	    return records
    73	      .filter((r) => r.type === "attachment" && r.attachment?.hookEvent === "SessionStart")
    74	      .map((r) => texts(r.attachment.content).join("\n"));
    75	  }
    76	  if (kind === "codex") {
    77	    const developer = (item) => item?.type === "message" && item?.role === "developer";
    78	    let kept = [];
    79	    if (afterCompact) {
    80	      const last = records.findLastIndex((r) => r.type === "compacted");
    81	      if (last < 0) throw new Error("no compacted record in the rollout");
    82	      kept = (records[last].payload?.replacement_history ?? []).filter(developer).map((i) => texts(i.content).join("\n"));
    83	      records = records.slice(last + 1);
    84	    }
    85	    return kept.concat(
    86	      records.filter((r) => r.type === "response_item" && developer(r.payload)).map((r) => texts(r.payload.content).join("\n")),
    87	    );
    88	  }
    89	  throw new Error(`unknown runtime ${kind}`);
    90	}
    91	
    92	function bundle(kind, file, id, mode, scope) {
    93	  const counts = { 1: 0, 2: 0, 3: 0 };
    94	  const others = [];
    95	  for (const text of contextTexts(kind, file, scope)) {
    96	    for (const m of text.matchAll(END)) {
    97	      if (m[2] === id && counts[m[1]] !== undefined) counts[m[1]]++;
    98	      else others.push(`chunk ${m[1]} (${m[2]})`);
    99	    }
   100	  }
   101	  const summary = `chunk 1: ${counts[1]}, chunk 2: ${counts[2]}, chunk 3: ${counts[3]} with ${id}; other END lines: ${others.length ? others.join(", ") : "none"}`;
   102	  const all = [1, 2, 3].map((i) => counts[i]);
   103	  let ok;
   104	  if (mode === "exact") ok = all.every((n) => n === 1) && others.length === 0;
   105	  else if (mode === "atleast") ok = all.every((n) => n >= 1);
   106	  else if (mode === "none") ok = all.every((n) => n === 0) && others.length === 0;
   107	  else throw new Error(`unknown mode ${mode}`);
   108	  console.log(summary);
   109	  return ok;
   110	}
   111	
   112	function toolUses(records) {
   113	  const uses = [];
   114	  for (const r of records) {
   115	    if (r.type !== "assistant") continue;
   116	    for (const c of r.message?.content ?? []) if (c.type === "tool_use") uses.push(c);
   117	  }
   118	  return uses;
   119	}
   120	
   121	const BEGIN_MARKERS = ["<!-- BEGIN upstream i-have-adhd", "<!-- BEGIN upstream unslop"];
   122	
   123	function skillRecords(kind, file) {
   124	  const records = jsonLines(file);
   125	  if (kind === "claude") {
   126	    const out = [];
   127	    for (const r of records) {
   128	      if (r.type === "user" && r.message) out.push({ where: r.isMeta ? "skill message" : "user message", text: texts(r.message.content).join("\n") });
   129	      if (r.type === "attachment" && r.attachment && r.attachment.type !== "prompt_snapshot")
   130	        out.push({ where: `${r.attachment.type} attachment`, text: texts(r.attachment.content ?? r.attachment.skills).join("\n") });
   131	    }
   132	    return out;
   133	  }
   134	  if (kind === "codex") {
   135	    return records
   136	      .filter((r) => r.type === "response_item" && r.payload?.type === "message")
   137	      .map((r) => ({ where: `${r.payload.role} message`, text: texts(r.payload.content).join("\n") }));
   138	  }
   139	  throw new Error(`unknown runtime ${kind}`);
   140	}
   141	
   142	function skillArrived(kind, file, skillPath, finalLine, whole) {
   143	  const markers = [...BEGIN_MARKERS, finalLine];
   144	  const records = skillRecords(kind, file);
   145	  const hit = records.find((r) => markers.every((m) => r.text.includes(m)));
   146	  if (!hit) {
   147	    const best = records
   148	      .map((r) => ({ r, n: markers.filter((m) => r.text.includes(m)).length }))
   149	      .sort((a, b) => b.n - a.n)[0];
   150	    const found = best ? markers.filter((m) => best.r.text.includes(m)) : [];
   151	    console.log(`no record holds all three markers; best: ${best ? `${best.r.where}, ${best.r.text.length} chars, with ${found.join(" | ") || "none"}` : "no records"}`);
   152	    return false;
   153	  }
   154	  if (whole !== "whole") {
   155	    console.log(`${hit.where}, ${hit.text.length} chars`);
   156	    return true;
   157	  }
   158	  const body = fs.readFileSync(skillPath, "utf8").replace(/^---\r?\n[\s\S]*?\r?\n---\r?\n/, "");
   159	  if (hit.text.includes(body)) {
   160	    console.log(`${hit.where} holds all ${body.length} characters of the SKILL.md body`);
   161	    return true;
   162	  }
   163	  let n = 0;
   164	  while (n < body.length && hit.text.includes(body.slice(0, n + 1))) n = Math.min(body.length, n + 256);
   165	  console.log(`${hit.where} (${hit.text.length} chars) lacks part of the ${body.length}-character SKILL.md body; the first ${Math.max(0, n - 256)} characters match`);
   166	  return false;
   167	}
   168	
   169	function compacted(file, skillName, finalLine) {
   170	  const records = jsonLines(file);
   171	  let boundary = -1;
   172	  records.forEach((r, i) => {
   173	    if (r.type === "system" && r.subtype === "compact_boundary") boundary = i;
   174	  });
   175	  if (boundary < 0) {
   176	    console.log("no compact boundary in the transcript");
   177	    return false;
   178	  }
   179	  const meta = records[boundary].compactMetadata ?? {};
   180	  const after = records.slice(boundary + 1);
   181	  const skills = after
   182	    .filter((r) => r.type === "attachment" && r.attachment?.type === "invoked_skills")
   183	    .flatMap((r) => r.attachment.skills ?? [])
   184	    .filter((s) => s.name === skillName);
   185	  const tokens = `${meta.preTokens ?? "?"} to ${meta.postTokens ?? "?"} tokens`;
   186	  if (!skills.length) {
   187	    console.log(`${meta.trigger ?? "?"} compaction, ${tokens}; no ${skillName} in an invoked_skills attachment after it`);
   188	    return false;
   189	  }
   190	  const text = texts(skills[skills.length - 1].content).join("\n");
   191	  const cut = text.includes("truncated for compaction");
   192	  const has = text.includes(finalLine);
   193	  const kept = BEGIN_MARKERS.filter((m) => text.includes(m)).map((m) => m.replace("<!-- BEGIN upstream ", ""));
   194	  console.log(
   195	    `${meta.trigger ?? "?"} compaction, ${tokens}; ${skillName} re-attached with ${text.length} chars${cut ? ", cut for compaction" : ""}; begins kept: ${kept.join(", ") || "none"}; final check line ${has ? "present" : "missing"}`,
   196	  );
   197	  return has;
   198	}
   199	
   200	function noSkill(file) {
   201	  const bad = toolUses(jsonLines(file)).filter(
   202	    (u) => u.name === "Skill" || (u.name === "Read" && /(SKILL\.md|\/references\/)/.test(String(u.input?.file_path ?? ""))),
   203	  );
   204	  for (const u of bad) console.log(`${u.name} ${JSON.stringify(u.input)}`);
   205	  if (!bad.length) console.log("no Skill call and no skill file read");
   206	  return bad.length === 0;
   207	}

   209	function session(file) {
   210	  const init = jsonLines(file).find((r) => r.type === "system" && r.subtype === "init");
   211	  if (!init?.session_id) return false;
   212	  console.log(init.session_id);
   213	  return true;
   214	}

   216	function plugins(kind, file) {
   217	  const data = JSON.parse(fs.readFileSync(file, "utf8"));
   218	  const list = kind === "claude" ? data : data.installed ?? [];
   219	  for (const p of list) {
   220	    if (kind === "claude") console.log(`${p.id} ${p.version} ${p.installPath ?? ""}`.trim());
   221	    else console.log(`${p.pluginId} ${p.version}`);
   222	  }
   223	  return true;
   224	}

   226	function hooksTrusted(file, pluginId, version, keys) {
   227	  const hooks = jsonLines(file).filter((h) => h.pluginId === pluginId);
   228	  let ok = true;
   229	  for (const h of hooks) {
   230	    const inVersion = String(h.sourcePath ?? "").includes(`/${version}/hooks/`);
   231	    console.log(`${h.key} ${h.trustStatus}${inVersion ? "" : ` from ${h.sourcePath}`}`);
   232	    if (h.trustStatus !== "trusted" || !inVersion) ok = false;
   233	  }
   234	  const got = hooks.map((h) => h.key).sort().join(" ");
   235	  if (got !== [...keys].sort().join(" ")) {
   236	    console.log(`expected keys ${keys.join(" ")}`);
   237	    ok = false;
   238	  }
   239	  return ok;
   240	}

   242	const [cmd, ...args] = process.argv.slice(2);
   243	const commands = {
   244	  bundle: () => bundle(args[0], args[1], args[2], args[3], args[4]),
   245	  "skill-arrived": () => skillArrived(args[0], args[1], args[2], args[3], args[4]),
   246	  compacted: () => compacted(args[0], args[1], args[2]),
   247	  "no-skill": () => noSkill(args[0]),
   248	  session: () => session(args[0]),
   249	  plugins: () => plugins(args[0], args[1]),
   250	  "hooks-trusted": () => hooksTrusted(args[0], args[1], args[2], args.slice(3)),
   251	};
   252	if (!commands[cmd]) {
   253	  console.error(`usage: inspect.mjs ${Object.keys(commands).join("|")} ...`);
   254	  process.exit(2);
   255	}
   256	let ok = false;
   257	try {
   258	  ok = commands[cmd]();
   259	} catch (err) {
   260	  console.log(`inspect.mjs ${cmd}: ${err.message}`);
   261	}
   262	process.exit(ok ? 0 : 1);
     1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
     2	# Install this marketplace into throwaway Claude Code and Codex homes and check
     3	# the behavior with the real CLIs. Your own ~/.claude and ~/.codex are not
     4	# touched, except that ~/.codex/auth.json is copied into each throwaway Codex
     5	# home for the run. Every throwaway home, with its auth.json copy and Codex
     6	# shell_snapshots, is deleted on exit. Logs, transcripts, and rollouts stay in
     7	# the printed logs folder.
     8	#
     9	# Needs both CLIs signed in, and node and git, so CI does not run it. Uses the
    10	# working tree, including uncommitted changes. Run `node tools/build.mjs`
    11	# first, so plugins/ is current.
    12	#
    13	#   tests/e2e/run.sh            run everything
    14	#   tests/e2e/run.sh claude     fresh install in Claude Code
    15	#   tests/e2e/run.sh codex      fresh install in Codex
    16	#   tests/e2e/run.sh migrate    upgrade from 0.2.2 in both runtimes
    17	#
    18	# By default the marketplace is a copy of the working tree. To install from
    19	# GitHub instead, which exercises the real clone and cache paths:
    20	#
    21	#   E2E_REPO=rubenvarela/adhd-unslop E2E_REF=main tests/e2e/run.sh
    22	#
    23	# migrate always serves a local git marketplace over smart HTTP on 127.0.0.1.
    24	# Its main branch starts at 0.2.2 (commit fc308bd) and then moves to the
    25	# working tree, or to E2E_REF of E2E_REPO when that is set.
    26	#
    27	# PASS and FAIL lines are checks. INFO lines record platform behavior that is
    28	# kept on purpose or outside this repo's control, and never fail the run.
    29	#
    30	# CLAUDE_BIN and CODEX_BIN pick other CLI binaries, for example a newer Codex:
    31	#
    32	#   CODEX_BIN=/path/to/node_modules/.bin/codex tests/e2e/run.sh codex
    33	
    34	# Codex skill names such as $adhd-unslop:adhd-unslop are literal prompt text.
    35	# shellcheck disable=SC2016
    36	set -u
    37	repo=$(cd "$(dirname "$0")/../.." && pwd)
    38	here=$repo/tests/e2e
    39	only=${1:-all}
    40	case $only in
    41	  all | claude | codex | migrate) ;;
    42	  *) echo "usage: $0 [claude|codex|migrate]"; exit 2 ;;
    43	esac
    44	
    45	claude_bin=${CLAUDE_BIN:-claude}
    46	codex_bin=${CODEX_BIN:-codex}
    47	real_home=$HOME
    48	# The commit that shipped adhd-unslop 0.2.2, the version migrate upgrades from.
    49	migrate_from=fc308bd
    50	# Hook trust keys of 0.2.2: three chunk handlers, then the dependency check.
    51	old_hook_keys=(0:0 0:1 0:2 1:0)
    52	# The three chunk handlers keep their keys, so their trust carries over.
    53	new_hook_keys=(0:0 0:1 0:2)

    55	# Drop the calling session's variables, so a run from inside Claude Code or
    56	# Codex behaves like one from a fresh terminal. Auth variables stay.
    57	for v in $(compgen -e); do
    58	  case $v in
    59	    CLAUDE_CODE_USE_* | CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN) ;;
    60	    CLAUDECODE | CLAUDE_CODE_* | CLAUDE_PID | CLAUDE_EFFORT | CLAUDE_PLUGIN_* | CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR | CLAUDE_SKILL_DIR) unset "$v" ;;
    61	    CODEX_HOME | CODEX_COMPANION_* | CODEX_THREAD_ID | PLUGIN_ROOT | AI_AGENT | ADHD_UNSLOP_*) unset "$v" ;;
    62	  esac
    63	done

    65	work=$(mktemp -d "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/adhd-unslop-e2e.XXXXXX")
    66	# Keep the model's working directory away from the marketplace copies, so a
    67	# file search cannot find an uninstalled plugin there.
    68	cwd=$(mktemp -d "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/adhd-unslop-cwd.XXXXXX")
    69	homes=$work/homes
    70	server_pid=
    71	cleanup() {
    72	  if [ -n "$server_pid" ]; then kill "$server_pid" 2>/dev/null; fi
    73	  # Delete the secrets first, then every throwaway home and marketplace copy,
    74	  # so no later run or model search finds their plugin copies.
    75	  find "$homes" \( -name auth.json -o -name 'logs_*.sqlite*' \) -exec rm -f {} + 2>/dev/null
    76	  find "$homes" -type d -name shell_snapshots -prune -exec rm -rf {} + 2>/dev/null
    77	  rm -rf "$cwd" "$homes" "$work/mkt" "$work/migrate"
    78	}
    79	trap cleanup EXIT
    80	trap 'exit 130' INT TERM HUP

    82	pass=0
    83	fail=0
    84	result() { if [ "$2" = ok ]; then echo "PASS  $1"; pass=$((pass + 1)); else echo "FAIL  $1"; fail=$((fail + 1)); fi; }
    85	expect() { local name=$1 pattern=$2 file=$3; if grep -Eq -- "$pattern" "$file" 2>/dev/null; then result "$name" ok; else result "$name" no; echo "      expected /$pattern/ in $file"; fi; }
    86	refuse() { local name=$1 pattern=$2 file=$3; if [ ! -f "$file" ]; then result "$name" no; echo "      missing $file"; elif grep -Eq -- "$pattern" "$file"; then result "$name" no; echo "      unexpected /$pattern/ in $file"; else result "$name" ok; fi; }
    87	# check NAME COMMAND...: PASS when COMMAND exits 0. Its output explains a FAIL.
    88	check() {
    89	  local name=$1 out
    90	  shift
    91	  if out=$("$@" 2>&1); then result "$name" ok; else result "$name" no; printf '%s\n' "$out" | sed 's/^/      /'; fi
    92	}
    93	# info NAME COMMAND...: an INFO line for platform behavior that is recorded,
    94	# not gated. It shows yes when COMMAND exits 0, no otherwise, and its output.
    95	info() {
    96	  local name=$1 out answer=no
    97	  shift
    98	  if out=$("$@" 2>&1); then answer=yes; fi
    99	  echo "INFO  $name: $answer"
   100	  if [ -n "$out" ]; then printf '%s\n' "$out" | sed 's/^/      /'; fi
   101	}
   102	inspect() { node "$here/inspect.mjs" "$@"; }
   103	
   104	# Plugin list helpers. FILE holds "id version [path]" lines from inspect plugins.
   105	has_plugin() {
   106	  local file=$1 id=$2 version=${3:-}
   107	  if awk -v id="$id" -v v="$version" '$1 == id && (v == "" || $2 == v) { found = 1 } END { exit !found }' "$file"; then return 0; fi
   108	  echo "expected $id${version:+ $version}; installed: $(awk '{ printf "%s %s; ", $1, $2 }' "$file")"
   109	  return 1
   110	}
   111	lacks_plugin() {
   112	  local file=$1 id=$2
   113	  if awk -v id="$id" '$1 == id { found = 1 } END { exit found }' "$file"; then return 0; fi
   114	  echo "unexpected $id; installed: $(awk '{ printf "%s %s; ", $1, $2 }' "$file")"
   115	  return 1
   116	}
   117	only_plugins() {
   118	  local file=$1 got want
   119	  shift
   120	  got=$(awk '$1 ~ /@adhd-unslop$/ { print $1 }' "$file" | sort | tr '\n' ' ')
   121	  want=$(printf '%s\n' "$@" | sort | tr '\n' ' ')
   122	  [ "$got" = "$want" ] && return 0
   123	  echo "installed from this marketplace: ${got:-nothing}; expected: $want"
   124	  return 1
   125	}
   126	only_entries() {
   127	  local dir=$1 got want
   128	  shift
   129	  got=$(find "$dir" -mindepth 1 -maxdepth 1 -exec basename {} \; 2>/dev/null | sort | tr '\n' ' ')
   130	  want=$(printf '%s\n' "$@" | sort | tr '\n' ' ')
   131	  [ "$got" = "$want" ] && return 0
   132	  echo "$dir holds: ${got:-nothing}; expected: $want"
   133	  return 1
   134	}
   135	exit_ok() { [ "$1" -eq 0 ] && return 0; cat "$2"; return 1; }
   136	keys_for() { local plugin=$1 k out=; shift; for k in "$@"; do out="$out $plugin:hooks/hooks.json:session_start:$k"; done; echo "$out"; }
   137	
   138	# Tree helpers.
   139	copy_tree() {
   140	  # Copy a checkout's tracked and untracked files, minus ignored and deleted ones.
   141	  (cd "$1" && git ls-files -co --exclude-standard -z | while IFS= read -r -d '' f; do
   142	    if [ -e "$f" ] || [ -L "$f" ]; then printf '%s\0' "$f"; fi
   143	  done | xargs -0 tar cf -) | (cd "$2" && tar xf -)
   144	}
   145	commit_all() { git -C "$1" add -A && git -C "$1" -c user.name=e2e -c user.email=e2e@example.invalid commit -qm "$2"; }
   146	json_field() { node -e 'const d=JSON.parse(require("fs").readFileSync(0,"utf8"));console.log(d[process.argv[1]])' "$1"; }
   147	bundle_from_manifest() { node -e 'console.log(JSON.parse(require("fs").readFileSync(0,"utf8")).compositeSha256.slice(0,12))'; }
   148	
   149	# Claude Code helpers. Each run gets its own config dir. CODEX_HOME points at
   150	# a missing folder, so a flag file in your real ~/.codex cannot turn
   151	# always-on on.
   152	claude_home=
   153	new_claude_home() { claude_home=$homes/$1; mkdir -p "$claude_home"; }
   154	cl() { CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR=$claude_home CODEX_HOME=$claude_home/no-codex "$claude_bin" "$@" </dev/null; }
   155	# clp LOG ARGS...: one print-mode turn from $cwd, as stream-json with hook events.
   156	clp() {
   157	  local log=$1
   158	  shift
   159	  (cd "$cwd" && CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR=$claude_home CODEX_HOME=$claude_home/no-codex \
   160	    "$claude_bin" -p --output-format stream-json --verbose --include-hook-events "$@" </dev/null >"$log" 2>&1)
   161	}
   162	# clturns LOG PROMPT...: several turns in one print-mode process from $cwd.
   163	clturns() {
   164	  local log=$1
   165	  shift
   166	  (cd "$cwd" && CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR=$claude_home CODEX_HOME=$claude_home/no-codex \
   167	    node "$here/claude-turns.mjs" "$claude_bin" "$log" "$@" </dev/null >/dev/null 2>&1)
   168	}
   169	claude_session() { inspect session "$1" 2>/dev/null; }
   170	claude_transcript() { find "$claude_home/projects" -name "$1.jsonl" 2>/dev/null | head -n 1; }
   171	claude_plugins() { cl plugin list --json >"$1.json" 2>"$1.err"; inspect plugins claude "$1.json" >"$1"; }
   172	
   173	# Codex helpers. HOME and CODEX_HOME point at the throwaway home, so neither
   174	# ~/.claude nor ~/.codex flag files count. API keys are unset, so Codex
   175	# cannot write them into shell_snapshots.
   176	codex_home=
   177	new_codex_home() {
   178	  codex_home=$homes/$1
   179	  mkdir -p "$codex_home/.codex"
   180	  cp "$real_home/.codex/auth.json" "$codex_home/.codex/auth.json"
   181	}
   182	cx_env() { env -u ANTHROPIC_API_KEY -u OPENAI_API_KEY -u CODEX_API_KEY HOME="$codex_home" CODEX_HOME="$codex_home/.codex" "$@"; }
   183	cxc() { cx_env "$codex_bin" "$@" </dev/null; }
   184	# cxe LOG ARGS...: one codex exec turn from $cwd.
   185	cxe() {
   186	  local log=$1
   187	  shift
   188	  (cd "$cwd" && cx_env "$codex_bin" exec --skip-git-repo-check -s read-only "$@" </dev/null >"$log" 2>&1)
   189	}
   190	codex_session() { sed -n 's/^session id: //p' "$1" | head -n 1; }
   191	codex_rollout() { find "$codex_home/.codex/sessions" -name "rollout-*-$1.jsonl" 2>/dev/null | head -n 1; }
   192	codex_plugins() { cxc plugin list --json >"$1.json" 2>"$1.err"; inspect plugins codex "$1.json" >"$1"; }
   193	codex_hooks() { cx_env node "$here/codex-hooks.mjs" "$codex_bin" "$cwd" "$@"; }

   195	same_claude_session() {
   196	  local log=$1 sid=$2 transcript=$3 prompt=$4 got
   197	  got=$(claude_session "$log")
   198	  [ "$got" = "$sid" ] || { echo "resumed session is ${got:-missing}, expected $sid"; return 1; }
   199	  grep -Fq "$prompt" "$transcript" || { echo "transcript $transcript lacks the resumed prompt"; return 1; }
   200	}
   201	same_codex_session() {
   202	  local log=$1 sid=$2 rollout=$3 prompt=$4 got
   203	  got=$(codex_session "$log")
   204	  [ "$got" = "$sid" ] || { echo "resumed session is ${got:-missing}, expected $sid"; return 1; }
   205	  grep -Fq "$prompt" "$rollout" || { echo "rollout $rollout lacks the resumed prompt"; return 1; }
   206	}

   209	echo "claude: $("$claude_bin" --version 2>&1 | head -n 1)"
   210	echo "codex: $("$codex_bin" --version 2>&1 </dev/null | head -n 1)"

   212	# Marketplace for the fresh-install runs. In local mode the expected versions
   213	# and bundle id come from the copy; in GitHub mode from the installed copy.
   214	source_ready=
   215	mkt=
   216	setup_source() {
   217	  [ -n "$source_ready" ] && return
   218	  source_ready=1
   219	  if [ -n "${E2E_REPO:-}" ]; then
   220	    ref=${E2E_REF:-main}
   221	    claude_source="$E2E_REPO#$ref"
   222	    codex_source=("$E2E_REPO" --ref "$ref")
   223	    echo "marketplace: $E2E_REPO at $ref"
   224	  else
   225	    mkt=$work/mkt
   226	    mkdir -p "$mkt"
   227	    copy_tree "$repo" "$mkt"
   228	    git -c init.defaultBranch=main init -q "$mkt"
   229	    commit_all "$mkt" e2e
   230	    claude_source=$mkt
   231	    codex_source=("$mkt")
   232	    echo "marketplace copy: $mkt"
   233	  fi
   234	}
   235	want_version() { [ -n "$mkt" ] && json_field version <"$mkt/plugins/$1/.claude-plugin/plugin.json"; }
   236	# The last line of the skill, which is the last line of the final check.
   237	want_final_line() {
   238	  local file
   239	  if [ -n "$mkt" ]; then file=$mkt/src/adhd-unslop/overlay/90-final-check.md; else file=$1/skills/adhd-unslop/SKILL.md; fi
   240	  awk 'NF { last = $0 } END { print last }' "$file" 2>/dev/null
   241	}
   242	want_bundle() {
   243	  local root=$1
   244	  if [ -n "$mkt" ]; then root=$mkt/plugins/adhd-unslop; fi
   245	  bundle_from_manifest <"$root/hooks/chunks/manifest.json" 2>/dev/null
   246	}

   248	run_claude() {
   249	  setup_source
   250	  new_claude_home claude
   251	  local log=$work/claude-install.log sid transcript bundle root final
   252	  cl plugin marketplace add "$claude_source" >"$log" 2>&1
   253	  cl plugin install adhd-unslop@adhd-unslop >>"$log" 2>&1
   254	  claude_plugins "$work/claude-plugins-1.txt"
   255	  check "claude: installing adhd-unslop installs only adhd-unslop" only_plugins "$work/claude-plugins-1.txt" adhd-unslop@adhd-unslop
   256	  check "claude: adhd-unslop has the expected version" has_plugin "$work/claude-plugins-1.txt" adhd-unslop@adhd-unslop "$(want_version adhd-unslop)"
   257	  refuse "claude: install reports no dependencies" "dependenc" "$log"
   258	  root=$(awk '$1 == "adhd-unslop@adhd-unslop" { print $3 }' "$work/claude-plugins-1.txt")
   259	  bundle=$(want_bundle "$root")
   260	  final=$(want_final_line "$root")
   261	  echo "      bundle id: ${bundle:-unknown}; final check line: ${final:-unknown}"
   262	
   263	  # Always-on is off: no flag file and ADHD_UNSLOP_ALWAYS unset.
   264	  log=$work/claude-invoke.log
   265	  clp "$log" '/adhd-unslop:adhd-unslop Reply with the single word READY.'
   266	  sid=$(claude_session "$log")
   267	  transcript=$(claude_transcript "$sid")
   268	  [ -n "$transcript" ] && cp "$transcript" "$work/claude-invoke.transcript.jsonl"
   269	  expect "claude: /adhd-unslop:adhd-unslop answers" '"result":"READY' "$log"
   270	  check "claude: always-on off injects no chunk" inspect bundle claude "$transcript" "$bundle" none
   271	  check "claude: skill text arrives with both upstream texts and the final check line" \
   272	    inspect skill-arrived claude "$transcript" "$root/skills/adhd-unslop/SKILL.md" "$final"
   273	  check "claude: skill body arrives whole" \
   274	    inspect skill-arrived claude "$transcript" "$root/skills/adhd-unslop/SKILL.md" "$final" whole
   275	
   276	  # The clean case: only adhd-unslop is installed.
   277	  log=$work/claude-unprompted.log
   278	  clp "$log" 'What is 17 times 3? Digits only.'
   279	  expect "claude: unprompted question answers" '"result":"51' "$log"
   280	  check "claude: unprompted question loads no skill" inspect no-skill "$log"
   281	
   282	  # Platform behavior, recorded as INFO: what an invoked skill keeps after
   283	  # compaction. The skill is larger than the 20,000-character re-attach budget.
   284	  log=$work/claude-compact-same.log
   285	  clturns "$log" '/adhd-unslop:adhd-unslop Reply with the single word READY.' '/compact'
   286	  transcript=$(claude_transcript "$(claude_session "$log")")
   287	  [ -n "$transcript" ] && cp "$transcript" "$work/claude-compact-same.transcript.jsonl"
   288	  info "claude: after /compact in the same process, the skill keeps its final check line" \
   289	    inspect compacted "$transcript" adhd-unslop:adhd-unslop "$final"
   290	  log=$work/claude-compact-resume.log
   291	  clp "$log" --resume "$sid" '/compact'
   292	  transcript=$(claude_transcript "$sid")
   293	  [ -n "$transcript" ] && cp "$transcript" "$work/claude-compact-resume.transcript.jsonl"
   294	  info "claude: after --resume then /compact, the skill keeps its final check line" \
   295	    inspect compacted "$transcript" adhd-unslop:adhd-unslop "$final"
   296	
   297	  log=$work/claude-install.log
   298	  cl plugin install au-i-have-adhd@adhd-unslop >>"$log" 2>&1
   299	  cl plugin install au-unslop@adhd-unslop >>"$log" 2>&1
   300	  claude_plugins "$work/claude-plugins-2.txt"
   301	  check "claude: au-i-have-adhd installs by name" has_plugin "$work/claude-plugins-2.txt" au-i-have-adhd@adhd-unslop "$(want_version au-i-have-adhd)"
   302	  check "claude: au-unslop installs by name" has_plugin "$work/claude-plugins-2.txt" au-unslop@adhd-unslop "$(want_version au-unslop)"
   303	
   304	  log=$work/claude-typed-adhd.log
   305	  clp "$log" '/au-i-have-adhd:i-have-adhd Reply with the number of the rule that caps list length, digits only.'
   306	  expect "claude: typed /au-i-have-adhd:i-have-adhd works" '"result":"9[^0-9]' "$log"
   307	
   308	  log=$work/claude-typed-unslop.log
   309	  clp "$log" '/au-unslop:unslop Reply with the number of the rule about em dashes, digits only.'
   310	  expect "claude: typed /au-unslop:unslop works" '"result":"13[^0-9]' "$log"
   311	
   312	  touch "$claude_home/.adhd-unslop-always"
   313	  log=$work/claude-always-on.log
   314	  clp "$log" 'Reply with the single word OK.'
   315	  sid=$(claude_session "$log")
   316	  transcript=$(claude_transcript "$sid")
   317	  [ -n "$transcript" ] && cp "$transcript" "$work/claude-always-on.transcript.jsonl"
   318	  check "claude: always-on delivers one complete bundle at startup" inspect bundle claude "$transcript" "$bundle" exact
   319	
   320	  log=$work/claude-resume.log
   321	  clp "$log" --resume "$sid" 'Reply with the single word AGAIN.'
   322	  check "claude: --resume continues the same session" same_claude_session "$log" "$sid" "$transcript" 'Reply with the single word AGAIN.'
   323	  expect "claude: resume fires SessionStart with source resume" '"hook_name":"SessionStart:resume"' "$log"
   324	  [ -n "$transcript" ] && cp "$transcript" "$work/claude-resume.transcript.jsonl"
   325	  check "claude: resumed transcript holds exactly one copy of each chunk" inspect bundle claude "$transcript" "$bundle" exact
   326	
   327	  # Always-on through compaction: /compact in the same process.
   328	  log=$work/claude-compact-always-on.log
   329	  clturns "$log" 'Reply with the single word OK.' '/compact'
   330	  transcript=$(claude_transcript "$(claude_session "$log")")
   331	  [ -n "$transcript" ] && cp "$transcript" "$work/claude-compact-always-on.transcript.jsonl"
   332	  expect "claude: /compact fires SessionStart with source compact" '"hook_name":"SessionStart:compact"' "$log"
   333	  check "claude: after /compact, the context holds exactly one complete bundle" \
   334	    inspect bundle claude "$transcript" "$bundle" exact after-compact
   335	}
