   337	run_codex() {
   338	  setup_source
   339	  new_codex_home codex
   340	  local log=$work/codex-install.log sid rollout bundle version root final
   341	  cxc plugin marketplace add "${codex_source[@]}" >"$log" 2>&1
   342	  cxc plugin add adhd-unslop@adhd-unslop >>"$log" 2>&1
   343	  codex_plugins "$work/codex-plugins-1.txt"
   344	  check "codex: installing adhd-unslop installs only adhd-unslop" only_plugins "$work/codex-plugins-1.txt" adhd-unslop@adhd-unslop
   345	  check "codex: adhd-unslop has the expected version" has_plugin "$work/codex-plugins-1.txt" adhd-unslop@adhd-unslop "$(want_version adhd-unslop)"
   346	  check "codex: plugin cache holds only adhd-unslop" only_entries "$codex_home/.codex/plugins/cache/adhd-unslop" adhd-unslop
   347	  version=$(awk '$1 == "adhd-unslop@adhd-unslop" { print $2 }' "$work/codex-plugins-1.txt")
   348	  root=$codex_home/.codex/plugins/cache/adhd-unslop/adhd-unslop/$version
   349	  bundle=$(want_bundle "$root")
   350	  final=$(want_final_line "$root")
   351	  echo "      bundle id: ${bundle:-unknown}; final check line: ${final:-unknown}"
   352	
   353	  # Always-on is off: no flag file, and the hooks are not trusted yet.
   354	  log=$work/codex-invoke.log
   355	  cxe "$log" -o "$work/codex-invoke.txt" '$adhd-unslop:adhd-unslop Reply with the single word READY.'
   356	  sid=$(codex_session "$log")
   357	  rollout=$(codex_rollout "$sid")
   358	  [ -n "$rollout" ] && cp "$rollout" "$work/codex-invoke.rollout.jsonl"
   359	  expect "codex: \$adhd-unslop:adhd-unslop answers" 'READY' "$work/codex-invoke.txt"
   360	  check "codex: always-on off injects no chunk" inspect bundle codex "$rollout" "$bundle" none
   361	  check "codex: skill text arrives with both upstream texts and the final check line" \
   362	    inspect skill-arrived codex "$rollout" "$root/skills/adhd-unslop/SKILL.md" "$final"
   363	  check "codex: skill body arrives whole, not cut" \
   364	    inspect skill-arrived codex "$rollout" "$root/skills/adhd-unslop/SKILL.md" "$final" whole
   365	
   366	  # The clean case: only adhd-unslop is installed.
   367	  log=$work/codex-unprompted.log
   368	  cxe "$log" -o "$work/codex-unprompted.txt" 'What is 17 times 3? Digits only.'
   369	  rollout=$(codex_rollout "$(codex_session "$log")")
   370	  expect "codex: unprompted question answers" '^51' "$work/codex-unprompted.txt"
   371	  refuse "codex: unprompted question reads no skill file" 'SKILL\.md' "$log"
   372	  refuse "codex: unprompted question injects no plugin skill" '<name>(adhd-unslop|au-i-have-adhd|au-unslop):' "$rollout"
   373	
   374	  log=$work/codex-install.log
   375	  cxc plugin add au-i-have-adhd@adhd-unslop >>"$log" 2>&1
   376	  cxc plugin add au-unslop@adhd-unslop >>"$log" 2>&1
   377	  codex_plugins "$work/codex-plugins-2.txt"
   378	  check "codex: au-i-have-adhd installs by name" has_plugin "$work/codex-plugins-2.txt" au-i-have-adhd@adhd-unslop "$(want_version au-i-have-adhd)"
   379	  check "codex: au-unslop installs by name" has_plugin "$work/codex-plugins-2.txt" au-unslop@adhd-unslop "$(want_version au-unslop)"
   380	
   381	  log=$work/codex-typed-adhd.log
   382	  cxe "$log" -o "$work/codex-typed-adhd.txt" '$au-i-have-adhd:i-have-adhd Reply with the number of the rule that caps list length, digits only.'
   383	  expect "codex: typed \$au-i-have-adhd:i-have-adhd works" '^9([^0-9]|$)' "$work/codex-typed-adhd.txt"
   384	
   385	  log=$work/codex-typed-unslop.log
   386	  cxe "$log" -o "$work/codex-typed-unslop.txt" '$au-unslop:unslop Reply with the number of the rule about em dashes, digits only.'
   387	  expect "codex: typed \$au-unslop:unslop works" '^13([^0-9]|$)' "$work/codex-typed-unslop.txt"
   388	
   389	  # With the mirrors installed. au-unslop keeps upstream's model-invocable
   390	  # "Must always apply" skill on purpose, so its auto-load is INFO.
   391	  log=$work/codex-unprompted-mirrors.log
   392	  cxe "$log" -o "$work/codex-unprompted-mirrors.txt" 'What is 17 times 3? Digits only.'
   393	  expect "codex: unprompted question with the mirrors answers" '^51' "$work/codex-unprompted-mirrors.txt"
   394	  refuse "codex: with the mirrors, the unprompted question loads no adhd-unslop or au-i-have-adhd skill" \
   395	    'cache/adhd-unslop/(adhd-unslop|au-i-have-adhd)/[^ ]*SKILL\.md' "$log"
   396	  info "codex: with the mirrors, the unprompted question auto-loads au-unslop:unslop" \
   397	    grep -Eo 'au-unslop/[^ ]*/SKILL\.md' "$log"
   398	
   399	  touch "$codex_home/.codex/.adhd-unslop-always"
   400	  log=$work/codex-always-on.log
   401	  cxe "$log" --dangerously-bypass-hook-trust -o "$work/codex-always-on.txt" 'Reply with the single word OK.'
   402	  sid=$(codex_session "$log")
   403	  rollout=$(codex_rollout "$sid")
   404	  [ -n "$rollout" ] && cp "$rollout" "$work/codex-always-on.rollout.jsonl"
   405	  check "codex: always-on delivers one complete bundle at startup" inspect bundle codex "$rollout" "$bundle" exact
   406	
   407	  log=$work/codex-resume.log
   408	  cxe "$log" --dangerously-bypass-hook-trust resume --last 'Reply with the single word AGAIN.'
   409	  check "codex: exec resume --last continues the same session" same_codex_session "$log" "$sid" "$rollout" 'Reply with the single word AGAIN.'
   410	  [ -n "$rollout" ] && cp "$rollout" "$work/codex-resume.rollout.jsonl"
   411	  check "codex: resumed rollout holds at least one copy of each chunk" inspect bundle codex "$rollout" "$bundle" atleast
   412	
   413	  # Always-on through compaction. codex exec cannot compact on request, so
   414	  # app-server runs a turn, thread/compact/start (what the TUI's /compact
   415	  # sends), and one more turn, which fires the queued compact source.
   416	  # App-server has no bypass flag, so the hooks need recorded trust.
   417	  local rc out
   418	  codex_hooks trust adhd-unslop@adhd-unslop >>"$work/codex-install.log" 2>&1
   419	  log=$work/codex-compact.log
   420	  out=$(cx_env node "$here/codex-thread.mjs" "$codex_bin" "$cwd" "$log" \
   421	    'turn:Reply with the single word OK.' compact 'turn:Reply with the single word AGAIN.' 2>&1)
   422	  rc=$?
   423	  printf '%s\n' "$out" >"$work/codex-compact.out"
   424	  rollout=$(sed -n 's/^rollout //p' "$work/codex-compact.out")
   425	  [ -n "$rollout" ] || rollout=$(codex_rollout "$(sed -n 's/^thread //p' "$work/codex-compact.out")")
   426	  [ -n "$rollout" ] && cp "$rollout" "$work/codex-compact.rollout.jsonl"
   427	  check "codex: app-server runs a turn, a compaction, and another turn" exit_ok "$rc" "$work/codex-compact.out"
   428	  check "codex: after thread compaction, the context holds exactly one complete bundle" \
   429	    inspect bundle codex "$rollout" "$bundle" exact after-compact
   430	}

   432	# A local git marketplace whose main branch starts at 0.2.2 and moves to the
   433	# tree under test. Both runtimes reset main to 0.2.2 before they install.
   434	setup_migrate() {
   435	  local src=$work/migrate/src srv=$work/migrate/srv next=$work/migrate/next port
   436	  mkdir -p "$src" "$srv" "$next"
   437	  git -C "$repo" archive "$migrate_from" | tar xf - -C "$src" || return 1
   438	  git -c init.defaultBranch=main init -q "$src"
   439	  commit_all "$src" "adhd-unslop 0.2.2 ($migrate_from)"
   440	  old_commit=$(git -C "$src" rev-parse HEAD)
   441	  if [ -n "${E2E_REPO:-}" ]; then
   442	    git clone -q --depth 1 --branch "${E2E_REF:-main}" "https://github.com/$E2E_REPO.git" "$work/migrate/gh" || return 1
   443	    copy_tree "$work/migrate/gh" "$next"
   444	  else
   445	    copy_tree "$repo" "$next"
   446	  fi
   447	  git -C "$src" rm -rqf .
   448	  (cd "$next" && tar cf - .) | (cd "$src" && tar xf -)
   449	  commit_all "$src" "tree under test"
   450	  new_commit=$(git -C "$src" rev-parse HEAD)
   451	  git clone -q --bare "$src" "$srv/adhd-unslop.git"
   452	  bare=$srv/adhd-unslop.git
   453	  old_version=$(git -C "$src" show "$old_commit:plugins/adhd-unslop/.claude-plugin/plugin.json" | json_field version)
   454	  new_version=$(git -C "$src" show "$new_commit:plugins/adhd-unslop/.claude-plugin/plugin.json" | json_field version)
   455	  new_mirror_version=$(git -C "$src" show "$new_commit:plugins/au-unslop/.claude-plugin/plugin.json" | json_field version)
   456	  new_bundle=$(git -C "$src" show "$new_commit:plugins/adhd-unslop/hooks/chunks/manifest.json" | bundle_from_manifest)
   457	
   458	  node "$here/githttp.mjs" "$srv" >"$work/githttp.log" 2>&1 &
   459	  server_pid=$!
   460	  for _ in $(seq 1 100); do
   461	    grep -q '^listening' "$work/githttp.log" 2>/dev/null && break
   462	    sleep 0.1
   463	  done
   464	  port=$(awk '/^listening/ { print $2 }' "$work/githttp.log")
   465	  [ -n "$port" ] || return 1
   466	  migrate_url=http://127.0.0.1:$port/adhd-unslop.git
   467	  echo "migrate marketplace: $migrate_url, $old_version at ${old_commit:0:7} then $new_version at ${new_commit:0:7} (bundle $new_bundle)"
   468	}
   469	move_main() { git --git-dir="$bare" update-ref refs/heads/main "$1"; }

     1	// Smart-HTTP git server for tests/e2e/run.sh. Serves the bare repos under
     2	// <root> on 127.0.0.1 by running `git http-backend` as CGI, so both CLIs can
     3	// add a git marketplace with real clone and cache paths and no GitHub push.
     4	// design/research/08-tests-claude.md has the method.
     5	//
     6	//   node tests/e2e/githttp.mjs <root> [port]
     7	//
     8	// Port 0, the default, picks a free port. The first stdout line is
     9	// "listening <port>".
    10	
    11	import http from "node:http";
    12	import { spawn } from "node:child_process";
    13	
    14	const root = process.argv[2];
    15	const port = Number(process.argv[3] || 0);
    16	if (!root) {
    17	  console.error("usage: githttp.mjs <root> [port]");
    18	  process.exit(2);
    19	}
    20	
    21	const server = http.createServer((req, res) => {
    22	  const url = new URL(req.url, "http://127.0.0.1");
    23	  const env = {
    24	    PATH: process.env.PATH,
    25	    GIT_PROJECT_ROOT: root,
    26	    GIT_HTTP_EXPORT_ALL: "1",
    27	    PATH_INFO: url.pathname,
    28	    QUERY_STRING: url.search.slice(1),
    29	    REQUEST_METHOD: req.method,
    30	    CONTENT_TYPE: req.headers["content-type"] || "",
    31	    REMOTE_ADDR: "127.0.0.1",
    32	  };
    33	  if (req.headers["git-protocol"]) env.GIT_PROTOCOL = req.headers["git-protocol"];
    34	  if (req.headers["content-encoding"]) env.HTTP_CONTENT_ENCODING = req.headers["content-encoding"];
    35	  const git = spawn("git", ["http-backend"], { env });
    36	  req.pipe(git.stdin);
    37	  let head = Buffer.alloc(0);
    38	  let headersDone = false;
    39	  git.stdout.on("data", (chunk) => {
    40	    if (headersDone) {
    41	      res.write(chunk);
    42	      return;
    43	    }
    44	    head = Buffer.concat([head, chunk]);
    45	    let end = head.indexOf("\r\n\r\n");
    46	    let sep = 4;
    47	    if (end < 0) {
    48	      end = head.indexOf("\n\n");
    49	      sep = 2;
    50	    }
    51	    if (end < 0) return;
    52	    let status = 200;
    53	    for (const line of head.subarray(0, end).toString().replace(/\r/g, "").split("\n")) {
    54	      const colon = line.indexOf(":");
    55	      if (colon < 0) continue;
    56	      const key = line.slice(0, colon).trim();
    57	      const value = line.slice(colon + 1).trim();
    58	      if (key.toLowerCase() === "status") status = Number.parseInt(value, 10);
    59	      else res.setHeader(key, value);
    60	    }
    61	    res.writeHead(status);
    62	    headersDone = true;
    63	    res.write(head.subarray(end + sep));
    64	  });
    65	  git.stdout.on("end", () => res.end());
    66	  git.stderr.on("data", (d) => process.stderr.write(d));
    67	  git.on("error", () => {
    68	    if (!headersDone) res.writeHead(500);
    69	    res.end();
    70	  });
    71	});
    72	
    73	server.listen(port, "127.0.0.1", () => {
    74	  console.log(`listening ${server.address().port}`);
    75	});

    84	result() { if [ "$2" = ok ]; then echo "PASS  $1"; pass=$((pass + 1)); else echo "FAIL  $1"; fail=$((fail + 1)); fi; }
    85	expect() { local name=$1 pattern=$2 file=$3; if grep -Eq -- "$pattern" "$file" 2>/dev/null; then result "$name" ok; else result "$name" no; echo "      expected /$pattern/ in $file"; fi; }
    86	refuse() { local name=$1 pattern=$2 file=$3; if [ ! -f "$file" ]; then result "$name" no; echo "      missing $file"; elif grep -Eq -- "$pattern" "$file"; then result "$name" no; echo "      unexpected /$pattern/ in $file"; else result "$name" ok; fi; }
    87	# check NAME COMMAND...: PASS when COMMAND exits 0. Its output explains a FAIL.

   104	# Plugin list helpers. FILE holds "id version [path]" lines from inspect plugins.
   105	has_plugin() {
   106	  local file=$1 id=$2 version=${3:-}
   107	  if awk -v id="$id" -v v="$version" '$1 == id && (v == "" || $2 == v) { found = 1 } END { exit !found }' "$file"; then return 0; fi
   108	  echo "expected $id${version:+ $version}; installed: $(awk '{ printf "%s %s; ", $1, $2 }' "$file")"
   109	  return 1
   110	}
   111	lacks_plugin() {
   112	  local file=$1 id=$2
   113	  if awk -v id="$id" '$1 == id { found = 1 } END { exit found }' "$file"; then return 0; fi
   114	  echo "unexpected $id; installed: $(awk '{ printf "%s %s; ", $1, $2 }' "$file")"
   115	  return 1
   116	}
   117	only_plugins() {
   118	  local file=$1 got want
   119	  shift

   121	  want=$(printf '%s\n' "$@" | sort | tr '\n' ' ')
   122	  [ "$got" = "$want" ] && return 0
   123	  echo "installed from this marketplace: ${got:-nothing}; expected: $want"
   124	  return 1
   125	}
   126	only_entries() {
   127	  local dir=$1 got want
   128	  shift
   129	  got=$(find "$dir" -mindepth 1 -maxdepth 1 -exec basename {} \; 2>/dev/null | sort | tr '\n' ' ')
   130	  want=$(printf '%s\n' "$@" | sort | tr '\n' ' ')
   131	  [ "$got" = "$want" ] && return 0
   132	  echo "$dir holds: ${got:-nothing}; expected: $want"
   133	  return 1
   134	}
   135	exit_ok() { [ "$1" -eq 0 ] && return 0; cat "$2"; return 1; }
   136	keys_for() { local plugin=$1 k out=; shift; for k in "$@"; do out="$out $plugin:hooks/hooks.json:session_start:$k"; done; echo "$out"; }

   138	# Tree helpers.
   139	copy_tree() {
   140	  # Copy a checkout's tracked and untracked files, minus ignored and deleted ones.
   141	  (cd "$1" && git ls-files -co --exclude-standard -z | while IFS= read -r -d '' f; do
   142	    if [ -e "$f" ] || [ -L "$f" ]; then printf '%s\0' "$f"; fi
   143	  done | xargs -0 tar cf -) | (cd "$2" && tar xf -)
   144	}
   145	commit_all() { git -C "$1" add -A && git -C "$1" -c user.name=e2e -c user.email=e2e@example.invalid commit -qm "$2"; }
   146	json_field() { node -e 'const d=JSON.parse(require("fs").readFileSync(0,"utf8"));console.log(d[process.argv[1]])' "$1"; }
   147	bundle_from_manifest() { node -e 'console.log(JSON.parse(require("fs").readFileSync(0,"utf8")).compositeSha256.slice(0,12))'; }

   149	# Claude Code helpers. Each run gets its own config dir. CODEX_HOME points at
   150	# a missing folder, so a flag file in your real ~/.codex cannot turn
   151	# always-on on.

   153	new_claude_home() { claude_home=$homes/$1; mkdir -p "$claude_home"; }
   154	cl() { CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR=$claude_home CODEX_HOME=$claude_home/no-codex "$claude_bin" "$@" </dev/null; }
   155	# clp LOG ARGS...: one print-mode turn from $cwd, as stream-json with hook events.
   156	clp() {
   157	  local log=$1
   158	  shift
   159	  (cd "$cwd" && CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR=$claude_home CODEX_HOME=$claude_home/no-codex \
   160	    "$claude_bin" -p --output-format stream-json --verbose --include-hook-events "$@" </dev/null >"$log" 2>&1)
   161	}
   162	# clturns LOG PROMPT...: several turns in one print-mode process from $cwd.
   163	clturns() {
   164	  local log=$1
   165	  shift
   166	  (cd "$cwd" && CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR=$claude_home CODEX_HOME=$claude_home/no-codex \
   167	    node "$here/claude-turns.mjs" "$claude_bin" "$log" "$@" </dev/null >/dev/null 2>&1)
   168	}

   198	  [ "$got" = "$sid" ] || { echo "resumed session is ${got:-missing}, expected $sid"; return 1; }
   199	  grep -Fq "$prompt" "$transcript" || { echo "transcript $transcript lacks the resumed prompt"; return 1; }

   205	  grep -Fq "$prompt" "$rollout" || { echo "rollout $rollout lacks the resumed prompt"; return 1; }

   235	want_version() { [ -n "$mkt" ] && json_field version <"$mkt/plugins/$1/.claude-plugin/plugin.json"; }
   236	# The last line of the skill, which is the last line of the final check.

   240	  awk 'NF { last = $0 } END { print last }' "$file" 2>/dev/null

   245	  bundle_from_manifest <"$root/hooks/chunks/manifest.json" 2>/dev/null

   248	run_claude() {
   249	  setup_source
   250	  new_claude_home claude
   251	  local log=$work/claude-install.log sid transcript bundle root final
   252	  cl plugin marketplace add "$claude_source" >"$log" 2>&1
   253	  cl plugin install adhd-unslop@adhd-unslop >>"$log" 2>&1
   254	  claude_plugins "$work/claude-plugins-1.txt"
   255	  check "claude: installing adhd-unslop installs only adhd-unslop" only_plugins "$work/claude-plugins-1.txt" adhd-unslop@adhd-unslop
   256	  check "claude: adhd-unslop has the expected version" has_plugin "$work/claude-plugins-1.txt" adhd-unslop@adhd-unslop "$(want_version adhd-unslop)"
   257	  refuse "claude: install reports no dependencies" "dependenc" "$log"
   258	  root=$(awk '$1 == "adhd-unslop@adhd-unslop" { print $3 }' "$work/claude-plugins-1.txt")
   259	  bundle=$(want_bundle "$root")
   260	  final=$(want_final_line "$root")
   261	  echo "      bundle id: ${bundle:-unknown}; final check line: ${final:-unknown}"
   262	
   263	  # Always-on is off: no flag file and ADHD_UNSLOP_ALWAYS unset.
   264	  log=$work/claude-invoke.log
   265	  clp "$log" '/adhd-unslop:adhd-unslop Reply with the single word READY.'
   266	  sid=$(claude_session "$log")
   267	  transcript=$(claude_transcript "$sid")
   268	  [ -n "$transcript" ] && cp "$transcript" "$work/claude-invoke.transcript.jsonl"
   269	  expect "claude: /adhd-unslop:adhd-unslop answers" '"result":"READY' "$log"
   270	  check "claude: always-on off injects no chunk" inspect bundle claude "$transcript" "$bundle" none
   271	  check "claude: skill text arrives with both upstream texts and the final check line" \
   272	    inspect skill-arrived claude "$transcript" "$root/skills/adhd-unslop/SKILL.md" "$final"
   273	  check "claude: skill body arrives whole" \
   274	    inspect skill-arrived claude "$transcript" "$root/skills/adhd-unslop/SKILL.md" "$final" whole
   275	
   276	  # The clean case: only adhd-unslop is installed.
   277	  log=$work/claude-unprompted.log
   278	  clp "$log" 'What is 17 times 3? Digits only.'
   279	  expect "claude: unprompted question answers" '"result":"51' "$log"
   280	  check "claude: unprompted question loads no skill" inspect no-skill "$log"
   281	
   282	  # Platform behavior, recorded as INFO: what an invoked skill keeps after
   283	  # compaction. The skill is larger than the 20,000-character re-attach budget.
   284	  log=$work/claude-compact-same.log
   285	  clturns "$log" '/adhd-unslop:adhd-unslop Reply with the single word READY.' '/compact'
   286	  transcript=$(claude_transcript "$(claude_session "$log")")
   287	  [ -n "$transcript" ] && cp "$transcript" "$work/claude-compact-same.transcript.jsonl"
   288	  info "claude: after /compact in the same process, the skill keeps its final check line" \
   289	    inspect compacted "$transcript" adhd-unslop:adhd-unslop "$final"
   290	  log=$work/claude-compact-resume.log
   291	  clp "$log" --resume "$sid" '/compact'
   292	  transcript=$(claude_transcript "$sid")
   293	  [ -n "$transcript" ] && cp "$transcript" "$work/claude-compact-resume.transcript.jsonl"
   294	  info "claude: after --resume then /compact, the skill keeps its final check line" \
   295	    inspect compacted "$transcript" adhd-unslop:adhd-unslop "$final"
   296	
   297	  log=$work/claude-install.log
   298	  cl plugin install au-i-have-adhd@adhd-unslop >>"$log" 2>&1
   299	  cl plugin install au-unslop@adhd-unslop >>"$log" 2>&1
   300	  claude_plugins "$work/claude-plugins-2.txt"
   301	  check "claude: au-i-have-adhd installs by name" has_plugin "$work/claude-plugins-2.txt" au-i-have-adhd@adhd-unslop "$(want_version au-i-have-adhd)"
   302	  check "claude: au-unslop installs by name" has_plugin "$work/claude-plugins-2.txt" au-unslop@adhd-unslop "$(want_version au-unslop)"
   303	
   304	  log=$work/claude-typed-adhd.log
   305	  clp "$log" '/au-i-have-adhd:i-have-adhd Reply with the number of the rule that caps list length, digits only.'
   306	  expect "claude: typed /au-i-have-adhd:i-have-adhd works" '"result":"9[^0-9]' "$log"
   307	
   308	  log=$work/claude-typed-unslop.log
   309	  clp "$log" '/au-unslop:unslop Reply with the number of the rule about em dashes, digits only.'
   310	  expect "claude: typed /au-unslop:unslop works" '"result":"13[^0-9]' "$log"
   311	
   312	  touch "$claude_home/.adhd-unslop-always"
   313	  log=$work/claude-always-on.log
   314	  clp "$log" 'Reply with the single word OK.'
   315	  sid=$(claude_session "$log")
   316	  transcript=$(claude_transcript "$sid")
   317	  [ -n "$transcript" ] && cp "$transcript" "$work/claude-always-on.transcript.jsonl"
   318	  check "claude: always-on delivers one complete bundle at startup" inspect bundle claude "$transcript" "$bundle" exact
   319	
   320	  log=$work/claude-resume.log
   321	  clp "$log" --resume "$sid" 'Reply with the single word AGAIN.'
   322	  check "claude: --resume continues the same session" same_claude_session "$log" "$sid" "$transcript" 'Reply with the single word AGAIN.'
   323	  expect "claude: resume fires SessionStart with source resume" '"hook_name":"SessionStart:resume"' "$log"
   324	  [ -n "$transcript" ] && cp "$transcript" "$work/claude-resume.transcript.jsonl"
   325	  check "claude: resumed transcript holds exactly one copy of each chunk" inspect bundle claude "$transcript" "$bundle" exact
   326	
   327	  # Always-on through compaction: /compact in the same process.
   328	  log=$work/claude-compact-always-on.log
   329	  clturns "$log" 'Reply with the single word OK.' '/compact'
   330	  transcript=$(claude_transcript "$(claude_session "$log")")
   331	  [ -n "$transcript" ] && cp "$transcript" "$work/claude-compact-always-on.transcript.jsonl"
   332	  expect "claude: /compact fires SessionStart with source compact" '"hook_name":"SessionStart:compact"' "$log"
   333	  check "claude: after /compact, the context holds exactly one complete bundle" \
   334	    inspect bundle claude "$transcript" "$bundle" exact after-compact
   335	}

    89	  throw new Error(`unknown runtime ${kind}`);

    92	function bundle(kind, file, id, mode, scope) {
    93	  const counts = { 1: 0, 2: 0, 3: 0 };
    94	  const others = [];
    95	  for (const text of contextTexts(kind, file, scope)) {
    96	    for (const m of text.matchAll(END)) {
    97	      if (m[2] === id && counts[m[1]] !== undefined) counts[m[1]]++;
    98	      else others.push(`chunk ${m[1]} (${m[2]})`);
    99	    }
   100	  }
   101	  const summary = `chunk 1: ${counts[1]}, chunk 2: ${counts[2]}, chunk 3: ${counts[3]} with ${id}; other END lines: ${others.length ? others.join(", ") : "none"}`;
   102	  const all = [1, 2, 3].map((i) => counts[i]);
   103	  let ok;
   104	  if (mode === "exact") ok = all.every((n) => n === 1) && others.length === 0;
   105	  else if (mode === "atleast") ok = all.every((n) => n >= 1);
   106	  else if (mode === "none") ok = all.every((n) => n === 0) && others.length === 0;
   107	  else throw new Error(`unknown mode ${mode}`);
   108	  console.log(summary);
   109	  return ok;
   110	}
   111	
   112	function toolUses(records) {
   113	  const uses = [];
   114	  for (const r of records) {
   115	    if (r.type !== "assistant") continue;
   116	    for (const c of r.message?.content ?? []) if (c.type === "tool_use") uses.push(c);
   117	  }
   118	  return uses;
   119	}
   120	
   121	const BEGIN_MARKERS = ["<!-- BEGIN upstream i-have-adhd", "<!-- BEGIN upstream unslop"];
   122	
   123	function skillRecords(kind, file) {
   124	  const records = jsonLines(file);
   125	  if (kind === "claude") {
   126	    const out = [];
   127	    for (const r of records) {
   128	      if (r.type === "user" && r.message) out.push({ where: r.isMeta ? "skill message" : "user message", text: texts(r.message.content).join("\n") });
   129	      if (r.type === "attachment" && r.attachment && r.attachment.type !== "prompt_snapshot")
   130	        out.push({ where: `${r.attachment.type} attachment`, text: texts(r.attachment.content ?? r.attachment.skills).join("\n") });
   131	    }
   132	    return out;
   133	  }
   134	  if (kind === "codex") {
   135	    return records
   136	      .filter((r) => r.type === "response_item" && r.payload?.type === "message")
   137	      .map((r) => ({ where: `${r.payload.role} message`, text: texts(r.payload.content).join("\n") }));
   138	  }
   139	  throw new Error(`unknown runtime ${kind}`);
   140	}
   141	
   142	function skillArrived(kind, file, skillPath, finalLine, whole) {
   143	  const markers = [...BEGIN_MARKERS, finalLine];
   144	  const records = skillRecords(kind, file);
   145	  const hit = records.find((r) => markers.every((m) => r.text.includes(m)));
   146	  if (!hit) {
   147	    const best = records
   148	      .map((r) => ({ r, n: markers.filter((m) => r.text.includes(m)).length }))
   149	      .sort((a, b) => b.n - a.n)[0];
   150	    const found = best ? markers.filter((m) => best.r.text.includes(m)) : [];
   151	    console.log(`no record holds all three markers; best: ${best ? `${best.r.where}, ${best.r.text.length} chars, with ${found.join(" | ") || "none"}` : "no records"}`);
   152	    return false;
   153	  }
   154	  if (whole !== "whole") {
   155	    console.log(`${hit.where}, ${hit.text.length} chars`);
   156	    return true;
   157	  }
   158	  const body = fs.readFileSync(skillPath, "utf8").replace(/^---\r?\n[\s\S]*?\r?\n---\r?\n/, "");
   159	  if (hit.text.includes(body)) {
   160	    console.log(`${hit.where} holds all ${body.length} characters of the SKILL.md body`);
   161	    return true;
   162	  }
   163	  let n = 0;
   164	  while (n < body.length && hit.text.includes(body.slice(0, n + 1))) n = Math.min(body.length, n + 256);
   165	  console.log(`${hit.where} (${hit.text.length} chars) lacks part of the ${body.length}-character SKILL.md body; the first ${Math.max(0, n - 256)} characters match`);
   166	  return false;
   167	}
   168	
   169	function compacted(file, skillName, finalLine) {
   170	  const records = jsonLines(file);
   171	  let boundary = -1;
   172	  records.forEach((r, i) => {
   173	    if (r.type === "system" && r.subtype === "compact_boundary") boundary = i;
   174	  });
   175	  if (boundary < 0) {
   176	    console.log("no compact boundary in the transcript");
   177	    return false;
   178	  }
   179	  const meta = records[boundary].compactMetadata ?? {};
   180	  const after = records.slice(boundary + 1);
   181	  const skills = after
   182	    .filter((r) => r.type === "attachment" && r.attachment?.type === "invoked_skills")
   183	    .flatMap((r) => r.attachment.skills ?? [])
   184	    .filter((s) => s.name === skillName);
   185	  const tokens = `${meta.preTokens ?? "?"} to ${meta.postTokens ?? "?"} tokens`;
   186	  if (!skills.length) {
   187	    console.log(`${meta.trigger ?? "?"} compaction, ${tokens}; no ${skillName} in an invoked_skills attachment after it`);
   188	    return false;
   189	  }
   190	  const text = texts(skills[skills.length - 1].content).join("\n");
   191	  const cut = text.includes("truncated for compaction");
   192	  const has = text.includes(finalLine);
   193	  const kept = BEGIN_MARKERS.filter((m) => text.includes(m)).map((m) => m.replace("<!-- BEGIN upstream ", ""));
   194	  console.log(
   195	    `${meta.trigger ?? "?"} compaction, ${tokens}; ${skillName} re-attached with ${text.length} chars${cut ? ", cut for compaction" : ""}; begins kept: ${kept.join(", ") || "none"}; final check line ${has ? "present" : "missing"}`,
   196	  );
   197	  return has;
   198	}
   199	
   200	function noSkill(file) {
   201	  const bad = toolUses(jsonLines(file)).filter(
   202	    (u) => u.name === "Skill" || (u.name === "Read" && /(SKILL\.md|\/references\/)/.test(String(u.input?.file_path ?? ""))),
   203	  );
   204	  for (const u of bad) console.log(`${u.name} ${JSON.stringify(u.input)}`);
   205	  if (!bad.length) console.log("no Skill call and no skill file read");
   206	  return bad.length === 0;
   207	}
   208	
   209	function session(file) {
   210	  const init = jsonLines(file).find((r) => r.type === "system" && r.subtype === "init");
   211	  if (!init?.session_id) return false;
   212	  console.log(init.session_id);
   213	  return true;
   214	}
   215	
   216	function plugins(kind, file) {
   217	  const data = JSON.parse(fs.readFileSync(file, "utf8"));
   218	  const list = kind === "claude" ? data : data.installed ?? [];
   219	  for (const p of list) {
   220	    if (kind === "claude") console.log(`${p.id} ${p.version} ${p.installPath ?? ""}`.trim());
   221	    else console.log(`${p.pluginId} ${p.version}`);
   222	  }
   223	  return true;
   224	}
   225	
   226	function hooksTrusted(file, pluginId, version, keys) {
   227	  const hooks = jsonLines(file).filter((h) => h.pluginId === pluginId);
   228	  let ok = true;
   229	  for (const h of hooks) {
   230	    const inVersion = String(h.sourcePath ?? "").includes(`/${version}/hooks/`);
   231	    console.log(`${h.key} ${h.trustStatus}${inVersion ? "" : ` from ${h.sourcePath}`}`);
   232	    if (h.trustStatus !== "trusted" || !inVersion) ok = false;
   233	  }
   234	  const got = hooks.map((h) => h.key).sort().join(" ");
   235	  if (got !== [...keys].sort().join(" ")) {
   236	    console.log(`expected keys ${keys.join(" ")}`);
   237	    ok = false;
   238	  }
   239	  return ok;
   240	}
   241	
   242	const [cmd, ...args] = process.argv.slice(2);
   243	const commands = {
   244	  bundle: () => bundle(args[0], args[1], args[2], args[3], args[4]),
   245	  "skill-arrived": () => skillArrived(args[0], args[1], args[2], args[3], args[4]),
   246	  compacted: () => compacted(args[0], args[1], args[2]),
   247	  "no-skill": () => noSkill(args[0]),
   248	  session: () => session(args[0]),
   249	  plugins: () => plugins(args[0], args[1]),
   250	  "hooks-trusted": () => hooksTrusted(args[0], args[1], args[2], args.slice(3)),
   251	};
   252	if (!commands[cmd]) {
   253	  console.error(`usage: inspect.mjs ${Object.keys(commands).join("|")} ...`);
   254	  process.exit(2);
   255	}
   256	let ok = false;
   257	try {
   258	  ok = commands[cmd]();
   259	} catch (err) {
   260	  console.log(`inspect.mjs ${cmd}: ${err.message}`);
   261	}

+Date: 2026-09-26. Claude Code 2.1.283, Codex 0.154.0 and 0.157.1, revision

+context that follows the compaction. Research 09 found the same with fixture

+### Method
+
+- Claude Code, flag file on. `tests/e2e/claude-turns.mjs` keeps one `claude
+  -p --input-format stream-json` process open and sends `Reply with the
+  single word OK.`, then `/compact`. `inspect.mjs bundle ... after-compact`
+  counts the SessionStart attachments after the last `compact_boundary`

+  auto-compaction depends on how much the model reads or prints, so the
+  test uses `codex app-server` instead. `tests/e2e/codex-thread.mjs` starts
+  a thread and sends a turn, then `thread/compact/start`, which is what the
+  TUI's `/compact` sends, then one more turn. Codex fires the queued
+  `compact` source at the start of that turn (research 09). App-server has
+  no bypass flag, so the script first records trust for the hooks with
+  `codex-hooks.mjs trust`. The count covers the `replacement_history` of the

+  early, and aborted the last turn.

+// Drives one Codex thread through `codex app-server` for tests/e2e/run.sh,
+// in the home that HOME and CODEX_HOME name. `compact` sends
+// thread/compact/start, which is what the TUI's /compact calls; codex exec
+// has no way to ask for it (design/research/09-tests-clear-compact.md).
+//
+//   node tests/e2e/codex-thread.mjs <codex-bin> <cwd> <log> <step>...
+//     A step is turn:<prompt> or compact. Each step waits until the thread
+//     is idle again, or for turn/completed or thread/compacted.
+//
+// App-server does not take --dangerously-bypass-hook-trust, so hooks run
+// only when trusted (see codex-hooks.mjs trust). Prints "thread <id>" and
+// "rollout <path>". Writes every JSON-RPC line to <log>. Exits 1 when a
+// request fails or a step takes longer than 5 minutes.
+
+import { spawn } from "node:child_process";
+import fs from "node:fs";
+
+const [codex, cwd, log, ...steps] = process.argv.slice(2);
+if (!codex || !cwd || !log || !steps.length || !steps.every((s) => s === "compact" || s.startsWith("turn:"))) {
+  console.error("usage: codex-thread.mjs <codex-bin> <cwd> <log> turn:<prompt>|compact ...");
+  process.exit(2);
+}
+
+const out = fs.createWriteStream(log);
+const env = { ...process.env, RUST_LOG: "warn" };
+delete env.OPENAI_API_KEY;
+delete env.CODEX_API_KEY;
+delete env.ANTHROPIC_API_KEY;
+const server = spawn(codex, ["app-server", "--listen", "stdio://"], { cwd, env, stdio: ["pipe", "pipe", "pipe"] });
+server.stderr.on("data", (d) => out.write(d));
+
+const waiting = new Map();
+const listeners = new Set();
+let lastError = "";
+let buffer = "";
+server.stdout.setEncoding("utf8");
+server.stdout.on("data", (chunk) => {
+  buffer += chunk;
+  let nl;
+  while ((nl = buffer.indexOf("\n")) >= 0) {
+    const line = buffer.slice(0, nl).trim();
+    buffer = buffer.slice(nl + 1);
+    if (!line.startsWith("{")) continue;
+    out.write(line + "\n");
+    let msg;
+    try {
+      msg = JSON.parse(line);
+    } catch {
+      continue;
+    }
+    if (msg.id !== undefined && waiting.has(msg.id)) {
+      waiting.get(msg.id)(msg);
+      waiting.delete(msg.id);
+    } else if (msg.method) {
+      if (msg.method === "error") lastError = msg.params?.error?.message ?? "";
+      for (const fn of [...listeners]) fn(msg);
+    }
+  }
+});
+
+let nextId = 0;
+function request(method, params) {
+  const id = ++nextId;
+  return new Promise((resolve, reject) => {
+    waiting.set(id, (msg) => (msg.error ? reject(new Error(`${method}: ${JSON.stringify(msg.error)}`)) : resolve(msg.result)));
+    server.stdin.write(JSON.stringify({ jsonrpc: "2.0", id, method, params }) + "\n");
+  });
+}
+
+// Resolves when the thread goes active and then idle, or on a done event.
+// A turn/completed counts only for turnId: Codex can send the compaction
+// turn's turn/completed late, after the next turn/start.
+function settled(threadId, doneMethods, turnId = () => null) {
+  return new Promise((resolve, reject) => {
+    let active = false;
+    const timer = setTimeout(() => {
+      listeners.delete(fn);
+      reject(new Error(`timed out waiting for ${doneMethods.join(" or ")}`));
+    }, 300000);
+    const fn = (msg) => {
+      const p = msg.params ?? {};
+      if (p.threadId && p.threadId !== threadId) return;
+      if (msg.method === "thread/status/changed") {
+        if (p.status?.type === "active") active = true;
+        if (p.status?.type === "systemError") {
+          clearTimeout(timer);
+          listeners.delete(fn);
+          reject(new Error(`thread status systemError${lastError ? `: ${lastError}` : ""}`));
+          return;
+        }
+        if (!(active && p.status?.type === "idle")) return;
+      } else if (!doneMethods.includes(msg.method)) {
+        return;
+      } else if (msg.method === "turn/completed" && p.turn?.id !== turnId()) {
+        return;
+      }
+      clearTimeout(timer);
+      listeners.delete(fn);
+      resolve(msg.method);
+    };
+    listeners.add(fn);
+  });
+}
+
+let code = 0;
+try {
+  await request("initialize", {
+    clientInfo: { name: "adhd-unslop-e2e", title: "adhd-unslop e2e", version: "0" },
+    capabilities: { experimentalApi: true, requestAttestation: false, optOutNotificationMethods: [] },
+  });
+  server.stdin.write(JSON.stringify({ jsonrpc: "2.0", method: "initialized" }) + "\n");
+  const started = await request("thread/start", { cwd, sandbox: "read-only", approvalPolicy: "never" });
+  const thread = started.thread;
+  console.log(`thread ${thread.id}`);
+  if (thread.path) console.log(`rollout ${thread.path}`);
+  for (const step of steps) {
+    if (step === "compact") {
+      const done = settled(thread.id, ["thread/compacted"]);
+      await request("thread/compact/start", { threadId: thread.id });
+      await done;
+    } else {
+      let id = null;
+      const done = settled(thread.id, ["turn/completed"], () => id);
+      const res = await request("turn/start", { threadId: thread.id, input: [{ type: "text", text: step.slice(5) }] });
+      id = res?.turn?.id ?? null;
+      await done;
+    }
+  }
+} catch (err) {
+  console.error(`codex-thread.mjs: ${err.message}`);
+  code = 1;
+} finally {
+  server.stdin.end();
+  server.kill("SIGTERM");
+  const killer = setTimeout(() => server.kill("SIGKILL"), 3000);
+  server.on("exit", () => {
+    clearTimeout(killer);
+    out.end(() => process.exit(code));
+  });
+}

 function jsonLines(file) {
   const out = [];
   for (const line of fs.readFileSync(file, "utf8").split("\n")) {
     if (!line.startsWith("{")) continue;
     try {
       out.push(JSON.parse(line));
     } catch {
       // Skip non-JSON lines such as CLI warnings.
     }
   }
   return out;
 }
 
 function texts(value) {
   if (typeof value === "string") return [value];
   if (Array.isArray(value)) return value.flatMap(texts);
   if (value && typeof value === "object") {
     if (typeof value.text === "string") return [value.text];
     if ("content" in value) return texts(value.content);
   }
   return [];
 }

 has_plugin() {
   local file=$1 id=$2 version=${3:-}
   if awk -v id="$id" -v v="$version" '$1 == id && (v == "" || $2 == v) { found = 1 } END { exit !found }' "$file"; then return 0; fi
   echo "expected $id${version:+ $version}; installed: $(awk '{ printf "%s %s; ", $1, $2 }' "$file")"
   return 1
 }

 # A local git marketplace whose main branch starts at 0.2.2 and moves to the
 # tree under test. Both runtimes reset main to 0.2.2 before they install.
 setup_migrate() {
   local src=$work/migrate/src srv=$work/migrate/srv next=$work/migrate/next port
   mkdir -p "$src" "$srv" "$next"
   git -C "$repo" archive "$migrate_from" | tar xf - -C "$src" || return 1
   git -c init.defaultBranch=main init -q "$src"
   commit_all "$src" "adhd-unslop 0.2.2 ($migrate_from)"
   old_commit=$(git -C "$src" rev-parse HEAD)
   if [ -n "${E2E_REPO:-}" ]; then
     git clone -q --depth 1 --branch "${E2E_REF:-main}" "https://github.com/$E2E_REPO.git" "$work/migrate/gh" || return 1
     copy_tree "$work/migrate/gh" "$next"
   else
     copy_tree "$repo" "$next"
   fi
   git -C "$src" rm -rqf .
   (cd "$next" && tar cf - .) | (cd "$src" && tar xf -)
   commit_all "$src" "tree under test"
   new_commit=$(git -C "$src" rev-parse HEAD)
   git clone -q --bare "$src" "$srv/adhd-unslop.git"
   bare=$srv/adhd-unslop.git
   old_version=$(git -C "$src" show "$old_commit:plugins/adhd-unslop/.claude-plugin/plugin.json" | json_field version)
   new_version=$(git -C "$src" show "$new_commit:plugins/adhd-unslop/.claude-plugin/plugin.json" | json_field version)
   new_mirror_version=$(git -C "$src" show "$new_commit:plugins/au-unslop/.claude-plugin/plugin.json" | json_field version)
   new_bundle=$(git -C "$src" show "$new_commit:plugins/adhd-unslop/hooks/chunks/manifest.json" | bundle_from_manifest)
 
   node "$here/githttp.mjs" "$srv" >"$work/githttp.log" 2>&1 &
   server_pid=$!

exec

    Make adhd-unslop self-contained and generate every plugin file
    
    adhd-unslop 0.3.0 embeds both upstream texts in its skill, the same bytes
    its always-on hook delivers, and no longer depends on the mirror plugins.
    The mirrors ship the upstream SKILL.md byte for byte. Every file under
    plugins/ is generated from tools/plugins.json, src/, and upstream/; the
    check fails on stray files and --prune deletes them.
    
    The launcher skips resume in Claude Code, which keeps the earlier copy,
    and still injects on Codex resume, which can lose it. The chunk handlers
    stay exactly as 0.2.2 shipped them, so Codex hook trust carries over.
    ADHD_UNSLOP_ALWAYS overrides the flag files for one process.
    
    A user-only doctor skill reports install problems with their fixes. CI
    gains a keyless load check in pinned Claude Code and Codex, a version
    gate, workflow linting, a daily drift check against the latest CLIs that
    also proposes raised pins, and Dependabot for SHA-pinned actions. The
    e2e script checks arrival from transcripts and the upgrade from 0.2.2.

    Add daily upstream bump workflow
    
    sync.mjs --latest finds the newest upstream commit that touched a pinned
    file, bumps each changed upstream, raises the patch version of every plugin
    that ships its text, and writes a Markdown report. The workflow opens or
    updates one PR from that report, starts the verify workflow on the PR
    branch, and opens an issue when a bump fails its checks.

    steps as well as rules. It caught a real case: upstream unslop removed
    process step 3, which the final check cites.

    Fix findings from the second review pass
    
    - The citation gate reads CRLF upstream bodies correctly, so a CRLF
      upstream is no longer refused for a citation it still has.
    - The leftover-directive test matches only our own directives, so an
      upstream line that starts with {{ no longer fails a bump.
    - The prune test writes its own fresh copy, and every test temp folder is
      removed when its file finishes.
    - The doctor gives an absolute build path or a reinstall instruction when
      the runtime is unknown, and words a plain adhd-unslop entry in
      ~/.agents/skills as a possible clash.
    - DECISIONS no longer states an untested local-marketplace behavior.

+## Verdict
+
+REVISE
+
+Scope: `git diff fc308bd HEAD`. HEAD moved from 3df5374 to b7f2896 during the review. b7f2896 touches only `tests/e2e/` and `design/research/11-tests-e2e.md`, which another agent owns, so I did not re-review `tests/e2e/`. On HEAD, `node tools/build.mjs --check`, `node tools/sync.mjs --check`, and `node --test tests/*.test.mjs` all pass (131 pass, 1 skip). Every experiment ran in a scratch clone.
+
+## First-pass items
+
+- Blocking 1, the prune test on the live tree: resolved. In a scratch clone I added `plugins/adhd-unslop/skills/doctor/scripts/my-wip-helper.mjs`. `node --test tests/build.test.mjs` failed two tests and left the file in place.
+- Blocking 2, a link into a plugin cache: resolved. In a scratch home with a Codex cache copy, I linked to `skills/adhd-unslop`, `skills/doctor/scripts`, the plugin root, and `au-unslop/.../skills/unslop`. Each link gave a WARN naming `adhd-unslop:adhd-unslop`, `adhd-unslop:doctor`, or `au-unslop:unslop`.
+- Blocking 3, CRLF: resolved for git storage, `userOnly`, and templates. I wrote a CRLF `upstream/unslop/SKILL.md` and its pin by hand, then built, committed, and re-cloned. `build.mjs --check` passed, `cmp` found the mirror identical, and `git ls-files --eol` showed `i/crlf attr/-text`. The real `sync.mjs` path never gets that far. See Blocking 1.
+- Optional, the CRLF template directive: resolved, with unit cases for a CRLF directive and for an unknown `{{` line. The new test regex is a regression. See Blocking 2.
+- Optional, `features = { hooks = false }`: resolved. Five inline and quoted forms each gave a WARN.
+- Optional, the reinstall fix with trailing prose: resolved. The command is on `fix:` and "start a new session" is on `then:`. One problem remains for an unknown runtime, listed under Optional.
+- Optional, the doctor home source: resolved. The doctor and the launcher both use `os.homedir()`.
+- Optional, the DECISIONS local directory row: reworded to match `load-check.mjs`. The new clause is not verified. See Optional.
+- Optional, the run.sh "5,000-token" wording: skipped as instructed. b7f2896 changed it to 20,000 characters.
+- Optional, the `sync.mjs` comment: resolved.
+- Optional, the `20-lifecycle.md` resume wording: resolved. `adhd-unslop` is at 0.3.0, against 0.2.2 on main, and `version-gate.mjs --base fc308bd` passes in a scratch clone.
+- Optional, the cli-drift version check: resolved. It rejects an empty Claude Code version, an empty Codex version, both empty, and a prerelease. It accepts two numeric versions. The unused `outcome` output is gone.
+- `tests/e2e/codex-thread.mjs`: now committed in b7f2896. Another agent owns it, so I did not re-review it.
+
+## Blocking
+
+1. `tools/sync.mjs:61-68` (`listNumbers`), which `CITATION_KINDS` uses at lines 74, 75, and 77. It searches for `\n${heading}\n`, so on a CRLF body the exception, check, and process lists come back empty. A CRLF upstream never reaches the storage fix from item 3. `bump()` refuses it at the citation gate and names the wrong cause.
+   - Proof, the parser: with the pinned bodies, `unslop process` returns `[1,2]` for LF and `[]` for CRLF. `ADHD exception` returns 6 items for LF and 0 for CRLF. `ADHD check` returns 5 and 0.
+   - Proof, the bump: I called `bump("unslop", <sha>, { fetched })` with the pinned SKILL.md converted to CRLF. It printed "refusing to bump unslop: the overlay cites unslop process 1, which no longer exists upstream". The issue report then says the usual cause is an upstream change to a cited rule, which is wrong here.
+   - With a CRLF upstream committed by hand, three unit tests in the overlay and citation-gate suites fail for the same reason.
+   - The first pass rated this kind of break to the unattended bump as blocking in item 3. Here it happens one step earlier.
+   - Fix: normalize line endings in the shared readers, so the bump and the tests both get the fix. For example, run `body = body.replace(/\r\n/g, "\n")` at the top of `listNumbers` and of each `numbers` function, or once in `citationReport` and `ruleNumbers`. Add a CRLF case to the `citationReport` tests in `tests/sync.test.mjs`.
+
+2. `tests/build.test.mjs:87-92`, a regression from 3df5374. The test now matches `/^\{\{/m` in every generated `.md` file, including the verbatim upstream text in the mirrors and in chunks 2 and 3. So a legitimate upstream line that starts with `{{` fails it. `bump()` runs the whole suite (`sync.mjs:167-170`) and rolls back on failure. D2 forbids editing upstream text, so only a test change can unblock the bump.
+   - Proof: in a scratch clone I called `bump("unslop", <sha>, { fetched })` with the pinned SKILL.md plus a fenced block holding `{{first_name}}, thanks for your order.`. The build and `--check` passed. Then `no template syntax survives the build` failed, and the result was "bump of unslop failed and was rolled back". The old regex, `^\{\{include `, would not have matched that line.
+   - Fix: `renderTemplate` already throws on an unknown `{{` template line at build time, so the test only needs to catch leftover directives. Either check only the outputs of `.tmpl` files, with the text between each BEGIN and END upstream marker removed, or match `^\{\{(include|upstream) ` instead of `^\{\{`.
+
+## Optional
+
+- `tests/build.test.mjs:43-57`. The prune test copies the live generated folders, so a person's stray file also fails it: `actual` listed `my-wip-helper.mjs` too. The test has no `try/finally`, so it leaks its temp dir when it fails. Write the copy from `expectedFiles()` instead of using `cpSync`, and remove the dir in `finally` or `t.after`.
+- `tests/helpers.mjs:12-25` and `tests/doctor.test.mjs:16-23`. `tempPlugin`, `tempConfigDirs`, and `tempDirs` never clean up. One `node --test tests/*.test.mjs` run left 48 dirs (13 `cfg`, 32 `doctor`, 3 `plugin`), and this machine's TMPDIR holds over 900. This is harmless on CI. Register an `after` cleanup.
+- `src/adhd-unslop/skills/doctor/scripts/doctor.mjs:134-138`. For an unknown runtime, the `fix:` line is the relative command `node tools/build.mjs`, and the condition "run that in a checkout of this repo" comes after it, on `then:`. The doctor skill runs a `fix:` command once the user says yes, from whatever the working directory is. When `<root>/../../tools/build.mjs` exists, print its absolute path. Otherwise make the reinstall instruction the fix.
+- `doctor.mjs:307-308`. An entry named `adhd-unslop` that is not a link into our plugins gets a WARN saying it "creates a duplicate adhd-unslop:adhd-unslop skill name". That includes a dangling link, which creates no skill (see the dangling-link test in `tests/doctor.test.mjs`). D20 covers only links into a plugin. Word it as a possible clash with the `adhd-unslop` skill.
+- `design/DECISIONS.md:543`. The new clause "so edits there show at the next session" is in the verified platform facts table, but no run in `design/research/` edited a source after a local install. Claim 1 in `research/05` is still open, and `research/08` installed from git only. Drop the clause or mark it untested. D29 at line 525 could also say that generated files are now stored byte for byte.

+// Drives one Codex thread through `codex app-server` for tests/e2e/run.sh,
+// in the home that HOME and CODEX_HOME name. `compact` sends
+// thread/compact/start, which is what the TUI's /compact calls; codex exec
+// has no way to ask for it (design/research/09-tests-clear-compact.md).
+//
+//   node tests/e2e/codex-thread.mjs <codex-bin> <cwd> <log> <step>...
+//     A step is turn:<prompt> or compact. Each step waits until the thread
+//     is idle again, or for turn/completed or thread/compacted.
+//
+// App-server does not take --dangerously-bypass-hook-trust, so hooks run
+// only when trusted (see codex-hooks.mjs trust). Prints "thread <id>" and
+// "rollout <path>". Writes every JSON-RPC line to <log>. Exits 1 when a
+// request fails or a step takes longer than 5 minutes.
+
+import { spawn } from "node:child_process";
+import fs from "node:fs";
+
+const [codex, cwd, log, ...steps] = process.argv.slice(2);
+if (!codex || !cwd || !log || !steps.length || !steps.every((s) => s === "compact" || s.startsWith("turn:"))) {
+  console.error("usage: codex-thread.mjs <codex-bin> <cwd> <log> turn:<prompt>|compact ...");
+  process.exit(2);
+}
+
+const out = fs.createWriteStream(log);
+const env = { ...process.env, RUST_LOG: "warn" };
+delete env.OPENAI_API_KEY;
+delete env.CODEX_API_KEY;
+delete env.ANTHROPIC_API_KEY;
+const server = spawn(codex, ["app-server", "--listen", "stdio://"], { cwd, env, stdio: ["pipe", "pipe", "pipe"] });
+server.stderr.on("data", (d) => out.write(d));
+
+const waiting = new Map();
+const listeners = new Set();
+let lastError = "";
+let buffer = "";
+server.stdout.setEncoding("utf8");
+server.stdout.on("data", (chunk) => {
+  buffer += chunk;
+  let nl;
+  while ((nl = buffer.indexOf("\n")) >= 0) {
+    const line = buffer.slice(0, nl).trim();
+    buffer = buffer.slice(nl + 1);
+    if (!line.startsWith("{")) continue;
+    out.write(line + "\n");
+    let msg;
+    try {
+      msg = JSON.parse(line);
+    } catch {
+      continue;
+    }
+    if (msg.id !== undefined && waiting.has(msg.id)) {
+      waiting.get(msg.id)(msg);
+      waiting.delete(msg.id);
+    } else if (msg.method) {
+      if (msg.method === "error") lastError = msg.params?.error?.message ?? "";
+      for (const fn of [...listeners]) fn(msg);
+    }
+  }
+});
+
+let nextId = 0;
+function request(method, params) {
+  const id = ++nextId;
+  return new Promise((resolve, reject) => {
+    waiting.set(id, (msg) => (msg.error ? reject(new Error(`${method}: ${JSON.stringify(msg.error)}`)) : resolve(msg.result)));
+    server.stdin.write(JSON.stringify({ jsonrpc: "2.0", id, method, params }) + "\n");
+  });
+}
+
+// Resolves when the thread goes active and then idle, or on a done event.
+// A turn/completed counts only for turnId: Codex can send the compaction
+// turn's turn/completed late, after the next turn/start.
+function settled(threadId, doneMethods, turnId = () => null) {
+  return new Promise((resolve, reject) => {
+    let active = false;
+    const timer = setTimeout(() => {
+      listeners.delete(fn);
+      reject(new Error(`timed out waiting for ${doneMethods.join(" or ")}`));
+    }, 300000);
+    const fn = (msg) => {
+      const p = msg.params ?? {};
+      if (p.threadId && p.threadId !== threadId) return;
+      if (msg.method === "thread/status/changed") {
+        if (p.status?.type === "active") active = true;
+        if (p.status?.type === "systemError") {
+          clearTimeout(timer);
+          listeners.delete(fn);
+          reject(new Error(`thread status systemError${lastError ? `: ${lastError}` : ""}`));
+          return;
+        }
+        if (!(active && p.status?.type === "idle")) return;
+      } else if (!doneMethods.includes(msg.method)) {
+        return;
+      } else if (msg.method === "turn/completed" && p.turn?.id !== turnId()) {
+        return;
+      }
+      clearTimeout(timer);
+      listeners.delete(fn);
+      resolve(msg.method);
+    };
+    listeners.add(fn);
+  });
+}
+
+let code = 0;
+try {
+  await request("initialize", {
+    clientInfo: { name: "adhd-unslop-e2e", title: "adhd-unslop e2e", version: "0" },
+    capabilities: { experimentalApi: true, requestAttestation: false, optOutNotificationMethods: [] },
+  });
+  server.stdin.write(JSON.stringify({ jsonrpc: "2.0", method: "initialized" }) + "\n");
+  const started = await request("thread/start", { cwd, sandbox: "read-only", approvalPolicy: "never" });
+  const thread = started.thread;
+  console.log(`thread ${thread.id}`);
+  if (thread.path) console.log(`rollout ${thread.path}`);
+  for (const step of steps) {
+    if (step === "compact") {
+      const done = settled(thread.id, ["thread/compacted"]);
+      await request("thread/compact/start", { threadId: thread.id });
+      await done;
+    } else {
+      let id = null;
+      const done = settled(thread.id, ["turn/completed"], () => id);
+      const res = await request("turn/start", { threadId: thread.id, input: [{ type: "text", text: step.slice(5) }] });
+      id = res?.turn?.id ?? null;
+      await done;
+    }
+  }
+} catch (err) {
+  console.error(`codex-thread.mjs: ${err.message}`);
+  code = 1;
+} finally {
+  server.stdin.end();
+  server.kill("SIGTERM");
+  const killer = setTimeout(() => server.kill("SIGKILL"), 3000);
+  server.on("exit", () => {
+    clearTimeout(killer);
+    out.end(() => process.exit(code));
+  });
+}
